$$
\sum_j\theta_jv_j-u\le\max_j\theta_j\big[v_j-(V_j-B)^{1/q}\big].
$$

Suppose $a,b,c<M/2$ and a finite family of caps with margins $u_i\cdot(x-y)+\beta_i z$, $u_i\ne0$, is critical at $(0,y)$ with common raw mass $Q<\gamma_d M/2$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0,\ \lambda_i>0$. Write $U_i,q_i,V_i$ for the three cap volumes, $g_A,g,g_B$ for the ordinary centroids, $m=(g_A+g_B)/2$, and $\Delta=\sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i$. No cap contains two lifted centroids. Every cap containing an endpoint centroid has $q_i<\gamma_dc$ and misses the lifted middle centroid. Let $I_0$ be the nonempty set containing the lifted middle centroid. For $i\in I_0$, $q_i\ge\gamma_dc$ and $U_i+V_i<\gamma_d\min(a,b)$.

For a body $D$ and $u\ne0$ write $S_D(u)=\sup_s\mathcal H^{d-1}(D\cap\{u\cdot x=s\})/\|u\|$. A cap of mass $w<\gamma_d|D|$ misses $g_D$ by a signed functional deficit at least $(\gamma_d|D|-w)/S_D(u)$. Put $D_i^-=(\gamma_da-U_i)/S_A(u_i)$, $D_i^+=(\gamma_db-V_i)/S_B(u_i)$ on $I_0$. Then $-u_i\cdot(m-g)\ge(D_i^-+D_i^+)/2$ there. Write $\ell_i^-=u_i\cdot(g_A-y)-\beta_i$, $\ell_i^0=u_i\cdot(g-y)$, $\ell_i^+=u_i\cdot(g_B-y)+\beta_i$. Their respective $\lambda_i$-weighted sums are $-\Delta,0,\Delta$. Set $P_\pm=\sum_i\lambda_i(\ell_i^\pm)_+$. Then
$
\begin{aligned}
P_-&\ge \Big(\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_iD_i^--\Delta\Big)_+,
& P_+&\ge \Big(\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_iD_i^++\Delta\Big)_+,\\
P_-+P_+&\ge\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_i(D_i^-+D_i^+),
& \sum_i\lambda_i\big(u_i\cdot(m-g)\big)_+
&\ge\tfrac12\sum_{i\in I_0}\lambda_i(D_i^-+D_i^+).
\end{aligned}
$

04408e720ec652dd:08.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let a compact convex set in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ have positive-volume fibers $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ at integer bases $z_1,\ldots,z_k$, with $k\ge2$ and $m=k^{-1}\sum_j z_j\in\mathbb Z^n$. Consider couplings whose marginals $\sigma_j\le \mathbf1_{A_j}\,dx$ all have mass $t$, and whose arithmetic-mean pushforward satisfies $\eta\le\mathbf1_K\,dx$. Let $Y$ be the set of centroids of $\mathbf1_K\,dx+k\eta$ over all such couplings, including the zero coupling. For $t>0$ put $Z_t(A)=\{t^{-1}\int x\,d\sigma:0\le\sigma\le\mathbf1_A\,dx,\ \sigma(A)=t\}$.

Then $Y$ is compact, convex, and contained in $K$. Its part obtainable at fixed mass $t>0$ is exactly
$$
 Y_t=\frac{b g_K+tZ_t(A_1)+\cdots+tZ_t(A_k)}{b+kt},
 \qquad 0<t\le\min_j|A_j|,
$$

$$

 \min_{\sum_j v_j=0}\sum_{j=1}^k \int_{A_j}(u\cdot x-h+v_j)_+\,dx.
$$
The inner minimum is attained at finite multipliers. At any minimizer the $k$ selected strict positive-part caps have equal mass, and their volume restrictions maximize the corresponding primal equal-mass objective. The outer function is continuous and $D_u(h_2)\le D_u(h_1)-b(h_2-h_1)$ for $h_2>h_1$. For $u=0$ the support is zero. In particular for $k=2$ the multiplier vector is $(v,-v)$ and the same formulas give the exact two-source center set and its one-scalar inner minimum.

For every closed ambient halfspace $H$, write $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$. Every feasible coupling gives $\eta(H_m)\le\sum_j \sigma_j(H_{z_j})$. When the source bases are pairwise distinct and different from $m$, $|K\cap H_m|+\eta(H_m)$ is therefore a lower bound for the original mixed cap mass.

For a finite slope $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. A law's record is the average of $(P,C,M)$, and a law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero.

Given any probability law on finite slopes $s\ge0$, let $\phi$ be the mixture of the uniform probabilities on $[-s,s]$, with the layer at $s=0$ interpreted as $\delta_0$. Put $v=\phi((-\infty,1])$, $w=\phi([-T,\infty))$, $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$, $p_0=(H/B)^d$, and $a_0=1/B$. For $0<q<1$ put $e(q)=\int_{[-T,1]}(1-qb)^{-d}\,d\phi(b)$. The averaged frustum records satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{P}{V_0}&=p_0e(a_0)+1-v-tw,\\
\frac{C}{C_0}&=e(a_0),\\
\frac{M}{C_0}&=-\frac HB\int_{[-T,1]} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The energy $e$ is differentiable and convex on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$.

Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. $$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_c&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^c+C_\mu(V_0-P_\nu^c)}{V_0(C_\mu+C_\nu)},&
\omega&=\frac{C_\nu}{C_\mu+C_\nu},\\
\beta_f&=\frac{C_\nu P_\mu^f+C_\mu(V-P_\nu^f)}{V(C_\mu+C_\nu)}

\end{aligned}
$$

For arbitrary separately centered frustum laws, use their record-preserving representatives on $[0,T]\cup\{\infty\}$ and write $\lambda_\mu,\lambda_\nu$ for their finite masses. If both are positive, let $\beta_f$ in the next formula be the bounded frustum ratio of their conditional finite laws, and $C_\mu,C_\nu$ their conditional finite coareas. The ratio for the original pair is

$$
\frac12+\frac{\lambda_\mu\lambda_\nu(C_\mu+C_\nu)}
{\lambda_\mu C_\mu+\lambda_\nu C_\nu}\left(\beta_f-\frac12\right).
$$

If exactly one law has zero coarea, the ratio is $1/2$. If both have zero coarea, the literal quotient has zero denominator, and its continuous extension has value $1/2$. 0da12d076aef855c:01.statement:
Let $r\ge2$ and let $f$ be a nonnegative Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^r$ of mass in $(0,\infty)$ with full-dimensional positive support. Assume the extended function $g=f^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex, taking value $+\infty$ where $f=0$. Translate an arbitrary interior anchor to $0$ and write $U=\operatorname{int}\{f>0\}$. The radial body $B$ has radii
$$
\rho_B(u)^r=r\int_0^\infty t^{r-1}f(tu)\,dt,\qquad u\in\mathbb S^{r-1}.
$$
Then $B$ is a compact convex body containing $0$ in its interior, with volume equal to the mass of $f$, and it preserves every through-anchor closed halfspace mass. If $B$ is a simplex, let $p_B$ denote its Minkowski gauge. In that case there are a linear functional $\ell$, $R\in(0,\infty]$ and a positive continuous $F$ on $[0,R)$ such that $h=F^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex and nondecreasing and
$$
r\int_0^R t^{r-1}F(t)\,dt=1.
$$
If $R<\infty$, then $R\max_B\ell\le1$. If $R=\infty$, then $\ell=0$. The map $\Phi(b)=b/(1-\ell(b))$ is a bijection from $\{p_B<R\}$ onto $U$, with inverse $\Psi(x)=x/(1+\ell(x))$ and positive denominators on their domains. On $U$,
$$
f(x)=(1+\ell(x))^{-r-1}F\!\left(\frac{p_B(x)}{1+\ell(x)}\right).
$$
Equivalently, $f(x)\,dx$ is the pushforward of $F(p_B(b))\,db$ restricted to $\{p_B<R\}$. Boundary values are immaterial. The functional $\ell$ is uniquely determined: for $L(x)=g'(0;x)/g(0)$, where the derivative is one-sided, $L=\ell+c p_B$ with $c\ge0$. If $v_i$ are the vertices and $0=\sum_i\alpha_i v_i$ is the strictly positive barycentric row of $0$, then $c=\sum_i\alpha_i L(v_i)$.

Conversely, every compact convex body $B$ containing $0$ in its interior and every triple $(\ell,R,F)$ meeting the displayed conditions gives by this construction an integrable density of mass $|B|$ with convex extended inverse $(r+1)$st root and radial body $B$. The finite endpoint equality $R\max_B\ell=1$ is allowed.

0e1bf4bac5d35265:05.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For another compatible family of compact convex bodies $K'_z$ over the same $P$, write $S'$, $C'$, and $dm'$ for the corresponding sampled set, hull, and measure. Retain the same marks and define $H_{C'}(b)$ by the same supremum with domain $C'$ and integral over $S'$ against $dm'/M$, with the fixed old denominator $M$.

There is a fixed function $\widetilde L$, a minimum of at most $k$ affine functions on the relative ambient space, positive on a neighborhood of $C$ and equal to $L$ on $S$. For all families sufficiently close to the old family in maximum fiber Hausdorff distance and all $b$ sufficiently close to $l$, the marks stay interior to their own fibers and $H_{C'}(b)$ is finite and attained. It has a representative that is the minimum of at most $k$ affine functions, whose coefficients are uniformly bounded and whose minimum has a uniform positive floor on $C'$, on $C$, and on a fixed neighborhood of $C$. The maximizing sampled restriction is unique. As $(K'_z,b)\to(K_z,l)$, the optimal value tends to zero, the maximizing restriction converges uniformly on $S'$ to $\widetilde L|_{S'}$, and the bounded finite-plane representatives in the proof converge uniformly to $L$ on $S$.

Let $t\downarrow0$ and let $K_z(t)$ be such compatible bodies with $\max_z d_H(K_z(t),K_z)=O(t)$, using subscript $t$ for the moving objects. For arbitrary $b(t)\to l$ in the positive orthant,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=H_C(b(t))+
\frac{1}{M}\left(\int_{S_t}\log\widetilde L\,dm_t-\int_S\log L\,dm\right)+o(t).
\tag{6}
$$
Suppose in addition that for each $z$ and some fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, the endpoint on the ray through each $X\in\partial K_z$ changes to $o_z+(1-s_{z,t}(X))(X-o_z)$. Assume $|s_{z,t}|\le Ct$ uniformly and
$s_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/(n_z(X)\cdot(X-o_z))$ for surface-almost every $X$, where $n_z$ is the outward unit normal and $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. Use counting measure on the two endpoints for $d=1$. For $b_i(t)=l_i+th_i+o(t)$, with arbitrary $h\in\mathbb R^k$,
$$
H_t(b(t))
=t\left[-\frac1M\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)v_z(X)\,dS(X)
+\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}\right]+o(t).
\tag{7}
$$
The minimum is attained. Using the current total volume $M_t=m_t(S_t)$ as the denominator gives the same first-order coefficient.

0e1bf4bac5d35265:07.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, with $n\ge0$ and $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Let $d\ge1$ and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior for $z\in P$. Put $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and assume $C\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_z$ for each $z\in P$. All hulls and affine coefficients are relative to $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $dm=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$ and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive, continuous, and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Fix $k\ge1$ marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ with $p_i\in P$ and $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_i}$, and write $l_i=L(Y_i)$ and $l=(l_i)_{i=1}^k$.

Assume there is at least one contact certificate. This means weights $\sigma_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$ and, for each $\sigma_i>0$, a probability measure $\rho_i$ on $S$ with
$$
\int_S w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad
\int_S L\,d\rho_i=l_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\,\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
\tag{1}
$$
Let $\mathcal W$ be the set of all weight vectors of such certificates. For $b\in(0,\infty)^k$, let $H_C(b)$ be the supremum of $M^{-1}\int_S\log U\,dm$ over positive continuous concave functions $U$ on $C$ with $U(Y_i)\le b_i$ for all $i$.

For every such $U$ and every $\sigma\in\mathcal W$ one has
$$
\frac1M\int_S\log(U/L)\,dm
\le\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i\log\frac{U(Y_i)}{l_i}.
\tag{2}
$$
This also holds for continuous nonnegative concave $U$ on $C$ that are positive in the interior of every sampled fiber and have integrable sampled $\log U$. If $U(Y_i)\le l_i$ for all $i$ and the left-hand side is zero, then $U=L$ on every closed sampled fiber.

The function $H_C$ is finite, concave, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on the positive orthant, with $H_C(cb)=H_C(b)+\log c$ for $c>0$. One has $H_C(l)=0$, attained by $L$, and
$$
\partial^+H_C(l)=\left\{\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{l_i}\right)_{i=1}^k:\ \sigma\in\mathcal W\right\},
\tag{3}
$$
where $\partial^+$ consists of the supergradients for the concave function. In particular $\mathcal W$ is compact and convex, and for every $h\in\mathbb R^k$ and $t\downarrow0$,
$$
H_C(l+th+o(t))=t\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal W}\sum_i \frac{\sigma_i h_i}{l_i}+o(t).
\tag{4}
$$

A simplex has strict distinct-vertex incidence if the open positive halfplane of each cap contains one vertex and its open negative halfplane contains every other vertex, with a different positive vertex for each cap.

Assume the resulting fibers lie in parallel $N$-dimensional affine planes, with the same Euclidean $N$-volume convention. Let $\mu_{j,z}$ be $\alpha_j>0$ times the $N$-volume restricted to the fiber of this cut at $z$, where $\alpha_j$ is independent of $z$. Assume simultaneous finite weak limits $\mu_{j,z}\to\mu_z$ at every $z\in P$. Put $P_+=\{z\in P:\mu_z\ne0\}$ and assume it is nonempty.

Whenever $z_i\in P_+$ and $\theta_i>0$ have $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ and $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i$ is integer, $z\in P_+$ and for all compact sets $E_i$ with $\mu_{z_i}(E_i)>0$,
$$
\mu_z\!\left(\sum_i\theta_i E_i\right)^{1/N}
\ \ge\ \sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}.
$$
In particular $P_+=\operatorname{conv}(P_+)\cap\mathbb Z^n$.

185fb6155f830e0e:02.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and let $\mu_z$ be nonzero finite positive Borel measures of compact support $S_z\subset\mathbb R^D$ indexed by a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$. Suppose every positive-weight combination $z=\sum_i\theta_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^n$, with $z_i\in P$ and $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, has $z\in P$ and satisfies
$$
\mu_z\!\left(\sum_i\theta_i E_i\right)^{1/N}
\ \ge\ \sum_i\theta_i\mu_{z_i}(E_i)^{1/N}
$$
for all compact $E_i$ with $\mu_{z_i}(E_i)>0$. For any such incidence, any input index $i$, and any choices $x_l\in S_{z_l}$ for $l\ne i$, put $F_i(x)=\theta_i x+\sum_{l\ne i}\theta_l x_l$. Then the finite measures satisfy $\mu_z\ge\theta_i^N(F_i)_\#\mu_{z_i}$.

Each $S_z$ is convex, and each $\mu_z$ is absolutely continuous in its own affine hull, with counting measure at a point. For positive support dimension $q$, writing $|\cdot|_q$ for Lebesgue measure in the support affine hull, its density is at most $2^N\mu_z(S_z)/|S_z|_q$ almost everywhere. At an incidence every input and the output have the same support affine dimension and tangent space. Partition $P$ into strata $P_c$ by the pair of these invariants. Every $P_c$ is lattice-complete, different strata use disjoint original parity classes, and hence $\sum_c k(P_c)=k(P)\le2^n$, where $k$ counts occupied classes modulo $2\mathbb Z^n$. The convex hull of the placed supports in any stratum has exactly those supports as its integer fibers. The same exact fiber assertion holds for the hull of all the placed supports.

18f8d2b72265ccb5:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be an ambient compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and let $D\subseteq C$ be an ambient convex body maximizing positive mixed $d$-volume among those whose true centroid $(j,c)$ has integral $j$ and whose normalized closed-halfspace depth at that centroid is at least a prescribed $\beta$. The set $P$ equals $\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Every affine fit
$$

$$
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i x_i^\top=\alpha I_d,qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i z_i^\top=0,qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0 .
$$

An affine graph taking values in $\operatorname{int}(C_z)$ at every $z\in P$ suffices for the strict fit.

$$
P(a,b)\ge\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\frac{b_j}{\sum_i a_i}\right)^{-1}
\ge\Gamma_q,\qquad \Gamma_q=\left(\frac{q}{q+1}\right)^q.

1972e280d049f336:04.statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing$, $q=\dim_H S$ and $\mu=\mathcal H^q|_S$ (counting measure for $q=0$). Let $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ be finite nonnegative measures of equal mass supported on $S$, and let $\Xi_{\rm old}$ be a coupling whose midpoints belong to $S$ almost everywhere. Assume $\gamma_i\le a_i\mu$ for bounded nonnegative upper semicontinuous $a_i$ on the compact supports $E_i=\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Let $E_{i,r}$ and $\gamma_{i,r}$ denote the restrictions to original base parity $r$. For $q\ge1$ put $H_q(t,s)=((t^{-1/q}+s^{-1/q})/2)^{-q}$ on positive arguments and zero if either vanishes. Put $H_0(t,s)=\min(t,s)$. Define on the physical space
$$
c_r(w)=\max_{\substack{u\in E_{-,r},\,v\in E_{+,r}\\(u+v)/2=w}} H_q(a_-(u),a_+(v)),
$$
with the empty maximum zero. Then each $c_r$ is bounded and upper semicontinuous. There is one coupling of the original marginals whose classwise midpoint laws satisfy $\rho_{{\rm old},r}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_r\le c_r\mu$ in full physical coordinates, and whose classwise endpoint marginals are $\gamma_{-,r},\gamma_{+,r}$. Its total midpoint law satisfies $\rho\le(\sum_r c_r)\mu$. For fiberwise constant ceilings $c_r(p,x)$ is bounded by the maximum of $H_q$ over positive class-$r$ input base pairs summing to $2p$.

In particular, for unit ceilings let $D_r=(E_{-,r}+E_{+,r})/2$. Then $\rho_r\le\mathbf1_{D_r}\mu$ and $\rho\le\kappa\mu$ with $\kappa(w)=\#\{r:w\in D_r\}\le2^n$. At a boundary base $p$ of the projection of $C$, any supporting affine hyperplane $A$ gives $\kappa(p,x)\le 2^{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{dir}A)}$. If $q<d$ then $n\ge1$ and $\kappa\le2^{n-1}$ on $S$. The uniform constants $2^n$ for $q=d$ and $2^{n-1}$ for $q<d$ are sharp.

19899b61b9ca5f3a:04.statement:
Use raw summed volume of a finite family of compact convex fibers with positive $d$-dimensional volume, and let $Y$ be interior to its own fiber with raw depth $Q$. Let finitely many nonvertical critical closed caps through $Y$ have mass $Q$ and continuous normals $u_j$ positively balanced by weights $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j=1$. Linearly perturb their full normals to $N_j+sN'_j$ with continuous parts $u_j+s w_j$. Define $m_j(W)=N_j\cdot(W-Y)$, $\ell_j(W)=N'_j\cdot(W-Y)$ and $F_j(s,c)=\mu\{m_j+s\ell_j\ge c\}$. Assume $F_j$ is $C^2$ near $(0,0)$ and $S_j=-\partial_cF_j(0,0)>0$. Put $A_j=\partial_{ss}F_j(0,0)$. Then $\partial_sF_j(0,0)=0$, $A_j\ge0$, and the actual raw $Q$-quantile threshold is
$$
c_j(s)=\frac{A_j}{2S_j}s^2+o(s^2).
$$
For $s>0$ the coefficients $\rho_j/s$ combine the continuous normals exactly to $\sum_j\rho_jw_j$ and the thresholds to $(s/2)\sum_j\rho_j A_j/S_j+o(s)$. If the missing components of unit representatives have magnitude $O(s)$, recovering a nonzero component there requires total positive coefficient $\Omega(1/s)$. With a $C^1$ cap map the scalar inversion still gives $c_j(s)=o(s)$ and the same normal identity with threshold sum $o(1)$.

Under local coarea moment regularity, writing $d\sigma$ for the sum of fiber-section areas divided by $|u_j|$, the first normal derivative is $\int_{m_j=0}\ell_j\,d\sigma$, and $A_j=-\partial_c\int_{m_j=c}\ell_j^2\,d\sigma|_{c=0}$. In particular the identities hold for stable proper, strictly full or strictly empty cuts of finite polytopal fibers whose varying planes avoid the vertices. R(u)=\frac{|T\cap\lbrace u\cdot x\ge 2b-\ell\rbrace|}{V},\qquad

$$

1ec792c66c5ddc47:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let convex bodies $K_j\subset\mathbb R^d$ converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body $K$, and let $M_j\to M>0$, $\lambda_j>0$ with $\lambda_j\to0$. On $K_j$ let $L_j=\min_{1\le i\le k}A_{ij}>0$ have a fixed finite affine presentation, with coefficient limits $A_i$ and limiting minimum $L$. Suppose $\int_{K_j}(M_jL_j)^{-1}\,dX\le C_{\rm inv}$. Put $r_j=\lambda_j(-\log L_j)_+$. Partition volume into geometric active cells $C_{ij}=K_j\cap\bigcap_l\{A_{ij}\le A_{lj}\}$, counting identical planes once and discarding volume-null cells. Pass to a subsequence with fixed retained labels and, for every retained cell, put $b_{ij}=\max_{C_{ij}}A_{ij}$ and $R_i=\lim_j\lambda_j(-\log b_{ij})_+$. For the finite-cell assertion suppose the rates are uniformly bounded, so these limits are finite after selection.

For any common weak limit of the cell measures $(M_jA_{ij})^{-1}\mathbf1_{C_{ij}}\,dX\,\delta_{r_j(X)}$, there is no mass on $0<r<R_i$. Its restriction to $r>R_i$ is $\gamma_i(r)(dX)\,dr$ with a decreasing, right-continuous version in measure order. The conditionals are locally bounded in mass on $r>R_i$, are supported on $K\cap\{A_i=L=0\}$, and for almost every such $r$ and all compact $U,V$ of positive conditional mass satisfy
$$
\gamma_i(r)(\theta U+(1-\theta)V)^{1/(d-1)}
\ge\theta\gamma_i(r)(U)^{1/(d-1)}+(1-\theta)\gamma_i(r)(V)^{1/(d-1)}
\qquad(0<\theta<1).
$$
In particular they are log-concave and their nonzero supports are convex and nested. The slicing conclusion leaves open mass at $R_i$. A constant limiting plane contributes no positive-rate mass.

For a single affine $L_j$ whose limit has nonzero gradient and zero face $F=K\cap\{L=0\}\ne\varnothing$, the same conclusions hold on all $r>0$ without a uniform upper rate bound, for every joint weak limit locally on that range. The projected prelimit slice masses at $r\ge r_0>0$ are at most $2^d C_{\rm inv}/r_0$ for all sufficiently large $j$. The same local slice argument applies to a single geometric cell with convergent nonzero limiting gradient and anchors of uniformly positive height.

206ce63695a66fe5:01.statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, and let $f:K\to\mathbb R$ be bounded, lower semicontinuous and convex. The same bound holds for the closed mean superlevel of a bounded upper semicontinuous concave function. The constant is sharp, with equality for $f(x)=\sum_i x_i$ on the standard $d$-simplex.

206ce63695a66fe5:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb R_x^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge1$, with ordinary projection $K$ onto $x$ and line sections $[a(x),b(x)]$. Let $g$ be the centroid of $K$ and let $\bar a,\bar b$ be the uniform means of the endpoint functions on $K$. For every $t_0\in[\bar a,\bar b]$, the point $(t_0,g)$ belongs to $C$ and every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing it has $|\pi_x(C\cap H)|\ge\Gamma_d|K|$ for $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.

Any integer in $[\bar a,\bar b]$ gives an actual mixed-integer point with that property. In particular, $|C|_{d+1}/|K|\ge1$ suffices. The interval can miss all integers even when the original mixed set has positive mass. In the planar body $0\le x\le1$, $x/2-1/10\le t\le11/10-x/2$, the endpoint-mean interval is $[3/20,17/20]$, the fibers at $t=0,1$ both equal $[0,1/5]$, and the line at $g=1/2$ has no integer $t$.

Let $g$ be the ordinary centroid of $K$, and suppose an integer $j$ belongs to the interval between the uniform means of $a,b$ on $K$. Put $y=(j,g)$, let $M$ be the mixed volume of $C$, and write $D_C(y)$ for raw closed-halfspace mixed depth. For every integer $k\ge0$, $C_k=C+[-k,k]e_t$ has mass $M+2kA$ and
$$
D_{C_k}(y)\ge D_C(y)+k\Gamma_d A,\qquad \Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

The difference between this guaranteed lower bound and $(\Gamma_d/2)(M+2kA)$ equals $D_C(y)-(\Gamma_d/2)M$.

207a0b33a5d3a235:02.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a convex body, and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability supported on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Fix $0<\alpha<1$. Suppose the ambient depth region $D_\alpha=\{y:\mu(H)\ge\alpha\text{ for every closed halfspace }H\ni y\}$ is nonempty and disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$. There is a compact full-dimensional ambient polytope $Q\supseteq D_\alpha$ disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, described by inequalities $a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x\le c_i$ with $\mu\{a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x>c_i\}<\alpha$.

Each facet $\ell_j\cdot z\le\delta_j$ of the base projection of $Q$ has a nonempty index set $I_j$ with $|I_j|\le d+1$ and positive multipliers $\lambda_{ji}$ such that
$$
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}\beta_i=0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}a_i=\ell_j\ne0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}c_i=\delta_j.
$$
Every lifted point of $Q$ above that facet is tight in all inequalities indexed by $I_j$. At most $2^n$ of the facet halfspaces already have intersection disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n$. Their strict exteriors cover $S$, each exterior for facet $j$ having mass less than $|I_j|\alpha\le(d+1)\alpha$.

2086e4eaa4bce465:01.statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{conv}(U)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be nonempty and finite, and let $L(U)$ be the space of scalar functions preserving every anchored convex representation on $U$. There are integer-valued $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ whose span together with $1$ and the original coordinate functions is $L(U)$. Put $\Psi(u)=(u,f_1(u),\ldots,f_s(u))$, choose $u_0\in U$, and let $E_0=\operatorname{aff}(\Psi(U))-\Psi(u_0)$ and $\Lambda_0=E_0\cap\mathbb Z^{n+s}$. The integer graph is affinely equivalent to the canonical lift, $\Lambda_0$ is a full-rank lattice of $E_0$, and $\operatorname{conv}(\Psi(U))\cap(\Psi(u_0)+\Lambda_0)=\Psi(U)$. For every $u,v\in U$ and integer $m\ge1$,
$$
\Psi(u)-\Psi(v)\in m\Lambda_0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u-v\in m\mathbb Z^n.
$$
In particular, the number of occupied parity classes in the inherited affine lattice equals that of $U$, even if the lifted rank is larger. A nonempty closed minor of a complete base is complete, so this applies to successive closed minors as well.

Let $\mu$ be the sum of their $d$-volumes, $M$ its total, and fix finitely many closed caps $H_j=\{v_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$ with $|u_j|=1$ and budgets $\mu(H_j)\le B_j$. For each fiber use the normal fan of $K_z\ominus tB_d$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$. Take a common simplicial refinement, and restrict ray supports to the linear subspace where each fiber support is linear on its own chosen fan. Let $A_0$ be the active homogeneous support-convexity and compatibility rows there. For each original facet $F$ let $n_F$ be its unit outward normal and $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-area. The total volume derivative in any radial direction $\delta$ is $L_0(\delta)=\sum_{z,F}|F|\delta_z(n_F)$. For a noncoincident facet the cap derivative term is $|F\cap\operatorname{int}(H_j)_z|\delta_z(n_F)$. On a coincident facet the term is $|F|\min(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when the body lies in the cap and $|F|\max(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when it lies on the outside. There exist nonnegative $\lambda_j,\eta$, with some $\lambda_j>0$ and $\lambda_j=0$ on slack caps, such that on the entire restricted chart
$$
L_0=\sum_j\lambda_j L_j-\eta^\top A_0 .
$$
Here $L_j$ uses the exact noncoincident coefficients and a coefficient $\theta_{jzF}|F|$, $0\le\theta_{jzF}\le1$, at each coincidence.

Put $t_j(z)=b_j-v_j\cdot z$. Define $s_{jz}$ as proper section area on a proper cut, zero at strict full or empty cuts and lower-dimensional contacts, $(1-\theta_{jzF})|F|$ at an inside coincidence, and $\theta_{jzF}|F|$ at an outside coincidence. With the same choices,
$$
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j s_{jz}u_j=0,\qquad
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j s_{jz}u_j z^\top=0,\qquad
dM=d\sum_j\lambda_j\mu(H_j)+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j t_j(z)s_{jz}.
$$
If all active masses are $\beta M$, the last identity is $1=\beta\sum_j\lambda_j+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_jt_j(z)s_{jz}/(dM)$. Facet and section areas in $d=1$ use endpoint counting.

$$
\sum_{z,F}|F|\,\delta_z(n_F)=\sum_j\lambda_j L_j(\delta)-\eta^\top A_0\delta.
$$
Here $L_j(\delta)=\sum_{z,F}a_{jzF}\delta_z(n_F)$. The coefficient is the area strictly inside cap $j$ at noncoincident facets and $\theta_{jzF}|F|$, $0\le\theta_{jzF}\le1$, at coincident facets.

For cap $H_j=\{v_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$ with $u_j$ unit, let $t_j(z)=b_j-v_j\cdot z$. The same trace choices satisfy

\sum_j\lambda_j u_j\bigl(\sum_z s_{jz}z\bigr)^\top=0,\qquad
1=\beta\sum_j\lambda_j+\frac{\sum_{j,z}\lambda_jt_j(z)s_{jz}}{dM}.

2201a46234e42aae:02.statement:
Let $S$ be the sampled mixed set of a compact convex body, with $q\ge1$ its largest integer fiber dimension. List its positive $q$-volume fibers $K_i$ at distinct bases $p_i$, let $V_i=\mathcal H^q(K_i)$, and let $\mu$ sum their intrinsic $q$-volumes. For nonnegative weights $\rho_i$ and thresholds $\alpha_i$, put
$$
T=\sum_i\rho_i V_i,\qquad
E_i(\alpha_i)=\sum_a(A_{ai}-\alpha_i)_+ +\alpha_i/\gamma_q-V_i,\qquad
L_a=\max(\{\rho_i:A_{ai}>\alpha_i\}\cup\{0\}).
$$
Then each surplus is nonnegative and
$$
T+\sum_i\rho_i E_i(\alpha_i)
=\sum_a\sum_i\rho_i(A_{ai}-\alpha_i)_+
  +\gamma_q^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\alpha_i
\le\sum_a L_a\mu(H_a)+\gamma_q^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\alpha_i.
$$
In particular, the last cap term is at most $B\sum_a L_a$ if each original cap has mass at most $B$.

Write $A_{(s)i}$ for the decreasing ranks of the actual local masses, with a fixed ordering of ties and zero padding. Write $a_s(i)$ for the corresponding original labels when present. D_a^{123}&=\max_i\rho_i(\mathbf1_{\{a=a_1(i)\}}+\mathbf1_{\{a=a_2(i)\}}+\kappa\mathbf1_{\{a=a_3(i)\}}),
\end{aligned}
$$
where a padded rank contributes no indicator. Then $E_i^{\mathrm{top}}\ge0$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
T-R&=\sum_i\rho_i A_{(1)i},\\
R+\sum_i\rho_i E_i^{\mathrm{top}}
 &=\sum_i\rho_i(A_{(2)i}+\kappa A_{(3)i})\le\sum_a D_a^{23}\mu(H_a),\\
T+\sum_i\rho_i E_i^{\mathrm{top}}
 &\le\sum_a D_a^{123}\mu(H_a).
\end{aligned}
$$
If every cap has mass at most $B$, the last sum is at most $B\sum_a D_a^{123}$.

22fb802a1dc82eb3:03.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact polytope with positive $d$-dimensional actual fibers $K_p$ at finitely many sampled bases $p$, with $d\ge1$. Write $\mu$ for the sum of their $d$-volumes and $\eta$ for their boundary area marked with the regular outward continuous normal. Use counting area at interval endpoints. Let $\Pi$ be a given finite coupling from $\nu\ll\eta$ to $\eta$ preserving that normal and having conditional physical output mean equal to its input $w=(p,x)$.

List the nonvertical ambient facets $F_f$ with supporting equation $a_f\cdot p+u_f\cdot x=b_f$, where $|u_f|=1$ is oriented outward, working over the affine span of the base projection. At each regular input choose the first containing nonvertical facet with that marked normal. Let $\Pi_f$ be the restriction by this source label, with marginals $\nu_f,\eta_f$, and write $W_f=\eta_f-\nu_f$. These laws sum to their original marginals, the outputs stay on the labeled facet, and $\int(1,w)\,dW_f=0$. The labeled covariance is
$$
Q_f=\int ww^{\mathsf T}\,dW_f
=\int(w'-w)(w'-w)^{\mathsf T}\,d\Pi_f\succeq0,\qquad Q_f(a_f,u_f)=0.
$$
More generally, for a compact marked coupling whose conditional physical output mean given the full marked input equals its physical input, the quadratic difference identity holds after localization by every bounded Borel function of the preserved parameter.

Suppose further that $\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\eta$ for finitely many nonvertical caps $H_j=\{a_j\cdot p+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$, $|v_j|=1$, and $\lambda_j\ge0$. The body selector $\alpha_j$ is the usual captured bit off supporting faces. Its section allocation $\sigma_j$ is $1-\alpha_j$ at inside supporting facets and $\alpha_j$ at outside supporting facets, with full area on proper cuts. Denote the resulting effective section measure by $\zeta_j$. Splitting each $\alpha_j$ by the common source label gives $\alpha_{jf}$, with $\sum_f\alpha_{jf}=\alpha_j$ almost everywhere, while the target owner fractions $\omega_f=d\eta_f/d\eta$ satisfy $\sum_f\omega_f=1$. Thus $dW_f=(\omega_f-\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_{jf})d\eta$. The $\zeta_j$ remain the original section allocations.

For each group $i$ of positive-section caps let $S_j=\zeta_j(\mathrm{total})$. Assume $\lambda_j S_j=t_i\rho_j$ within each group, that all its section measures have the same full physical centroid $\bar w_i=(\bar p_i,\bar x_i)$, and that $\sum_{j\in i}\rho_j(b_j-a_j\cdot\bar p_i)=0$. Set $V_j=\int(w-\bar w_i)(w-\bar w_i)^{\mathsf T}\,d\zeta_j$ in those groups and $V_j=0$ for a zero section measure. Then $V_j\succeq0$ and $V_j(a_j,v_j)=0$. If $m_p,m_x$ are the full mixed first moments and $m_{pj},m_{xj}$ their analogues restricted to $H_j$, then
$$
\begin{aligned}
d\left(m_p-\sum_j\lambda_jm_{pj}\right)
  &=-\sum_f Q_f^{pp}a_f-\sum_j\lambda_j V_j^{pp}a_j,\\
(d+1)\left(m_x-\sum_j\lambda_jm_{xj}\right)
  &=\sum_f Q_f^{xx}u_f+\sum_j\lambda_j V_j^{xx}v_j .
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $pp$ and $xx$ denote the base and continuous diagonal blocks. In zero base dimension the $pp$ blocks are absent and each continuous term on the right vanishes individually.

$$
p_{\mathcal A}(y)=\inf_{H\ni(j,y)}\sum_i |\{x\in A_i:(p_i,x)\in H\}|,
\qquad y\in D_{\mathcal A},
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed ambient halfspaces and $|\cdot|$ denotes ordinary $d$-volume.

For another such array $\mathcal B=(B_i)$ and $t\in[0,1]$, set $\mathcal K=((1-t)A_i+tB_i)_{i=1}^N$. For every $y\in D_{\mathcal A}$ and $z\in D_{\mathcal B}$,
$$
p_{\mathcal K}((1-t)y+tz)^{1/d}
\ge (1-t)p_{\mathcal A}(y)^{1/d}+t p_{\mathcal B}(z)^{1/d}.
$$
The fixed-base maximum $M(\mathcal A)=\max_{y\in D_{\mathcal A}}p_{\mathcal A}(y)$ is positive and attained, and
$$
M(\mathcal K)^{1/d}\ge (1-t)M(\mathcal A)^{1/d}+tM(\mathcal B)^{1/d}.
$$
Both inequalities have homogeneous versions with any nonnegative coefficients $\alpha,\beta$ of positive sum in place of $1-t,t$, using componentwise Minkowski combinations and omitting terms with zero coefficient.

2623b39acd3d4a1d:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty mixed set $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, and write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Put $q=\dim_H S\ge1$, $V_z=\mathcal H_q(C_z)$, $P=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:V_z>0\}$, $M=\mathcal H_q(S)=\sum_{z\in P}V_z$, and let $k$ count the occupied coordinate parity classes of $P$. Fix finitely many original closed ambient halfspaces $H_i$ and an integer $t\ge1$. The mass of a cap is $\mathcal H_q(S\cap H_i)$.

Let $\ell:\operatorname{conv}(P)\to[0,\infty)$ be finite and convex. Suppose at every $z\in P$ some at most $t$ original caps leave $\mathcal H_q$-measure at most $\ell(z)^q$ uncovered in $C_z$. Then one subfamily of at most $kt$ original caps gives that same residual bound simultaneously at every $z\in P$. Its total residual is at most $\sum_{z\in P}\ell(z)^q$. If every original cap has mass at most $B$ for some $B\ge0$, then $ktB\ge M-\sum_{z\in P}\ell(z)^q$. In particular, for any $g$ with $0\le tg\le1$, a total allowance $\sum_{z\in P}\ell(z)^q\le(1-tg)M$ yields $B\ge gM/k$. For $q=d$, $t=2$ and $g=\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, this allowance is $M/9$ when $d=2$ and zero when $d=1$. For general $q$ one can take $g=\gamma_q$ or $g=\gamma_d$ whenever the corresponding $tg\le1$.

2623b39acd3d4a1d:03.reason: Compactness is in sampled value vectors. 2623b39acd3d4a1d:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty mixed set $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, and write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Among affine functions $L$ on $\operatorname{aff}(P)$ with $L(z)\ge V_z^{1/q}$ on $P$, define the normalized minimum
$$
A_q(P,V)=\frac{1}{M}\min_L\sum_{z\in P}L(z)^q.

It is attained, its sampled value vector is unique when $q>1$, and $1\le A_q(P,V)\le |P|\max_{z\in P}V_z/M$. One has $A_q(P,V)=1$ exactly when the volume roots are affine on $P$. If each $z\in P$ admits at most $t$ original caps with residual measure at most $\tau V_z$ for $\tau\ge0$, then at most $kt$ original caps leave total residual at most $\tau A_q(P,V)M$. 26455afca6af9c16:01.reason: Volume-root and energy-root concavity combine in the body-tied profile. Its normalization, boundary continuity and invariance use the actual sampled mass and covariance. The bound f≤1 is restricted to sampled bases.
26455afca6af9c16:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite, nonempty and equal to $\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. For $d\ge1$, let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies for $z\in P$ satisfying $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subset K_p$ for every convex representation $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Set $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $V(z)=|C_z|$, $V_z=|K_z|$ at sampled bases, $M=\sum_{z\in P}V_z$, and $N=d+1$. Let $E_K(y)$ be the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over strictly positive affine denominators on $K$ for $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, extended by zero on $\partial K$. Define
$$
H(z,y)=[E_{C_z}(y)V(z)^{1/d}]^{1/N},\qquad f(z,y)=H(z,y)/M^{1/d}.
$$
Then $H$ is continuous and jointly concave on $C$, strictly concave on each own-fiber interior, and zero on each own-fiber boundary. At sampled bases $0\le f(z,y)\le(V_z/M)^{1/d}\le1$. The sampled profiles are jointly continuous under simultaneous positive-fiber Hausdorff convergence and convergence of sampled marks. Write $g_z$ for the centroid of $K_z$, $\Sigma=M^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^\mathsf{T}\,dX$, and $\Gamma(u)=(u^\mathsf{T}\Sigma u)^{1/2}$. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$ define buffered depth as the infimum of the mixed volume of the caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
together with the closed pure-base caps through $p$. Normalized cap masses and normalized buffered depths are invariant under common invertible affine changes of the continuous coordinates, continuous base-affine shears, and unimodular affine changes of the base.

26455afca6af9c16:02.reason: On the assumed invariant positive compact original sublevel, the exact all-tilt comparison gives a fixed-scale minimum. Uniform boundary control and the closed pure-base gap yield proper source sections and finite cap attainment.
26455afca6af9c16:02.statement:
Fix a complete base $P$ in the body-tied profile setting. Let $\beta_\varepsilon$ be the maximum buffered depth divided by total sampled mass, and let $\beta_0$ denote its ordinary unbuffered version. Put $\beta_*=\inf_K\beta_0(K)$ over all positive compatible families on $P$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Assume $\beta_*<b<\gamma_d/k(P)$, where $k(P)$ counts parity classes in the inherited affine lattice, and assume every family with $\beta_0\le b$ has an invariant representative in a single compact class of positive compatible families, with $M=1$, $V_z\ge v_0>0$, $K_z\subset R B_d$, a common positive inradius, and $\lambda_- I\le\Sigma\le\lambda_+ I$ for positive $\lambda_-,\lambda_+$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the infimum of $\beta_\varepsilon$ over all positive compatible families on $P$ is attained. With $\omega_j=|B_j|$ and $\omega_0=1$, put $A_{\mathrm{sec}}=|P|\omega_{d-1}R^{d-1}$ and $C=A_{\mathrm{sec}}\sqrt{\lambda_+}$. There is $c_1>0$ such that uniformly on the compact class
$$
\beta_0+c_1\varepsilon\le\beta_\varepsilon\le\beta_0+C\varepsilon,
\qquad
\beta_*+c_1\varepsilon\le\inf_K\beta_\varepsilon(K)\le\beta_*+C\varepsilon.
$$
In these representatives put $q_0=\gamma_d/|P|$ and $r_s=q_0/(2A_{\mathrm{sec}})$. Ordinary deepest marks have own-boundary distance at least $q_0/A_{\mathrm{sec}}$, and buffered deepest marks have distance at least $(q_0-C\varepsilon)/A_{\mathrm{sec}}$. 2b7d1c7e003a98d0:1.reason: The exact face reduction includes full-P infimum, nonattainment on proper faces, relative attainment and the finite Hölder dual with uniqueness.
2b7d1c7e003a98d0:1.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.

2b7d1c7e003a98d0:7.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

Let $\alpha_p$ be the unique relative minimizer and $M_p=\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z$. For $p\in Q$ define
$$
T_p=\max_{\substack{0\le q_z\le m_z\\\sum_{z\in P}q_z(z-p)=0}}\sum_{z\in P}q_z,\qquad
D_p=\min_{H\ni p}\sum_{z\in P\cap H}m_z,
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed affine halfspaces in $\operatorname{aff} Q$, with the whole-space trace allowed, including rank zero. The capacity and the halfspace depth are unchanged on restriction to $P_p$ in $\operatorname{aff}F_p$. With $a$ ranging over $\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$,
$$
T_p=\inf_a\sum_{z\in P}m_z(1+a\cdot(z-p))_+,\qquad
E_p\ge T_p\ge D_p .
$$
Writing $b_N(L)=L^{-N}-(1-N(L-1))_+$ for $L>0$, one has
$$
E_p-T_p\ge\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z b_N(L_z(\alpha_p)),\qquad
E_p=T_p\ \Longleftrightarrow\ p=M_p^{-1}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z z .
$$
At equality $E_p=T_p=M_p$.

The escort masses $e_z=m_z L_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$ and zero off $P_p$ are dominated by the $m_z$ exactly when $\alpha_p=0$. The largest scalar $c\ge0$ with $c e_z\le m_z$ for all $z$ is $c=\min_{z\in P_p}L_z(\alpha_p)^{N+1}$. The resulting dominated row has total mass $cE_p$ and mean $p$. On the whole of $Q$, $E_p\le M$ with equality exactly at the original weighted base mean. If this mean is occupied and the compatible-fiber assumptions of the face-attainment result hold with $m_z=|K_z|$, its escort-selected continuous coordinate equals the original volume-weighted fiber centroid.

Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and lattice-complete with at least two points. $$
t_z=r_z+\varepsilon(R-\|z\|^2),\qquad
\lambda=\left(\frac{\sum_zr_z^d}{\sum_zt_z^d}\right)^{1/d},\qquad s_z=\lambda t_z.
$$
For every $\varepsilon\ge0$ the family $s_zK$ is compatible and preserves $M$ and each canonical budget $\gamma_dM$. If $\varepsilon>0$, every anchored radius gap for a representation of its target using only other sites is at least $\lambda\varepsilon\min_{p\ne q}\|p-q\|^2$. Consequently there is an open product neighborhood of independently variable convex fibers around this family, each realized with exactly the original integer bases. An affine shear for the centroid field or use of the induced relative lattice preserves these conclusions.

If $d\ge2$, there are arbitrarily close actual compatible simplex families whose total volume is strictly larger and whose mass in each fixed canonical cap is strictly smaller. At any strictly compatible family, let $V_p,V_q$ be the positive volumes of two distinct fibers, $m=d+1$, and let $c$ be a nonzero zero-sum column vector in $\mathbb R^m$. The opposing weighted vertex lifts used below have aggregate Lagrangian Hessian
$$
H=\frac{d^2-1}{d(dm-1)}\|c\|^2\left(V_p+V_p^2/V_q\right)>0.
$$
A vertex acceleration gives second derivative $-\gamma_dH/2$ in every aggregate cap and $H/2$ in the total volume. For $d=1$ both fixed canonical cap budgets cannot be lowered while increasing total volume.

2d0fea5cdbf7c841:05.statement:
Let $n\ge0,d,N\ge1$, let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite nonempty and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be fixed full-dimensional compact polytopes. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with summed fiber volume $\mu$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For $N$ cap margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, $\lVert u_i\rVert=1$, let $H_i=\{L_i\ge0\}$, $c_i=\mu(S\cap H_i)$, $\Psi_i=\int (L_i)_+\,d\mu$, $\Psi=\sum_i\Psi_i$, $s=\max_i c_i/M$, and $F_z=\min_{x\in K_z}\max_i L_i(z,x)$. Let $J\subset(0,1)$ consist of budgets $\tau$ admitting a cover ($F_z\ge0$ for all $z$) with $s\le\tau$, and $v(\tau)$ be the minimum hinge. The minimum is attained, $J$ is upward closed in $(0,1)$, and $v$ is nonincreasing and $C^1$ locally on $\operatorname{int}J$ except at a finite set.

At every such regular budget and every minimizing cover there exist $r_i,\eta_z\ge0$ with $r_i(c_i-\tau M)=0$, $\eta_zF_z=0$, and $M\sum_i r_i=-v'(\tau)$. Set $Z_i=\int_{H_i} z\,d\mu$, $X_i=\int_{H_i} x\,d\mu$. For each cap use one consistent section measure $d\omega_i=\theta_{iz}\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\lVert u_i\rVert$ on each $K_z\cap\{L_i=0\}$, with $0\le\theta_{iz}\le1$ and $\theta_{iz}=1$ a.e. on proper sections, yielding moments $(S_i,Z_i^s,X_i^s)=\int(1,z,x)\,d\omega_i$. For every $z$ with $\eta_z>0$ there is a finite probability law on actual saddle pairs $(x,\lambda)$ for $F_z$. Let $p_{zi}=\int\lambda_i$ and $q_{zi}=\int\lambda_i x$ for that law. The stress has objective multiplier one and satisfies
$$
\begin{aligned}
c_i+r_i S_i&=\sum_z\eta_z p_{zi},\\
Z_i+r_i Z_i^s&=\sum_z\eta_z z p_{zi},\\
X_i+r_i X_i^s&=\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}+\Psi_i u_i.
\end{aligned}
$$
In the tangent equation prior to eliminating the sphere normal, its multiplier is $-\Psi_i$. The section measure uses counting measure for $d=1$.

311680d006cf5fea:01.statement:
Let an actual planar convex body have positive integer interval fibers $I_i=[l_i,r_i]$ of widths $w_i>0$ at $i=0,\ldots,N-1$; other fibers have zero length or are empty. Put $M=\sum_i w_i$ and $R_*=\max_{j,y\in I_j}\sum_i|I_i\cap(2y-I_{2j-i})|$, with zero terms for missing or null fibers. For each $j$, let $K_j=\min(j,N-1-j)$, $N_j=2K_j+1$, $C_j=\sum_{0\le 2j-i<N}w_iw_{2j-i}$, and $\Delta_j=N_j w_j^2-C_j$. Then
$
(N_jw_j-R_*)_+^2\le N_j\Delta_j,\qquad
R_*\ge N_jw_j-\sqrt{N_j\Delta_j}>\frac{C_j}{2w_j}.
$
With $s_k=(w_{j-k}+w_{j+k})/2$ the defect decomposes as
$
\Delta_j=2\sum_{k=1}^{K_j}(w_j-s_k)(w_j+s_k)
+\tfrac12\sum_{k=1}^{K_j}(w_{j-k}-w_{j+k})^2.
$
In particular $R_*<M/2$ implies $\Delta_j\ge (N_jw_j-M/2)_+^2/N_j$, strictly when $N_jw_j>M/2$. For an exact limitation of these conditions, the actual fibers $[0,2],[0,6],[0,10],[0,3]$ satisfy the full set of defect inequalities with proposed budget $b=10\ge\max_i w_i$, although $b<M/2$ and their actual $R_*$ equals $12$.

316afa5f01281a91:01.statement:
Let $K_-,K_0,K_+\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(K_-+K_+)/2\subset K_0$. Let $n:U\subset\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb S^{d-1}$ be a $C^2$ injective immersion of rank $k$ on an open set, let $m=d-1-k$, and assume $h_i(t)=h_{K_i}(n(t))$ is $C^2$ for each body. Suppose the actual support faces at $n(t)$ have affine dimension $m$, and their relative interiors give regular boundary patches with the indicated unique normal and ordinary surface measure given by the area Jacobian of the one-to-one affine-face parametrizations below. Use common orthonormal frames $N(t)$ of $\operatorname{im}Dn(t)$ and $E(t)$ of $L(t)=\ker n(t)^{\mathsf T}\cap\ker Dn(t)^{\mathsf T}$ locally. For the canonical perpendicular origins $a_i(t)$ of the affine face hulls and points $X_i(t,s)=a_i(t)+E(t)s$ on those faces, put $R=N^{\mathsf T}Dn$ and $Q_i(t,s)=D^2h_i(t)-\sum_j X_{i,j}(t,s)D^2 n_j(t)$. For $k>0$, the $Q_i$ are positive semidefinite and the actual marked surface densities relative to the common $dt\,ds$ are $J_i=\det Q_i/|\det R|$.

Write $Z=\{t:h_0(t)=(h_-(t)+h_+(t))/2\}$. At Lebesgue-almost every $t\in Z$, and at every point of an open tight chart, $a_0=(a_-+a_+)/2$. For every endpoint face pair at such a parameter, its physical midpoint is $X_0(t,s_0)$ with $s_0=(s_-+s_+)/2$, and $Q_0(t,s_0)=(Q_-(t,s_-)+Q_+(t,s_+))/2$. For $k>0$ this gives
$$
J_0(t,s_0)^{1/k}\ge \frac{J_-(t,s_-)^{1/k}+J_+(t,s_+)^{1/k}}2.
$$
If $m>0$, in particular $J_0(t,s_0)\ge ((J_-(t,s_-)^{-1/m}+J_+(t,s_+)^{-1/m})/2)^{-m}$, with zero on the right if either input is zero. For $m=0$ the conditional densities are singleton masses and $J_0\ge\min(J_-,J_+)$. For $k=0$ the fixed normal has unit Euclidean facet density, including unit endpoint counting mass when $d=1$.

Let $U$ and $X$ be compact, with $U$ a metric space of recorded normals and $X$ in a finite-dimensional affine physical space. Let finite positive measures $\eta_j$ on $U\times X$ converge weakly to $\eta$. For each $j$ the physical projection of $\operatorname{supp}\eta_j$ lies in a compact convex body range on which the finite minimum of affine functions $L_j$ is positive. Assume the $L_j$ converge uniformly on $X$ to a nonnegative $L$, $\eta(Z)=0$ for $Z=\{(u,w):L(w)=0\}$, and $\sup_j\int \ell_{j,+}\,d\eta_j<\infty$, where $\ell_j=-\log L_j$ on the support of $\eta_j$. Suppose $0\le W_j\le1$, $W_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup W\eta$, $\beta_j\to\beta$, and $\lambda_j>0$ tends to zero. Assume $|R_j|\le C\lambda_j$ $\eta_j$-almost everywhere and that the common inequality
$$
\int \psi(u)\Phi(w)(W_j-\beta_j+\lambda_j\ell_j+R_j)\,d\eta_j\le0
$$
holds for every continuous $\psi\ge0$ and every globally finite convex $\Phi$ on the physical space.

The measures $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ have bounded masses. Along any joint weakly converging subsequence write the limits of $\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, $W_j\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, and $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ as $\ell_+\eta+b$, $W\ell_+\eta+a$, and $q$, respectively, with $\ell=-\log L$ off $Z$. Then $0\le a\le b$ and $q\ge0$, all three supported on $Z$. For every such $\psi$ and every nonnegative globally finite convex $f$,
$$
\int\psi(u)f(w)\,d(a+q)\le\beta\int\psi(u)f(w)\,db .
$$
In particular $a(U\times X)+q(U\times X)\le\beta b(U\times X)$.

3502773126e88b57:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body, let $\mu$ be uniform probability on $K$, and let $\pi:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R^r$ be a surjective linear map with $1\le r\le D$. Put $\nu=\pi_\#\mu$ and $B=\pi K$. Let $\alpha$ be the maximum closed-halfspace depth for $\nu$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its set of maximizers. The set $\mathcal A$ is nonempty and compact in $\operatorname{int}B$. Let $\ell$ have width one on $B$ and let $p$ be the scalar section-volume density of $\ell_\#\nu$, extended by zero off its support. Then $0\le p\le D$. For each $c_*\in\mathcal A$, put $t_*=\ell(c_*)$ and $L=t_*-\min_B\ell$. Then $p(t_*)\ge\alpha$ and
$$
\nu\{x:t_*-a\le\ell(x)\le t_*\}\ge\alpha a/D\qquad (0\le a\le L).
$$
In particular, if $c\in B$ and $\ell(c_*-c)\ge0$, the cap $\{x:\ell(x-c)\ge0\}$ has mass at least $\alpha+(\alpha/D)\ell(c_*-c)$.

$$
\max_i\ell_i(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_{r-1}-\tau}{D}\qquad(v\in\partial(B-B)).

Equivalently, the convex hull of the $\ell_i$ contains $(\gamma_{r-1}-\tau)(B-B)^\circ/D$, where $(B-B)^\circ$ is the polar in the dual space. In particular, the $\ell_i$ span the dual space.

3bbe467275a530f8:01.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let $q\ge1$, and let $w_z>0$, $r_z=w_z^{1/q}$ for $z\in P$. Put $\gamma=(q/(q+1))^q$ and $c=1-\gamma$. For each $z$, form the polytope of representations $\lambda\ge0$ with $\sum_p\lambda_p=1$ and $\sum_p\lambda_pp=z$. Let $D$ have a row for $l_z-\sum_p\lambda_p l_p$ for every vertex of each such polytope, dropping any zero rows. The sample vectors of finite convex functions $\ell$ on $\operatorname{conv}P$ with $\ell(z)\ge r_z$ are exactly $\mathcal L=\{l:l\ge r,\ Dl\le0\}$. Every vector in $\mathcal L$ has a positive convex piecewise-affine interpolant on the relative domain. For $A\subseteq P$, put $V_A=\min_{l\in\mathcal L}\sum_{z\in A}l_z^q$, with $V_{\varnothing}=0$. Every minimum is attained, and so is the maximum
$$
J_*=\max_\ell\sum_{z\in P}[w_z-c\ell(z)^q]_+
=\max_{A\subseteq P}\left(\sum_{z\in A}w_z-cV_A\right).
$$

For the same $V_A$ and $D$, the following dual maxima are attained. For $q=1$,
$$
V_A=\max\{\eta\cdot r:\ \eta-D^\mathsf{T}\lambda=\mathbf1_A,\ \eta,\lambda\ge0\}.
$$
For $q>1$, put $p=q/(q-1)$ and $\kappa=(q-1)q^{-p}$. Then
$$
V_A=\max\left\{\eta\cdot r-\kappa\sum_{z\in A}a_z^p:
\eta-D^\mathsf{T}\lambda=a,\ \eta,\lambda,a\ge0,\ a_z=0\ (z\notin A)\right\}.
$$
No strict feasibility assumption is needed.

3bbe467275a530f8:03.statement:
Fix an integer $q\ge1$, a volume-one convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^q$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and $0<a\le b$. The body over $[-1,1]$ with fiber $(b-(b-a)|z|)K$ is full-dimensional and has integer fibers of masses $(a^q,b^q,a^q)$. $$
J_*=\gamma b^q+\max\left\{2[a^q-cb^q]_+,\ \gamma a^q+[a^q-c(2b-a)^q]_+\right\}.
$$

$$

U(\theta)=-\alpha_j(1-\theta)^2/2\quad(b\le\theta\le1).

3d8aa8562dba80fc:01.statement:

4103337048e3d0cb:7.statement:
Fix $k\ge0$ and $m\ge1$. Let $C_\ell\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^m$ be compact and convex. Assume that all $C_\ell$ have the same finite nonempty integer fiber base set $P$, that $K_{z,\ell}=(C_\ell)_z$ for $z\in P$ lie in one bounded region, and that $M_\ell=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{z,\ell}|_m>0$ tends to zero. Suppose $K_{z,\ell}\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance and $\mathbf1_{K_{z,\ell}}dx/M_\ell\rightharpoonup\mu_z$ for every $z\in P$. Put $p_z=|\mu_z|$ and $P_+=\{z:p_z>0\}$. Then $\sum_zp_z=1$ and $P_+=\operatorname{conv}(P_+)\cap\mathbb Z^k$. For $z\in P_+$, $\operatorname{supp}\mu_z=K_z$ and $q_z=\dim\operatorname{aff}K_z<m$. For $q_z>0$, the density $f_z$ of $\mu_z$ relative to $\mathcal H^{q_z}$ on $K_z$ has a bounded representative whose $1/(m-q_z)$ power is upper semicontinuous and concave on $K_z$ and positive and continuous on $\operatorname{relint}K_z$. For $q_z=0$, $\mu_z$ is a point mass of size $p_z$.

There exist compact convex $L_z\subset\mathbb R^m_x\times\mathbb R^m_y$ of intrinsic affine dimension $m$, using a single additional $\mathbb R^m_y$, with $\mathcal H^m(L_z)=p_z$ and $(\operatorname{pr}_x)_\#(\mathcal H^m|_{L_z})=\mu_z$. Every combination of bases $z_i\in P_+$ with $\lambda_i>0$, $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ and $j=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i\in\mathbb Z^k$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_iL_{z_i}\subset L_j$. The hull $H$ of the placed $L_z$ has exactly those integer fibers and no other integer bases.

In saturated coordinates on the affine base span, $H$ is affinely equivalent to a full-dimensional convex body $H'\subset\mathbb R^{k'}\times\mathbb R^D$, where $k'=\dim\operatorname{aff}P_+\le k$ and $m\le D\le2m$. The equivalence preserves the sample census and is an isometry on each continuous fiber. An affine map $\Pi$ from the reduced ambient space pushes the intrinsic mixed $\mathcal H^m$ probability of $H'$ to $\sum_{z\in P_+}\delta_z\otimes\mu_z$. It maps every mixed point of $H'$ to the corresponding physical limiting fiber and its closed-halfspace depth cannot decrease under this pushforward.

41893e0c805c3bf4:01.statement:
Take a finite nonempty base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ with positive prior $\pi_z$ and fixed uniform laws on positive compact convex fibers $K_z$. Let
$$
Z(a,t)=\sum_z\pi_z e^{a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2},\qquad p_z(a,t)=\pi_z e^{a\cdot z-t|z|^2/2}/Z(a,t).
$$
For a bounded fixed statistic with fiber means $g_z$, put $G=\sum_z p_zg_z$ and $m=\sum_zp_zz$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
\nabla_a\log Z&=m,&D_a^2\log Z&=\operatorname{Cov}_p(z),&
\partial_t\log Z&=-\tfrac12\mathbb E_p|z|^2,\\
\nabla_aG&=\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,z),&
D_a^2G&=\mathbb E_p[(g-G)(z-m)(z-m)^{\mathsf T}],&
\partial_tG&=-\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,|z|^2).
\end{aligned}
$$
In particular $(\partial_t+m\cdot\nabla_a+\Delta_a/2)G=0$. Sample $Z_0\sim\pi$ and independent standard Brownian motion $B_t$; observe $A_t=tZ_0+B_t$. In the observation filtration the conditional base probabilities are $p_z(A_t,t)$, and the innovation $W_t=A_t-\int_0^t m_s\,ds$ is Brownian. The processes $p_z,G$ are bounded martingales with $dp_z=p_z(z-m)\cdot dW$ and $dG=\operatorname{Cov}_p(g,z)\cdot dW$. For fixed actual mark $Y$, its normalized depth $D_Y(p)$ for this measure is a concave $1$-Lipschitz function of $p$ in $\ell^1$ and is a supermartingale. The attained maximum $D_*(p)$ over actual marks is also $1$-Lipschitz.

$$
P_j(y)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n,\ w\in\mathcal W_d}\sum_{p\in P}
\left|r_pT_d\cap\{X:a\cdot\Delta_p+w\cdot X\ge w\cdot y\}\right|.
$$

49e262af8d182671:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define
$$
E_K(y)=\min_{\substack{a\in\mathbb R^d\\1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}}
\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx,\qquad
T_K(y)=\max_{\substack{0\le f\le1\\\int_K(x-y)f(x)\,dx=0}}\int_Kf(x)\,dx,
$$
where $f$ is Lebesgue measurable. Both extrema are attained, and the energy minimizer is unique. The maximizing density for $T_K(y)$ is the indicator, up to null sets, of a unique convex cap of centroid $y$. The cap is all of $K$ at its centroid. In particular $T_K(y)$ is the greatest volume of a convex subbody of $K$ with centroid $y$.

For every such $(K,y)$,
$$
0<T_K(y)\le E_K(y)<(d+1)T_K(y).
$$
Equality $T_K(y)=E_K(y)$ holds exactly when $y$ is the centroid of $K$. For each fixed $d\ge1$, the supremum of $E_K(y)/T_K(y)$ over these pairs is $d+1$, and no pair attains it. More precisely, if $K=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$ and $y=(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1/(d+1)$, then
$$
\frac{E_K(y)}{T_K(y)}=(d+1)(1-d\varepsilon).
$$
For an arbitrary simplex of volume $V$ and an interior mark with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, $E_K(y)=V(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. In dimension one, for $K-y=[-\ell,r]$ with $\ell,r>0$, $T_K(y)=2\min(\ell,r)$ and $E_K(y)=4\ell r/(\ell+r)$.

4a8c4181997d22b7:03.statement:
Let $B$ be the standard $5$-simplex, of volume $V=1/120$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_5$, where $\lambda_i=x_i$ for $i\ge1$. Set
$$

$$
Let $D$ be the simplex with vertices $p=(0,11/12,0,0,0)$, $b_0=(r,\ell,0,0,0)$, and $b_0+T e_i$ for $2\le i\le5$, where $e_i$ are the coordinate vectors. Put $m=rT^4$, $q=m^{-1/5}$, $A=(2-q)D$, $C=qD$, and $a=(2m^{1/5}-1)^5$. Let $K$ be the convex hull of the lifts of $A,B,C$ at levels $-1,0,1$, respectively. These are its exact integer fibers, of volumes $aV,V,V$, with $0<a<10^{-5}$. Write $\mu_K$ for their summed five-dimensional volume, regarded as a measure on the ambient space.

Let $y$ be the interior point of $B$ with
$$
\lambda_1(y)=\frac16-\frac a3,\qquad \lambda_i(y)=\frac16+\frac a{15}\quad(i\ne1).
$$
Then $y\notin\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$.

Writing $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, the infimum of $\mu_K(H)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(0,y)$ is strictly greater than $\Gamma_5(1+a/2)V$. Thus $(0,y)$ has normalized depth strictly greater than $\Gamma_5/2$ in $K$.

Use exactly two caps with unit continuous normals, required to cover the whole continuous line at each binary base, and impose cap mass at most $\tau M$. Feasibility holds exactly for $\tau\ge1/2$, and the minimum total hinge is $v(\tau)=4L$ throughout that range.

The minimizing pair $x\ge0,x\le0$ has an objective-one mass and moment stress with zero cap-budget multipliers, balanced weights $(1/2,1/2)$ and contact $x=0$ at each base, and $\eta_z=1$. The identity $M\sum_i r_i=-v'(\tau)=0$ holds for $1/2<\tau<1$. The source measure $\nu$ obtained by summing the cap restrictions of mixed volume is the original mixed volume. Label its two parts by their continuous normal $U=\epsilon_z$. If $x$ is projected in $L^2(\nu)$ onto the affine base features, the prediction is identically zero. $$
A=4,\quad Q=4L,\quad R_x=4L^2+1/3,\qquad
R_x-QA^+Q=1/3,\quad \frac{R_x}{QA^+Q}=1+\frac{1}{12L^2}.
$$
Consequently no coefficient greater than one can hold uniformly in the source regression bound $R_x\ge QA^+Q$, even within these actual minimizing whole-line covers.

501dba519aa398a9:01.statement:

Set $b=1/(d+1)$, $\Gamma=(1-b)^d$ and $\kappa=dV(1-b)^{d-1}$. At each of the four bases in $\{0,1\}^2$ place $T$. At $r=(-1,0)$, $p=(-1,1)$ and $p'=(1,-1)$ place convex bodies $R_t,A_t,C_t\subseteq T$ of respective volumes $t w_t,t a_t,t c_t$, where $(w_t,a_t,c_t)\to(w,a,c)\in(0,\infty)^3$ as $t\downarrow0$. Take their lifted convex hull and use the sum of $d$-volumes on the actual integer fibers and all closed ambient halfspaces. The auxiliary six-base hull deletes the generator at $r$. Let $q=(0,0)$, let $D_{6,t}^0$ and $D_{7,t}^0$ be the maximum raw depths on the $q$ fibers, and let $D_{7,t}$ be the global maximum raw depth in the seven-base hull.

The seven listed sites are precisely the actual integer fibers, with their placed bodies unchanged, and the total mixed volume is $M_t=4V+t(w_t+a_t+c_t)$. There is a fixed neighborhood $U\subseteq T$ of $g$ such that for every sufficiently small $t$ and every $y\in U$ the raw depth at $(q,y)$ in the seven-base hull is its six-base raw depth plus $tw_t$. All local maxima are attained. The full sets of $q$-fiber maximizers coincide for sufficiently small $t$ and all their marks are $O(t)$ from $g$, so $D_{7,t}^0=tw_t+D_{6,t}^0$.

At bases $(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)$ the raw local maxima are respectively $\Gamma V+ta_t$, $\Gamma V+tc_t$ and $\Gamma V$ for sufficiently small $t$. The first two occur only at $g$ in their fibers. Every added-fiber mark has depth at most the mass of its fiber. Thus
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+\max\{ta_t,tc_t,tw_t+D_{6,t}^0-\Gamma V\}.
$$
In particular, if $D_{6,t}^0=\Gamma V+t\bar J+o(t)$ and $L=\max\{a,c,w+\bar J\}$, then
$$
D_{7,t}=\Gamma V+tL+o(t),\qquad
\frac{D_{7,t}}{M_t}=\frac{\Gamma}{4}
+t\frac{4L-\Gamma(w+a+c)}{16V}+o(t).
$$
A strictly largest term among $a,c,w+\bar J$ forces every global maximizer into its corresponding base $(0,1),(1,0),q$. In the first two cases the centroid there is the unique global maximizer.

Let $q=(0,0)$, let $D_{6,t}^0$ and $D_{7,t}^0$ be the maximum raw depths on the $q$ fibers, and let $D_{7,t}$ be the global maximum raw depth in the seven-base hull.

Assume either of these two regimes.

- The normalized uniform laws of $A_t,C_t$ converge weakly to $\nu,\omega$, respectively, and both limits give zero mass to every level of every $\lambda_i$. Set
  $J_i=\min_{s\in\mathbb R}[a\,\nu\{\lambda_i\ge b+s\}+c\,\omega\{\lambda_i\ge b-s\}]$.
- With $\epsilon_t=t^{1/d}$, write $A_t=g+\epsilon_t B_t$ and $C_t=g+\epsilon_t E_t$ where $B_t,E_t$ converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional convex bodies $B,E$. Then $a=|B|,c=|E|$. Set

53c44db9ae559bfe:01.statement:
If $D$ is an $m$-dimensional compact convex set, $m\ge1$, and $F:D\to[0,\infty)$ is concave with $F(x_0)\ge c>0$ at some $x_0\in D$, then
$$
|\{F<t\}|_m\le [1-(1-t/c)^m]|D|_m\le (m|D|_m/c)t\quad(0<t<c).
$$
In particular, for $B\ge0$ with $e^{-B}<c$, the integral of $(-\log F)_+$ over $\{(-\log F)_+>B\}$ is at most $(m|D|_m/c)(B+1)e^{-B}$.

Let full-dimensional compact convex $K_j\subset\mathbb R^d$ in a common ball converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional $K$. Let $L_j$ be positive concave on $K_j$, with uniform convergence on the common compact range to a continuous $L$ that is nonnegative on $K$ and positive on its interior. Put $\Pi_j=\{u_j\cdot X=t_j\}$, with $(u_j,t_j)\to(u,t)$ and $|u_j|\ge b_*>0$, $D_j=K_j\cap\Pi_j$, and $0\le\lambda_j\le |u_j|^{-1}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_j}$. Take a subsequence with $\lambda_j\rightharpoonup\lambda$ and $(-\log L_j)_+\lambda_j\rightharpoonup\mu$ finite. The section-log defect is $s=\mu|_{\{L=0\}}$. Uniformly positive section anchors imply $s=0$ and $\mu=(-\log L)_+\lambda$, as does a limiting plane $\Pi=\{u\cdot X=t\}$ meeting the interior of $K$. If $s\ne0$, every retained Hausdorff limit of the nonempty $D_j$ is contained in $\{L=0\}\cap K$.

If additionally $L$ on $K$ is a finite minimum of affine functions and $\sup_j\int_{K_j}1/L_j<\infty$, then each exposed affine zero face has dimension at most $d-2$ for $d\ge2$. A nonzero $s$ then forces $\mathcal H^{d-1}(D_j)\to0$ and $\lambda_j(D_j)\to0$ along its retained subsequence. For $d=1$ the section measure uses counting measure, a uniformly positive anchor suffices directly, and the finite-affine and inverse-integral hypotheses imply that $L$ has no zero in $K$.

54f82268e7df4e32:02.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be compact convex bodies of positive volume. Write $\mu$ for the sum of their labeled fiber volumes, $M=\int d\mu$, and $\beta$ for the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth on the sampled fibers. Assume this maximum is locally minimized at $L=1$ when the measure on the same sampled family is reweighted by $L(p)^{-d}$ for positive affine $L$ near $1$. Equivalently one can use ordinary fiber volumes of the image family $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$.

Select finitely many circuits indexed by $i$, at least one at each deepest base. In each circuit the caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad \|u_{ij}\|_2=1,
$$
have mass $\beta M$, pass through the same interior deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$, and have weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base assume there is a fixed finite cover of the entire fiber plane by caps of mass strictly below $\beta M$. Define $\delta_{ip}=p-p_i$, $T_{ijp}=b_{ij}-a_{ij}\cdot p$, and $F_{ijp}(s)=|K_p\cap\{u_{ij}\cdot x\ge s\}|$. Assume $F_{ijp}$ is $C^2$ near $T_{ijp}$ for all $i,j,p$. At that threshold set
$$
S_{ijp}=-F'_{ijp},\quad R_{ijp}=-F''_{ijp},\quad S_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}>0,\qquad
\kappa_{ij}=\frac{\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}}{\sum_l \rho_{il}/S_{il}}.
$$
Put $H^*_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $V_{ij}=\sum_p S_{ijp}\delta_{ip}\delta_{ip}^{\mathsf T}$, $h_{ij}=\sum_p R_{ijp}\delta_{ip}$, and $k_{ij}=-\sum_p R_{ijp}$. Use matrices on $\operatorname{span}(P-P)$. Then $H^*_{ij}\succeq0$. For an affine direction $A$ with linear part $b$, define
$$
B_{ij}(A)=-d\int_{H_{ij}}A\,d\mu,\quad t_i(A)=\sum_j\kappa_{ij}B_{ij}(A),\quad
g_i(A)=t_i(A)+d\beta\int A\,d\mu,
$$
and put $v_{ij}=(B_{ij}(A)-t_i(A))/S_{ij}$, $w_{ij}=dV_{ij}b-v_{ij}h_{ij}$. The first-order condition is $\max_i g_i(A)\ge0$ for every affine $A$.

Fix any $A$ with $\max_i g_i(A)=0$. Let $I_0(A)=\{i:g_i(A)=0\}$ and $J(A)=\{i\in I_0(A): w_{ij}\in\operatorname{ran}H^*_{ij}\text{ for all }j\}$. For $i\in J(A)$ set
$$
n_i(A)=d(d+1)\left[\sum_j\kappa_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}}A^2\,d\mu-\beta\int A^2\,d\mu\right]
 +\sum_j\kappa_{ij}\left[k_{ij}v_{ij}^2-w_{ij}^{\mathsf T}(H^*_{ij})^\dagger w_{ij}\right].
$$
Here the dagger denotes the inverse on the range and zero on the kernel. Then $J(A)$ is nonempty and there are weights $\pi_i\ge0$ on $J(A)$ with
$$
\sum_i\pi_i=1,\qquad \sum_i\pi_i g_i=0\text{ as an affine-direction functional},\qquad
\sum_i\pi_i n_i(A)\ge0.
$$
Moreover, if $W$ is a linear space of affine directions on which every $g_i$ vanishes, let $E(W)$ be the groups $i$ for which $A\mapsto w_{ij}(A)$ belongs to $\operatorname{ran}H^*_{ij}$ for every $A\in W$ and every $j$. Then $0\in\operatorname{conv}\{g_i:i\in E(W)\}$.

55fd8fec61360536:03.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with affine coordinates $(v,t,y)$, where $v\in\mathbb R^r$, $1\le r\le D-1$, $y\in\mathbb R^{D-r-1}$, and $t\ge0$ on $K$. Write $J>0$ for the constant volume Jacobian of these coordinates. The pushforward of $D$-volume on $K\cap\{t>0\}$ under $z=v/t$ has bounded integrable density
$$
F(z)=J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_K(tz,t,y)t^r\,dy\,dt
    =J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_\Omega(z,s,w)s^{-(D+1)}\,dw\,ds,
$$
where $\Omega=\{(z,s,w):s>0,\ (z/s,1/s,w/s)\in K\}$. The set $\{F>0\}$ is convex and full-dimensional, and $F^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex on it. Its boundary may be discarded without changing the measure. The total mass is $|K|$, and any cap on $K$ with margin $a\cdot v+bt$ has exactly the mass of $\{z:a\cdot z+b\ge0\}$ under $F(z)\,dz$.

55fd8fec61360536:05.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$, with $D\ge1$. Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be proper closed halfspaces covering $K$, where $m\ge1$, and write $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$. Put $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for integers $q\ge1$. For any fixed inclusion-minimal subcover indexed by $I$, let $j=|I|$ and let $\rho$ be the rank of its normals. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\sum_{i\in I}(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\min(\rho,j-1)}}\ge V,
\qquad x_+=\max(x,0).
$$
Consequently, with $s=\min(D,m-1)$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_s}\ge V
\quad(\alpha\ge0),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge (m-1/\gamma_s)\min_i A_i .
$$
For each pair $(D,m)$, $\gamma_s$ is the largest constant that can replace it in the all-cover positive-part profile.

$$

56a670ccbde263ec:01.statement:
Let $C$ be a full-dimensional $(n+d)$-simplex in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$. Choose $n+1$ vertices with affinely independent base projections and let $Q$ be their projected $n$-simplex. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ be the other projected vertices and $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ their barycentric coordinates. The map to $(z,x)$ fixes the base $z$ and is an affine bijection taking $C$ to
$$
\mathcal C=\{(z,x):x\in T_d,\ z\in\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\},\qquad S=\sum_jx_j,\quad T_d=\{x\ge0:S\le1\}.
$$
The image volume is $n!|Q|/(n+d)!$ and the absolute continuous-coordinate Jacobian is $J=n!|Q|/((n+d)!|C|)$. It multiplies full $d$-volume on each integer fiber and every mixed closed cap mass by $J$. For positive mixed total mass, it transports normalized depth and the mixed centroid. The continuous projection of raw mixed measure in these new coordinates has density
$$
N(x)=\left|\mathbb Z^n\cap\left(\textstyle\sum_jh_jx_j+(1-S)Q\right)\right|\qquad(x\in T_d)
$$
and zero outside $T_d$. For $n=1$ choose the extreme projected vertices $a<b$. The interval has endpoints $\ell(x)=a+\sum_j(h_j-a)x_j$, $u(x)=b+\sum_j(h_j-b)x_j$, with width $(b-a)(1-S)$. Its count is $\max(0,\lfloor u(x)\rfloor-\lceil\ell(x)\rceil+1)$. For $n=0$ use $|Q|_0=1$ and $N=1$ on $T_d$.

For $c<0$ its mass is the full mixed mass, and for $c\ge1$ it has zero mixed mass. The formula includes vertical caps and closed boundary fibers.

571b5ceb2d4e114a:01.statement: Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, and $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies for $p\in P$. Fix $q\in P$. 571b5ceb2d4e114a:03.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge3$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$. For each $p\in P$ let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let $E_q$ be the polytope of nonnegative coefficient vectors $(\lambda_p)_{p\ne q}$ with $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1$ and $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q$. The family is strictly compatible if for every $q\in P$ and every extreme point $\lambda$ of $E_q$, the Minkowski sum $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. An empty $E_q$ imposes no condition. Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ and assume its actual integer fibers are the given $K_p$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on those fibers, $M$ its total mass, $\beta$ the maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth over the measured points, and $I$ the bases where this maximum is attained. Assume that $C$ is a local minimum of $\beta$ among all actual positive fiber families on this fixed $P$, in the fiberwise Hausdorff topology.

For each $p\in I$ fix a finite positive circuit of actual critical caps $H_{pj}=\{(z,x):a_{pj}\cdot z+u_{pj}\cdot x\ge b_{pj}\}$, with $\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1$, $\rho_{pj}>0$, and $\sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0$. Each circuit passes through an interior maximizing mark of its own fiber and its caps have raw mass $Q=\beta M$. Assume each old aggregate threshold mass is $Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ when its threshold is moved by $s\to0$ from either side, with $S_{pj}>0$. Write $\kappa_{pj}=(\rho_{pj}/S_{pj})/\sum_\ell(\rho_{p\ell}/S_{p\ell})$. Let a finite collection of nonempty relatively open boundary patches $U$ be given, each in some $\partial K_q$, with $U$ a $C^1$ hypersurface containing no nontrivial line segment.

There exists one probability vector $\pi$ on $I$ such that on every patch in the collection, at each point $x$ off all restricted cap planes, $\sum_{p\in I,j}\pi_p\kappa_{pj}\mathbf1_{H_{pj}}(q,x)=\beta$. For every listed unoriented restricted plane $L$ that meets the patch and intersects $\operatorname{int}K_q$, the total weight $\pi_p\kappa_{pj}$ of the restricted caps with plane $L$ is the same in either orientation.

If a patch in fiber $q$ is the whole boundary, let $F_q$ be the total stress weight of nonproper cap restrictions that contain the whole boundary off the planes, and $P_q$ the total stress weight of properly cutting restricted caps. Then $\beta=F_q+P_q/2$. For such a fiber with $q\in I$ one has $\pi_q\le2\beta$. If the collection includes the entire boundary of every deepest fiber, then $\beta\ge 1/(2|I|)$. The two-sided positive slope hypothesis holds automatically if every $K_p$ is strictly convex.

57e3e17a84fce5c1:02.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty lattice polytope of affine dimension $s$, and let $N=|Q\cap\mathbb Z^n|$. For every integer $m\ge1$,

$$
For $s=0$, both sides equal one.

57e3e17a84fce5c1:03.statement:
Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex with $d\ge1$, let $r\in\mathbb Z^n$ and let $m\ge2$ be an integer. Write $w_p=\operatorname{vol}_d(E_p)$, $\mu(E)=\sum_{p\in\mathbb Z^n}w_p$, $A_t=\{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}$, and $a_r=\max_{p\in r+m\mathbb Z^n}w_p$ with empty maximum zero. For $0<t<a_r$ put $N_t=|A_t|$, $s_t=\dim\operatorname{aff}A_t$ and $Q_t=\operatorname{conv}((A_t-r)/m)$. Then
$$
|Q_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|=N_t,\qquad
\big|\{p\in\mathbb Z^n:w_p>t\}\big|\ge |mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\ge B_m(s_t,N_t),
$$
where $B_m(s,N)=\binom{m+s}{s}+(N-s-1)\binom{m+s-1}{s}$. Consequently
$$
\mu(E)\ge\int_0^{a_r}|mQ_t\cap\mathbb Z^n|\,dt\ge\int_0^{a_r} B_m(s_t,N_t)\,dt.
$$
The integrals are zero when $a_r=0$. At $m=2$, the integrand $B_2(s,N)=(s+1)N-s(s+1)/2$ is at least $2N-1$, giving $\mu(E)\ge 2\sum_{p\in r+2\mathbb Z^n}w_p-a_r$. With $r=0$, both integral inequalities are equalities for $E=[0,m(N-1)]\times K$ with $N\ge2$ and for $E=(m\Delta_s)\times K$, where $K$ is a $d$-dimensional convex body and $\Delta_s$ the standard unimodular simplex in its integer coordinates. The inequalities apply to $E=C\cap H$ for any compact convex $C$ and closed ambient halfspace $H$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$ put $L_a(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)$ and define
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{\{a:L_a>0\ \text{on }K\}}\int_K L_a(x)^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
The infimum is positive and attained at a unique admissible $a_*$, and $E_K(y)$ is the minimum $d$-volume of the images of $K-y$ under $w\mapsto w/(1+a\cdot w)$ over these $a$. For $L=L_{a_*}$ and $E=E_K(y)$,
$$
\int_K (x-y)L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_K L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=\int_K L(x)^{-d-1}\,dx=E.
$$
Thus $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E$ on $K$ is a probability density with barycenter $y$ and $\int_K L\rho\,dx=1$. Its restriction to $K$ extends to a smooth positive function on a neighborhood of $K$.

For every invertible linear $Q$ and every $b\in\mathbb R^d$, $E_{QK+b}(Qy+b)=|\det Q|E_K(y)$. If $K\subset H$ for another convex body $H$, then $E_K(y)\le E_H(y)$ with equality exactly when $K=H$. Writing $g_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K x\,dx$ for the ordinary centroid, $E_K(y)\le |K|$ with equality exactly when $y=g_K$.

5811f0ad1132ce56:04.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, and choose $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_i$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Use the energy $E_K(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$. Put $M=\sum_i\lambda_i K_i$ and $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}M$ and
$$
E_M(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ \sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_i}(y_i)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when the centered bodies $K_i-y_i$ with $\lambda_i>0$ are positive scalar multiples of one another. In particular $y\mapsto E_K(y)^{1/d}$ is strictly concave on $\operatorname{int}K$.

If $H$ is a convex body containing $M$, the same lower bound holds for $E_H(y)^{1/d}$. Equality then requires both $H=M$ and the same marked homothety condition. Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Put $p=(d+1)/(d+2)$ and let $E_K(y)$ be the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over affine denominators strictly positive on $K$. Then
$$
E_K(y)=\max_{\substack{\rho\ge0,\ \int_K\rho\,dx=1\\\int_K x\rho(x)\,dx=y}}
\left(\int_K\rho(x)^p\,dx\right)^{d+2}.
$$
The maximum is over ordinary Lebesgue densities on $K$ with the displayed mass and mean. Its unique maximizer up to Lebesgue null sets is $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E_K(y)$, where $L(x)=1+a_*\cdot(x-y)$ is the attained optimal denominator.

58dcf29bfb78a573:02.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite subset of a real affine space, with $k$ occupied labels. Assume the geometric midpoint of every pair of distinct points of the same label belongs to $P$. Give each $p\in P$ a weight $w_p>0$, put $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and $\alpha=M/k$, and set $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ for each face $F$ of $Q$, allowing $Q$ itself. Let $\mathcal F$ be the faces of weight $\alpha$, and write $\chi_F$ for their incidence vectors on $P$.

Exactly one of the following holds.

1. There is $v\in\mathbb R^P$ with $\sum_{p\in P}v_p=0$ and $v\cdot\chi_F<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. When $\mathcal F$ is empty, $v=0$ works.
2. The set $P$ consists of exactly $k$ vertices of $Q$, all of weight $\alpha$.

Moreover, a nonnegative combination $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\lambda_F\chi_F=\mathbf 1_P$ exists precisely in case 2. In that case its coefficients are $\lambda_{\{p\}}=1$ for all $p\in P$.
