58dcf29bfb78a573:03.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a real affine space with $k$ occupied labels. For every pair of distinct points of the same label, assume their geometric midpoint belongs to $P$. Give the points positive weights $w_p$, with total $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ whose relative interior contains $p$, allowing $Q$ itself. Write $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ and let $\delta_w(p)$ be the minimum weight in any closed affine halfspace containing $p$. The whole-space trace is allowed and is the sole trace containing $p$ in rank zero.

There exists $p\in P$ with $\delta_w(p)\ge M/k$. Such a point can be chosen with $w(F_p)>M/k$ except exactly when $P$ consists of $k$ vertices of $Q$ of weight $M/k$ each. In the exception every point has $\delta_w(p)=w(F_p)=M/k$. In particular, strict minimal-face mass holds for some center whenever $|P|>k$.

For a finite nonempty complete subset $P=Q\cap(c+L)$ of an affine lattice, the labels can be the occupied cosets modulo $2L$. Then $k\le 2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$, including rank zero. For a finite graph $P=\{(p,g_p):p\in P_0\}$ over an affine-lattice base, the labels can be the occupied base parities if every distinct same-parity pair $p,q\in P_0$ has $m=(p+q)/2\in P_0$ and $g_m=(g_p+g_q)/2$. In this graph case the depth and the minimal face are taken in the lifted space.

Let $d\ge1$ and $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. If $h$ is nonnegative affine on $D$ and vanishes somewhere on $D$, then $\int_Dh^{-r}\,dx=+\infty$ for every $r\ge d$. When $h$ is nonconstant, the cone lower bound has logarithmic divergence at $r=d$. If convex bodies $D_j$ converge in Hausdorff distance to $D$ and affine $h_j>0$ on $D_j$ converge coefficientwise to such an $h$, then $\int_{D_j}h_j^{-r}\,dx\to+\infty$.

For each $0<r<d$ the standard simplex $D=\{x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$ has positive affine $h_\delta=\delta+\sum_i x_i$, $\delta>0$, with $|D|^{-1}\int_D h_\delta^{-r}\,dx\to d/(d-r)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. 5a3c8a5af6aaf266:6.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $P$ be a fixed nonempty finite base, and let $\mathcal A$ be a compact family in the simultaneous Hausdorff metric of tuples of positive convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $z\in P$, of total volume one, with every fiber volume at least $v>0$ and all fibers contained in a fixed ball. Use mixed measure $\mu_K=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf 1_{K_z}\,dX)$, its centroid $m_K$, and $C_K=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_z(\{z\}\times K_z)$. There is $\rho>0$ such that every $C_K$ contains the relative $\rho$-ball about $m_K$. Hence the affine functions $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ with $\int h\,d\mu_K=1$ have relative linear coefficient norm at most $1/\rho$ and uniformly bounded constant coefficients in fixed relative affine coordinates.

Fix $r\ge d$. For every sequence $K_j\in\mathcal A$ and affine $L_j>0$ on $C_{K_j}$ with $\int L_j^{-r}\,d\mu_{K_j}=1$, there is a subsequence with $K_j\to K\in\mathcal A$ and $h_j=L_j/\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}$ converging coefficientwise to an affine $h\ge0$ on $C_K$ of mixed mean one. If $h>0$ on $C_K$, then $L_j$ converges coefficientwise to a finite positive normalized affine parameter on $C_K$. Otherwise $\int L_j\,d\mu_{K_j}\to+\infty$. In this second case, write $g_{j,z}$ for the actual centroid of $K_{j,z}$. If $h$ has nonzero continuous coefficient then $L_j(z,g_{j,z})\to+\infty$ for every $z\in P$. If its continuous coefficient vanishes, its base zero set is a nonempty proper exposed face $F$ of $\operatorname{conv}P$ and the same divergence holds for each $z\in P\setminus F$.

5a3c8a5af6aaf266:7.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $r\ge d$, $N=d+1$, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Choose $\beta_0^*<b<\Gamma_d/k$. Use the original sublevel's compact representative frame under invertible common continuous affine maps and affine continuous shears, with $M=\sum_z|K_z|=1$, all $|K_z|\ge v>0$ and all $K_z\subset RB_d$. Write $L_{\mathrm{slab}}=|P|\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1}$, with $\kappa_j$ the volume of the Euclidean unit $j$-ball and $\kappa_0=1$.

For a family $K$ with canonical hull $C_K$, let $L$ be affine on $\operatorname{aff}P\times\mathbb R^d$, positive on $C_K$, and normalized by $\int L^{-r}\,d\mu_K/M=1$, where $\mu_K$ sums the fiber $d$-volumes. For a mark $(p,y)$ put

G_K(u)=\left(\frac{1}{M}\sum_z\int_{K_z}[u\cdot(X-g_z)]^2\,dX\right)^{1/2},
$$
where $g_z$ is the fiber centroid and $E_{K_p}$ is the marked projective energy with value zero on the own-fiber boundary. Use unchanged pure-base closed caps and nonvertical through-mark caps enlarged by $\varepsilon f_L(p,y)G_K(u)$ in their affine margins. Let $\beta_\varepsilon(K,L)$ be the resulting maximum normalized depth. For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the joint sublevel $\{\beta_\varepsilon\le b\}$ is compact modulo the specified affine normalizations. If a reference pair has $\beta_\varepsilon<b$, the infimum over all admissible pairs is attained. A reference with $L=1$ has this property for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, and for each $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
\beta_0^*\le\inf_{K,L}\beta_\varepsilon(K,L)\le\beta_0^*+\varepsilon L_{\mathrm{slab}}R .
$$

5c1f3bb21840ea60:01.statement:
Let $T$ be a nondegenerate tetrahedron with barycentric coordinates $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_3$. For the strict split $\{0,1\}\mid\{2,3\}$, the section planes are in bijection with their interior diagonal intersection $e=(x,y,z,w)$, where $x,y,z,w>0$ and $x+y+z+w=1$. The corresponding oriented affine vertex values are $t=(1/x,1/y,-1/z,-1/w)$, with the first pair on the cap side. The cyclic section vertices are
$$
A=(x,0,z,0)/(x+z),\quad B=(x,0,0,w)/(x+w),\quad
C=(0,y,0,w)/(y+w),\quad D=(0,y,z,0)/(y+z).
$$
The barycentric section centroid is $\lambda=(A+B+C+D-e)/3$. Put $P=x+y$, $R=z+w$, $a=xy$, $b=zw$ and $\Delta=(x+z)(x+w)(y+z)(y+w)=(a-b)^2+aR+bP$. If $m=\sum_i t_i\xi_i$, the cap fraction $F=|T\cap\{m\ge0\}|/|T|$, normalized coarea $S=\mathcal H^2(T\cap\{m=0\})/(|T|\lVert\nabla m\rVert)$, effective section-normal vector and normalized scalar moment to the ordinary tetrahedral centroid $g$ are
$$
F=\frac{b(P-a+b)}{\Delta},\qquad
1-F=\frac{a(R+a-b)}{\Delta},\qquad
S=\frac{3xyzw}{\Delta},\qquad
S\nabla m,\qquad S\nabla m\cdot(g-\lambda)=\frac{3(bP-aR)}{4\Delta}.
$$
Here $\lambda$ denotes the physical point when it appears in a displacement.

Equivalently, allow arbitrary positive raw heights $t=(p,q,-r,-s)$. Define $\alpha=ps/[(p+r)(p+s)(q+s)]$ and $\delta=qr/[(p+r)(q+s)(q+r)]$. Then $F=p(\alpha+\delta)+q^2/[(q+r)(q+s)]$ and $S=3(\alpha+\delta)$. In the standard tetrahedron, the oriented cross products for $ABC$ and $ACD$ are $-\alpha\nabla m$ and $-\delta\nabla m$. In any tetrahedron, with $\tau=\alpha/(\alpha+\delta)$, the centroid is $\lambda=(A+C+\tau B+(1-\tau)D)/3$. The formulas allow repeated heights within either pair. Regarding $F$ as a function of all four signed heights, $\partial F/\partial t_i=S\lambda_i$. When the four heights are distinct, $F=\sum_{t_i>0}t_i^3/\prod_{j\ne i}(t_i-t_j)$.

Choose at each base $z_i$ an actual positive critical cap circuit through an interior maximizing mark, with cap margins $v_{ij}\cdot z+u_{ij}\cdot x-b_{ij}$, $u_{ij}\ne0$, and positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. Every cap in a circuit has the restricted maximal raw depth at its origin as its mass. Put $A_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}v_{ij}$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}b_{ij}=A_i\cdot z_i$. Select at most $2^n$ deepest-origin groups whose projected halfspaces $\{p:A_i\cdot p\ge h_i\}$ cover the deepest bases, and assign each deepest base to one of these covering groups. Such a selection exists. Assign every nondeep base to its own additional local circuit, whose caps have mass strictly below $\beta M$.

In the compatible support chart linear on each fiber's own small-erosion normal fan, allow the base coefficients and offsets of every selected cap occurrence to vary freely and keep $u_{ij},\rho_{ij}$ fixed. For every assigned pair $(i,p)$ impose $C_{ip}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}(v_{ij}\cdot p-b_{ij})\ge0$. There is an objective-one stress with nonnegative active-cap multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$, nonnegative active-coverage multipliers $\eta_{ip}$, and nonnegative multipliers of the active support and compatibility rows. Its cap covectors use consistent facet and coarea allocations. Specifically, a facet portion strictly inside a cap contributes its area times its outward support speed, and a proper cap section contributes its area divided by $\|u_{ij}\|$ times the cap margin speed $\dot v_{ij}\cdot z-\dot b_{ij}$. At a coincident facet of area $|F|$, one $\theta\in[0,1]$ supplies the facet coefficient $\theta|F|$ and the cap-margin coefficient $(1-\theta)|F|/\|u_{ij}\|$ when the body lies inside, or $\theta|F|/\|u_{ij}\|$ when it lies outside. Strictly empty and strictly full traces, and lower-dimensional supporting contacts, have zero coarea. Use counting measure for $d=1$.

Let $s_{ijz}$ be the resulting effective coarea coefficient in fiber $z$, $S_{ij}=\sum_zs_{ijz}$, and $t_i=\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}$. The same multipliers and allocations satisfy
$$
\lambda_{ij}S_{ij}=\rho_{ij}t_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij}\sum_zs_{ijz}z=\rho_{ij}\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}p .
$$
Each $S_{ij}$ is positive in a deepest-origin group. If $t_i>0$, that group is selected from a deepest origin, each $\lambda_{ij}=t_i\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}>0$, and every cap's section-base barycenter equals
$$
\bar z_i=\frac{\sum_zs_{ijz}z}{S_{ij}}
=\frac{\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}p}{t_i},
\qquad A_i\cdot\bar z_i=h_i .
$$
Thus $\bar z_i$ lies in the convex hull of its assigned globally deepest bases. Every group with $t_i=0$ has zero cap and coverage stress. The signed offsets cancel groupwise, and the full normalization is
$$
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_{ij}(b_{ij}-v_{ij}\cdot z)s_{ijz}=0
\quad\text{for every }i,\qquad
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta
=\sum_{i:t_i>0}t_i\sum_j\frac{\rho_{ij}}{S_{ij}}.
$$

6146c77d1d7c5e08:01.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $H>0$. Put $B=H+1$ and $r(z)=(H-z)/B$. On $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$, take density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{d-2}/2$ with respect to $dx\,dz$. The total mass is $V=B/d$. For finite $s\ge0$, let $P(s)$ be the mass of the cap $z+sx\ge0$. Let $C(s)$ and $M(s)$ be the integrals of $f$ and $zf$, respectively, over the section $z+sx=0$ inside the support, against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. The records of a probability law are the averages of $(P,C,M)$, and the law is centered if its averaged $M$ is zero. Write $C_0=(H/B)^{d-1}$ and $p_0=(H/B)^d$.

For a probability law on finite slopes, let $\phi$ be the mixture of uniform probability laws on $[-s,s]$ with the given slope weights and with $\delta_0$ at $s=0$. Put $v=\phi((-\infty,1])$, $a_0=1/B$, and $e(q)=\int_{b\le1}(1-qb)^{-d}\,d\phi(b)$ for $0<q<1$. Then $1/2<v\le1$ and the averaged records are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline P/V &= p_0e(a_0)+1-v,\\
\overline C/C_0 &= e(a_0),\\
\overline M/C_0 &= -\frac HB\int_{b\le1} b(1-b/B)^{-d-1}\,d\phi(b).
\end{aligned}
$$

The function $e$ is convex and differentiable on $(0,1)$. Centering is equivalent to $e'(a_0)=0$, or equivalently to $a_0$ minimizing $e$ on $(0,1)$. Every such centered law satisfies $2v-1\le e(a_0)\le(2v-1)/v$.

For real $d\ge1$, set $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and $L_d=4A_d/3-1$. Write $t_+=\max(t,0)$ and define

$$
\Delta_d=2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
   -2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-L_d/(2d))_+^{d+1},
\qquad \varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\Delta_d.
$$

Then $\Delta_d>0$. For each integer $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, let $0\le\eta\le\mathbf 1_K\,dx$, and let $g$ be the centroid of $\mathbf 1_K\,dx+2\eta$. Then $g\in\operatorname{int}K$, and every closed halfspace $H$ containing $g$ satisfies

$$
|K\cap H|+\eta(H)\ \ge\
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(|K|+\eta(K))
+\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d}{4\cdot3^d}|K|.
$$

660db01ed45063dd:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies of volumes $v,k,v>0$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of the $d$-volumes on the integer fibers $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull. The actual mixed centroid is

$$
Y=\left(0,\frac{v g_A+k g_K+v g_B}{k+2v}\right),
$$

where $g_A,g_K,g_B$ are the uniform-volume centroids. It lies in $\lbrace 0\rbrace\times\operatorname{int}K$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and let the positive constant $\varepsilon_d$ be

$$
\varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\left[2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
-2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-(4A_d/3-1)/(2d))_+^{d+1}\right],
$$

with $t_+=\max(t,0)$. The raw depth at $Y$, the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces containing $Y$, is at least

$$
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(k+v)+
\min\left(\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d k}{4\cdot3^d},
               (1-3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\right).
$$

In particular it is strictly greater than $(3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\ge(\Gamma_d/2)(k+2v)$. The same conclusion holds in any convex body whose only positive $d$-volume integer fibers are those three fibers; any other integer fibers of zero $d$-volume do not affect $\mu$.

\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_z\ge0,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p .
\tag{1}
$$
Use the given Euclidean base coordinates. The affine rank $r=\dim\operatorname{span}(P-p)$ may be any integer from $0$ to $n$. Write $h_z(u)=\max_{x\in K_z}u\cdot x$. For every $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ the inequalities
$$
h_z(u)\le h_p(u)+A\cdot(z-p)\qquad(z\in P)
\tag{2}
$$
have a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution $A_p(u)$. It lies in $\operatorname{span}(P-p)$, and the map $u\mapsto A_p(u)$ is continuous and bounded. The affine function $z\mapsto h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ yields a supporting inequality $u\cdot x\le h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ on $\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with equality at every point of the $u$-supporting face of $\{p\}\times K_p$.

Assume $d\ge2$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. Suppose exactly one row $r$ is strictly positive, with a proper minimizing threshold $t$. Write $x=X_r$, $b$ for its actual section centroid, $\lambda=c_r\nabla\phi_d(x)$ and $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$. Group the nonzero rows other than $r$ by their unique zero column, and replace each group by its sum in one of its own row labels, setting the other rows in that group to zero. Permute columns to place each surviving such row's zero on its diagonal. After this relabeling, let $\mu_i=c_i\phi_d(X_i)/d$ for each surviving row other than $r$, and set $\mu_i=0$ at unmatched labels including $r$. Write $\mu=\sum_i\mu_i$. The merger preserves the objective and gives
$$
H(X)=S,\qquad b=\lambda/S,\qquad
0<t=x\cdot b<1,\qquad
\lambda_j(1-x_j)=\mu-\mu_j,\qquad
\mu=\frac{S(1-t)}d .
$$
The image of the actual section measure under $u_j\mapsto (1-x_j)u_j/(1-t)$ is a probability on $\Delta_d$ whose $j$th centroid coordinate is
$$
\frac{(1-x_j)b_j}{1-t}=\frac1d-\frac{\mu_j}{S(1-t)}\le\frac1d.
$$
Equality holds exactly at unmatched labels. The pushforward statement includes collapsed coordinates.

Suppose the capacity vector $(\phi_d(X_i))_i$ differs from every standard unit vector and at least one row is strictly positive. Then all strictly positive rows have a unique proper minimizing threshold $t_i$, with $\min_j X_{ij}<t_i<\max_j X_{ij}$. Let $F_i=F_{X_i}(t_i)$ and let $b_i$ be the barycentric centroid of the actual section $\{u\in\Delta_d:X_i\cdot u=t_i\}$ under normalized coarea measure. There is a common vector $\lambda>0$ such that, for each strictly positive row $i$ and $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$,
$$
\lambda=c_i\nabla\phi_d(X_i)=c_i F_i^{-1/d}b_i,\qquad
c_i F_i^{-1/d}=S,\qquad b_i=\frac{\lambda}{S},
\qquad t_i=X_i\cdot b_i,\qquad c_i\phi_d(X_i)=St_i .

The same equations hold between any pair of strictly positive rows with proper minimizing thresholds at a local maximum, by comparing those rows directly.

Suppose at least one strictly positive row has a proper minimizing threshold. Let $\lambda>0$ be its weighted capacity gradient and put $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$. For a row $i$ whose only zero is in column $h$, put $g_i=\phi_d(X_i)$ and $\mu_i=c_i g_i/d$. Then
$$
X_{ij}=\frac{\mu_i}{\lambda_j}\quad(j\ne h),\qquad
c_i=d\,\operatorname{GM}_d((\lambda_j)_{j\ne h}),\qquad

Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and convex with compact nonempty integer fibers, where $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$. Write $P$ for its positive-$d$-volume integer bases, $V_z=|C_z|_d$ and $r_z=V_z^{1/d}$ on $P$. Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in C_p$. Write $D$ for the raw ambient depth at $(p,y)$ under the sum of $d$-volumes of the integer fibers, and $f$ for the ordinary raw depth of $y$ in $C_p$. For $k\ge0$ define
$$
\Phi_k(b)=\sum_{z\in P}\min\{V_z,[k+b\cdot(z-p)]_+^d\},\qquad b\in\mathbb R^n,
$$
where $[t]_+=\max(t,0)$.

Suppose $u\ne0$ gives a proper through-$y$ cap in $C_p$ with raw mass $q\in(0,V_p)$ and $k=q^{1/d}$. For every $b$ there is a closed ambient through-$(p,y)$ halfspace with continuous normal $u$ whose capture on each positive fiber is at most its summand in $\Phi_k(b)$. In particular $D\le\min_b\Phi_k(b)$. Also $D\le\min_b\Phi_{f^{1/d}}(b)\le |P|f$. Both minima are attained at finite slopes, including the zero-budget case at $b=0$ when $f=0$.

If an actual depth-attaining cap through $(p,y)$ with nonzero continuous normal has captured volume roots $a_z=a_p+\ell\cdot(z-p)$ satisfying $0<a_z<r_z$ on all of $P$, then $\ell$ minimizes $\Phi_{a_p}$ globally with minimum $Q=D=\sum_z a_z^d$. One has $\sum_z (z-p)a_z^{d-1}=0$. For $d\ge2$ this gives
$$
|P|a_p^d-Q=\sum_z(a_p-a_z)^2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)a_p^{d-2-j}a_z^j.
$$
For $d=1$ it gives $\sum_z(z-p)=0$ and $Q=|P|a_p$.

773c78a48aafd464:02.reason: The fractional-site and dual conclusions use arbitrary finite real base data and linear costs. The older proofs establish parts of the conclusion under narrower hypotheses.
773c78a48aafd464:02.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be finite, with capacities $a_z>0$ for $z\in P$. Fix a mass $m\ge0$ and a vector $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and assume
$$
Q=\{b:0\le b_z\le a_z,\ \sum_{z\in P}b_z=m,\ \sum_{z\in P}z b_z=mg\}
$$
is nonempty. A point of $Q$ is extreme exactly when the columns $(1,z)$ at its partially filled sites $0<b_z<a_z$ are linearly independent. Every linear cost $\sum_z c_zb_z$ has an extreme minimizer, and this minimizer has at most $\operatorname{rank}((1,z)_{z\in P})\le n+1$ partially filled sites.

There are a scalar $\lambda$ and vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the minimum value is
$$
\lambda m+v\cdot(mg)+\sum_{z\in P}a_z\min(0,c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z).
$$
For this pair a feasible $b$ is optimal exactly when $b_z=a_z$ at each strict negative reduced cost $c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z$ and $b_z=0$ at each strict positive one. 7e2883b5a7576b2b:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Fix $0<r\le s$ and translations $c_-,c_+\in\mathbb R^d$. The middle body $B$ is arbitrary subject to $m+\rho K\subseteq B$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. For $0<r\le s$ put
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r,&d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d,&d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d,&d\ge2,\ s\ge dr,
\end{cases}
$$
and extend $\Phi_d$ symmetrically to $r>s$. The branches agree at $s=dr$.

Let $a=r^dV$, $b=s^dV$, $U=|B|$, and let $g_B$ be the ordinary volume centroid of $B$. If $S$ is the actual mixed-integer part of the body and $h_S$ is its raw depth, then
$$
h_S((0,m))\ge V[\Gamma_d\rho^d+\Phi_d(r,s)],
\qquad
h_S((0,g_B))\ge\Gamma_d U.
$$
In particular, under the scalar condition
$$
\rho^d+\frac{\Phi_d(r,s)}{\Gamma_d}\ge r^d+s^d,
$$
choosing $(0,m)$ for $U\le a+b$ and $(0,g_B)$ for $U\ge a+b$, with either choice at equality, gives raw depth at least $\Gamma_d(a+b+U)/2$ and normalized depth at least $\Gamma_d/2$. The same conclusion holds under the simpler sufficient condition $b/a\le (3+\sqrt5)/2$.

$$
f_-(h)=F_{1-kh}(t-\beta h),\qquad f_+(h)=F_{1-kh}(t+\beta(h+1))\qquad(0\le h\le1/k)
$$
and extend both by zero for $h\ge1/k$. Each is nonnegative and convex on $[0,\infty)$. For either function $f$, the sum over nonnegative integers satisfies
$$
\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge \int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+f(0)/2,\qquad \sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge f(0).
$$
If $k\le1$ it follows that $\sum_{h\ge0}f(h)\ge(1-k)\int_0^\infty f(h)\,dh+(1+k)f(0)/2$.

Let $\Theta$ be uniform on the opposite facet $\operatorname{conv}(e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, with $\Theta=e_1$ if $d=1$, and put $U=u\cdot\Theta$. For $s>0$, $F_r(s)=\mathbb E[(r^d-(s/U)^d)_+]$, taking the integrand to be zero at $U=0$. Write $c=\beta/k$ and $B=t+\beta$. If $c>0$, then $\int_0^\infty f_\pm(h)\,dh=\mathbb E[J_\pm(U)]/[k(d+1)]$, where $J_-(U)=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_+(U)=0$ for $U\le B$. On their respective remaining domains,
$$
J_-(U)=1-\frac{t^{d+1}}{cU^d}+\frac{(t-c)^{d+1}}{c(U-c)^d},\qquad
J_+(U)=1+\frac{B^{d+1}}{cU^d}-\frac{(B+c)^{d+1}}{c(U+c)^d}.
$$
If $c=0$ the same integral formula uses $J_-=J_+=0$ for $U\le t$ and $J_-=J_+=1-(d+1)(t/U)^d+d(t/U)^{d+1}$ for $U>t$.

$$

\ge c_d(b)\bigl(\psi(g)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr)
$$

$$
c_d(b)=\frac{a-a^d/(1-b)^{d-1}}{(d-1)^2}.
$$
It is positive for $0<b<1/d$ and vanishes at both endpoints. The test $\psi(x)=\min_i x_i$ attains equality with a positive Jensen gap throughout the parameter interval. In particular,
$$

$$
E_d(\psi)=m\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb E\psi(Y_{1/m})-\mathbb E\psi(Z)\bigr).
$$
For every continuous concave $\psi$ and every supporting affine majorant $\ell$ at $g_F$,
$$
\int_F(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu=\psi(g_F)-\int_F\psi\,d\mu\le\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\Gamma c}.

Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$, $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2(d+1)]$, and $V=1/d!$. For a fixed continuous concave $\psi\ge0$ on $B$ and $\varepsilon>0$ put
$$
K_\varepsilon=\{(z,r):z\in B,\ \sum_jz_j-1\le r\le\varepsilon\psi(z)\}.
$$
This is a full-dimensional convex body, with $|K_\varepsilon|=V+\varepsilon dV\int_B\psi\,d\mu$. Let $\ell(z)=A+\sum_j B_jz_j$ be a fixed supporting affine majorant at the centroid of $B$. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the simplex $S_\varepsilon$ given by
$$
q\ge0,\qquad z_j\ge0,\qquad q+\sum_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)z_j\le1+\varepsilon A,\qquad q=r-\sum_jz_j+1
$$
encloses $K_\varepsilon$. It satisfies
$$
|S_\varepsilon|=\frac{V(1+\varepsilon A)^d}{\prod_j(1-\varepsilon B_j)},\qquad
1-\frac{|K_\varepsilon|}{|S_\varepsilon|}
=\varepsilon d\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu+O(\varepsilon^2).
$$
For a full-dimensional body $K$, write $D(K)$ for maximum ordinary halfspace depth with respect to normalized volume. With $E_d(\psi)=\int_B[\#\{i:s_i\ge1/m\}-m\Gamma]\psi\,d\mu$,
$$
D(K_\varepsilon)=\Gamma+\varepsilon\frac{d}{m}E_d(\psi)+o(\varepsilon).
$$
For each fixed nonaffine roof the denominator in the following limit has positive linear coefficient, and
$$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{D(K_\varepsilon)-\Gamma}{1-|K_\varepsilon|/|S_\varepsilon|}
=\frac{E_d(\psi)}{m\int_B(\ell-\psi)\,d\mu}
\ge\Gamma c.
$$
Equality in this limit is attained by $\psi=\min_i s_i$. If $\psi$ is affine, both linear terms vanish and the enclosing simplex formula still holds. The total variation distance of the two normalized uniform laws equals the displayed missing fraction, which therefore bounds their discrepancy over closed halfspaces. All error estimates are for the fixed roof and, where applicable, the fixed majorant.

86934b651b11f7d5:01.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Use planar area on each fiber. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and nonzero spanning vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Set $h_i=h_B(v_i)$, where $h_B(v)=\max_{x\in B}v\cdot x$, and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Assume each of the three closed ambient caps
$$
v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0
$$
attains the actual mixed depth at $(0,y)$, and cuts both $A$ and $K$ properly. The trace on $B$ is the supporting face $F_i=B\cap\{v_i\cdot x=h_i\}$. Let $a_i,k_i$ be the lengths of the $A,K$ cutting chords, respectively, divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $\lambda_i=1/(2a_i+k_i)$ and $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$.

Let $J$ be rotation through a right angle. Give the three cutting lines compatible coordinates by writing $x=y+r v_i/\lVert v_i\rVert^2+uJv_i$, using the appropriate constant $r$ on each line. Let $c_{A,i}$ and $c_i$ be the $u$-centers of the $A,K$ chords. Then $F_i$ contains a $u$-interval of length $a_i$ centered at $-c_{A,i}-(k_i/a_i)c_i$. In particular,
$$
k_i\ge a_i,\qquad
|c_i|\le \frac{a_i(k_i-a_i)}{k_i+2a_i}.
$$
For the single centrally symmetric body $(K-y)\cap(y-K)$, its Minkowski gauge $N$ satisfies
$$
2\lambda_i\le N(Jv_i)\le 6\lambda_i,\qquad
\lambda_i\le3\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j,\qquad
\frac{\lambda_i}{\Lambda}\le\frac34.
$$

86934b651b11f7d5:02.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body and let the finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ cover $A$ and cut it properly. Write $w_i>0$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$ and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. If $\sum_{i:x\in H_i}w_i\ge\tau$ almost everywhere on $A$, then every $p\in A$ satisfies
$$
\sum_i w_i\bigl[dU_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)\sigma_i\bigr]\ge d|A|\tau.
$$
If all singleton-capture regions with indices in a set $E$ are null, a valid $\tau$ is the minimum of the singleton weights $w_i$ for $i\notin E$ and all pair sums $w_i+w_j$ with $i\ne j$, taking the minimum over the combined nonempty list.

86934b651b11f7d5:03.statement:
Let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be convex bodies at the only integer bases $-1,0,1$, with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and nonzero spanning normals $v_i$ for $1\le i\le3$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. Put $h_i=h_B(v_i)$ and $b_i=2v_i\cdot y-h_i$. Suppose the caps $v_i\cdot(x-y)+(v_i\cdot y-h_i)z\ge0$ have common raw mass $Q$ and proper $A,K$ cuts. Write $a=|A|$, $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$, $U_i=|A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}|$, and $a_i,k_i$ for the $A,K$ chord lengths divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $s_i=2a_i+k_i$, $\lambda_i=1/s_i$, $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, and
$$
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i,\qquad
\overline L(p)=\frac{\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)}{\Lambda}.
$$

For every $p\in A$, contract $A$ to $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ and keep $K,B$ fixed. For all sufficiently small $t\ge0$ there is a $C^1$ meeting point $y(t)$ with $y(0)=y$ and a common cap budget $q(t)$ with $q(0)=Q$, obtained by substituting $y(t)$ for $y$ in the same three ambient caps. They cover the full middle plane, and $q'(0)=-\overline L(p)$. If $Q$ is the original global raw maximum and the two ordinary endpoint maxima are strictly below $Q$, the new global raw maximum is at most $q(t)$ for all sufficiently small $t\ge0$. Writing $M(t)=|A_t|+|K|+|B|$,
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{M(t)}\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{-M\overline L(p)+2aQ}{M^2}.
$$
In particular the optimized normalized depth strictly decreases if $\overline L(p)>2aQ/M$.

If the three original caps attain the true depth at $(0,y)$ and every singleton-capture region of the $A$ traces is null, then $\overline L(p)\ge a/2$ for every $p\in A$. The derivative above is then at most $(-Ma/2+2aQ)/M^2$. At a budget ratio $Q/M<2/9$ this last expression is less than $-a/(18M)$.

86934b651b11f7d5:05.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, let $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ for $1\le i\le3$ cover $A$, and assume the normals are pairwise linearly independent and all cuts are proper. Write $a=|A|$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$, $a_i=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i$. For arbitrary positive weights $\lambda_i$ put $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $\tau_2=\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i$, and $c_i=(\tau_2-\lambda_i)_+$. The region $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<b_j\}$ is the region captured only by $H_i$. For each $i$ with $r_i=|R_i|>0$, set $C_i=\overline{R_i}$ and, for $j\ne i$, let $\ell$ be the third index and put
$$
\tau_{ij}=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j,\ v_\ell\cdot x\le b_\ell\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert}.
$$
Then $C_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x\le b_j\}$. For every $p\in A$ and $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ the exact right loss is
$$
D_i(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{|R_i\setminus A_t|}{t}
=2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}(b_j-v_j\cdot p)\tau_{ij}\ge0.
$$
It satisfies $D_i(p)\le2r_i$ on $C_i$ and its minimum there is attained and equals
$$
2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
-h_{C_i}\Bigl(-\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr),
$$
where $h_C$ is the support function of $C$.

With null corners omitted, for every $p\in A$,
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-\sum_i c_iD_i(p).
$$
The right side attains its maximum at one common $p\in A$, with value
$$
2a\tau_2-2\sum_i c_ir_i+\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
+h_A\Bigl(-\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr).
$$
If just one positive-area corner $R_j$ has $c_j>0$, every $p\in C_j$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-2(\tau_2-\lambda_j)r_j$. If all deficient corners are null, $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge2a\tau_2$ for every $p\in A$.

In the actual mixed setting of the critical chord-weight theorem, these one-corner and all-deficient-null estimates imply a normalized loss of at least $(a-r_j)/2$ and $a/2$, respectively, after dividing by $\Lambda$. In particular $r_j\le a/9$ gives a normalized loss of at least $4a/9$ at every $p\in C_j$.

86dd5366456916a8:04.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty and let each $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. Assume $\sum_{p\in P}\lambda_p K_p\subseteq K_z$ for every convex combination with $\sum_p\lambda_p p=z\in P$. Put $B=\operatorname{conv}P$, $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and let $\mu=\sum_{p\in P}\delta_p\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_p}\,dx)$ have total mass $M$. Write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Work relative to $\operatorname{aff}B$ in the base. Let $f:C\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave, positive on each own-fiber interior and zero on each own-fiber boundary.

For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define $b_\varepsilon(z,x)$ as the minimum of the closed pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(z)$ for the atomic masses $|K_p|$ and the infimum over all base vectors $a$ and unit $u\in\mathbb R^d$ of $\mu\{a\cdot Z+u\cdot X\ge a\cdot z+u\cdot x-\varepsilon f(z,x)\}$. In base rank zero put $b_{\rm base}=M$. In particular $b_0$ is the original closed mixed depth. For $0<q\le M$ set $c_q(a,u)=\sup\{c:\mu\{a\cdot Z+u\cdot X\ge c\}\ge q\}$. Then the exact buffered region is the compact convex set
$$
D_{q,\varepsilon}
=\{(z,x)\in C:b_{\rm base}(z)\ge q,\
 a\cdot z+u\cdot x-\varepsilon f(z,x)\le c_q(a,u)\ \text{for every }a,\ \|u\|=1\}.
$$
For fixed $q$, the quantile changes by at most $\sup_S|(a-a')\cdot Z+(u-u')\cdot X|$ under replacement of $(a,u)$ by $(a',u')$.

With $L=\sum_{p\in P}\sup_{\|u\|=1,s\in\mathbb R}\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_p\cap\{u\cdot X=s\})$, one has $0\le b_\varepsilon(w)-b_0(w)\le\varepsilon Lf(w)$ throughout $C$. The maxima $Q_\varepsilon=\max_S b_\varepsilon$ are attained and $0<Q_0\le Q_\varepsilon\le Q_0+\varepsilon L\max_C f$. Every cluster point of maximizing marks as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ attains $Q_0$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, all maximizing $(p,y)$ stay a uniformly positive distance from $\partial K_p$ and all shifted own thresholds $u\cdot y-\varepsilon f(p,y)$ stay uniformly between the two support levels.

Admissible buffers include $E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ and $E_{C_z}(x)^{1/(d+1)}$, each extended by zero at own-fiber boundary marks, with $E$ the projective energy of fact d90ba05577427854.

9158d8d941246660:03.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite complete affine-lattice base with positive compatible convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $d\ge1$, canonical hull $C$ and summed mixed volume $dm$ of mass $M$. Compatibility means $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_zz=p\in P$ is a convex combination. Write $C_z$ for the fiber of $C$ at any real base $z$ and $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ for the pooled within-fiber covariance norm. Let $L>0$ be a finite minimum of affine functions on a neighborhood of $C$, with $\int\log L\,dm=0$. Put $N=d+1$ and $f(z,x)=(L(z,x) E_{C_z}(x)/M)^{1/N}$, using zero own-boundary projective energy. The profile is continuous and jointly concave on $C$, strictly concave on own interiors and positive precisely there. For an own-interior sampled mark $Y=(p,y)$, let $F=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ and $a_E$ be the minimizing projective parameter at $Y$. Every own supergradient of $f$ at $Y$ is $g=f(Y)a_E+f(Y)c/(NL(Y))$ for an own slope $c$ of a convex combination of the active affine $L$-planes. If $\alpha_L$ is the base slope of that combination and $(\alpha_F,\nabla_x F(Y))$ a full supergradient of $F$, then $(\alpha,g)$ is a full supergradient of $f$, with $\alpha=f(Y)\alpha_L/(NL(Y))+d f(Y)\alpha_F/(NF(Y))$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and define buffered cap depth using threshold $a\cdot p+u\cdot y-\varepsilon\Gamma(u)f(p,y)$ for nonzero $u$ and unchanged closed pure-base caps. Let $Q$ be the maximum raw depth on sampled fibers and $I$ its deepest bases. Assume every deepest mark has own-interior distance $>\varepsilon f(Y)\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)}$. Then $I$ is lattice-complete and admits a covering by at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ groups, with $k$ counting inherited parities. For each group $i$ there is an inclusion-maximal face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ among those with a sampled point in their relative interior. Assign it the finite set $J_i=I\cap F_i$, allowing overlaps. There are at most $d+1$ actual mass-$Q$ caps $N_{ij}\cdot w\ge c_{ij}$ in each group, with $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, right $Q$-quantile thresholds and positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ summing to one. Put $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. The margin $\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot w-h_i-\varepsilon f(w)$ is nonnegative throughout every whole real fiber over $F_i$. On each sampled assigned fiber it has exactly one zero, at the own-interior deepest mark, where all selected quantiles are active.

Now move the compatible positive fibers on the same bases by $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance. Let $L_t$ be positive on the new hull, continuous there, and converge to $L$ on matched sampled marks uniformly. Let $N_{ij}(t)\to N_{ij}$ and $\varepsilon(t)\to\varepsilon$ be the current normals and scale, use the actual updated mass and covariance, and put $f_t=(L_t E_t/M_t)^{1/N}$ and $A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}(t))$. \alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}\left[\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}(t)\cdot(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon(t)A_i(t)f_t(z,x)\right].

91db436274c254e2:01.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact mixed-integer convex body with intrinsic mixed measure $\mu$. Let $L_i(z,x)=\beta_i+b_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x$ be finitely many affine scores, with $\mu$-null pairwise ties and positive-mass winner cells $D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{k\ne i}\{L_i\ge L_k\}$. $$
\Delta_{ki}=L_k(y_k)-L_i(y_k)=t_k^{-1}\int_{D_k}(L_k-L_i)\,d\mu>0\quad(k\ne i).
$$
For every nonnegative off-diagonal circulation $\alpha$ (its row and column sums agree label by label),
$$
\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\ell_i(y_k)=-\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}.
$$
Consequently the relation $i\to k$ for $i\ne k$ and $\ell_i(y_k)\ge0$ is acyclic. For arbitrary centered margins $h_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot(z-j_i)+v_i\cdot(x-c_i)$ the corresponding identity is
$$
\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}h_i(y_k)=
-\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}
+\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\big[(a_i-b_i)\cdot(j_k-j_i)+(v_i-u_i)\cdot(c_k-c_i)\big].
$$
In particular, if $v_i=u_i$, $\alpha\ne0$ and every positive-weight edge captures its destination, the base correction is at least $\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}\Delta_{ki}>0$. For finite families $h_{ir}$ of such margins with weights $\rho_{ir}\ge0$, $\sum_r\rho_{ir}=1$ and $\sum_r\rho_{ir}v_{ir}=0$, the averaged circulation is exactly $\sum_{i,k}\alpha_{ik}(\sum_r\rho_{ir}a_{ir})\cdot(j_k-j_i)$.

More locally, its density ceiling over a given $(u,p)$ is the number of classes having positive conditional endpoint bases $z,w$ in that class with $z+w=2p$ and $h_{K_z}(u)+h_{K_w}(u)=2h_{K_p}(u)$. The uniform factor $2^n$ is sharp.

97b12ef4ecc6c56e:01.statement:
Let $C=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(3,0),(3,3),(2,10),(0,2)\}$. Its integer fibers are $[0,2],[0,6],[0,10],[0,3]$ and its total mixed length is $21$. For $0<t\le1$, enlarge just the middle fiber to $[0,6+t]$ and take the corresponding hull $D_t$. Then $D_t\subseteq C$ has exactly these three integer fibers, mass $12+t$, and true centroid $(2,c_t)$ with $c_t=3+(3t+t^2/2)/(12+t)$. 97eab0f821e54041:01.reason: Only finitely many nontrivial extreme barycentric rows need be checked. Their strict support gaps survive a common small fiberwise Hausdorff change, and the exact integer hull reconstruction follows.
97eab0f821e54041:01.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$ be integers. Let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, with $\operatorname{aff}(P)=\mathbb R^n$, and let $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$, $p\in P$, be compact convex bodies with nonempty interior. For each $q\in P$, let
$$
E_q=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{P\setminus\{q\}}:\quad
\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p=1,\quad \sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p p=q\right\}.
$$
Call the family strictly compatible if for each extreme point $\lambda$ of each nonempty $E_q$, the Minkowski combination $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p$ is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}K_q$. Under this condition there is a common $\kappa>0$ such that $\sum_{p\ne q}\lambda_p K_p+\kappa B_d\subseteq K_q$ for every such extreme point, where $B_d$ is the closed unit ball. For any family of convex bodies $K'_p$ with $d_H(K'_p,K_p)<\eta<\kappa/2$ for all $p$, the convex hull of the lifted bodies $\{p\}\times K'_p$ has exactly the prescribed integer fibers $K'_p$ at $p\in P$. In particular the original family is actual.

97eab0f821e54041:02.reason: Strict exposure and unique own support localize the exact hull additions and cuts in any prescribed neighborhood, with continuous strictly positive volume functions.
97eab0f821e54041:02.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Let $v\in\partial K$ have a unique outward unit supporting normal $u$, with $K\cap\{x:u\cdot x=h_K(u)\}=\{v\}$. Fix $h$ with $u\cdot h>0$. Then $K(t)=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{v+th\})$ has added volume $\Delta(t)=|K(t)|-|K|>0$ for $t>0$. The function $\Delta$ is continuous and strictly increasing, with $\Delta(0)=0$, and $\sup_{x\in K(t)\setminus K}\lVert x-v\rVert\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$. In particular each sufficiently small prescribed positive added volume has a unique small positive parameter.

For a finite list of distinct points $v_i$ with these hypotheses and corresponding directions $h_i$, write $a_i=v_i+t_i h_i$. For all sufficiently small positive $t_i$ one has the exact disjoint union
$$
\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i:i\})\setminus K
=\bigsqcup_i\bigl(\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{a_i\})\setminus K\bigr).
$$

97eab0f821e54041:03.reason: Disjoint neighborhoods let the exact positive and negative volume changes be tuned independently. Small Hausdorff changes preserve all strict rows and hence the full actual integer census.
97eab0f821e54041:03.statement:
Let $P$, $K_p$, and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ satisfy the strict compatibility hypotheses of the open compatibility lemma. Let $\mu_C$ be summed $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on its integer fibers and $M=\mu_C(\mathbb R^{n+d})$. Choose finitely many distinct $w_i=(p_i,v_i)$, $p_i\in P$, each exposed in $C$ by an ambient linear functional with unique maximizer $w_i$. Assume $v_i$ has a unique unit supporting normal $u_i$ in $K_{p_i}$, whose support face is $\{v_i\}$, and fix $h_i$ with $u_i\cdot h_i>0$. For each fixed real vector $\xi=(\xi_i)$ and every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual convex body $C_\varepsilon$ with nonempty integer fibers of positive volume exactly at $P$, converging fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to $C$. The signed measure $\mu_{C_\varepsilon}-\mu_C$ is a sum of signed restrictions of mixed volume to pairwise disjoint regions shrinking to the respective $w_i$, each of exact signed mass $\varepsilon\xi_i$. In particular $M_\varepsilon=M+\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i$. For every fixed finite family of closed halfspaces $H$ whose boundaries avoid all $w_i$, one has
$$
\mu_{C_\varepsilon}(H)-\mu_C(H)=\varepsilon\sum_i\xi_i\mathbf1_H(w_i)
$$
for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. The same identity holds for parallel threshold changes of order $O(\varepsilon)$, comparing the two measures at the same shifted threshold and keeping the old indicators on the right.

97eab0f821e54041:04.reason: Use one regular positive circuit per deepest base and strict-budget covers elsewhere. The two-sided slopes of each selected cap match, so the signed threshold shifts give the stated upper derivative and one dual on every finite feasible sample set.
97eab0f821e54041:04.statement:
In the setting of the exact signed local mass theorem, write $D(C)$ for the maximum over the measured set of the infimum of normalized $\mu_C$-mass of closed ambient halfspaces containing the point. Put $\beta=D(C)$, $Q=\beta M$, and let $I$ be the bases attaining this deepest value. At each $p\in I$ choose a finite positive circuit of actual caps
$$
H_{pj}=\{(z,x):a_{pj}\cdot z+u_{pj}\cdot x\ge b_{pj}\},\qquad
\lVert u_{pj}\rVert=1,\qquad \sum_j\rho_{pj}u_{pj}=0,\quad \rho_{pj}>0,
$$
through one maximizing mark in that fiber. Assume every selected cap has old mass $Q$, its boundary avoids every selected $w_i$, and its old threshold function satisfies $F_{pj}(b_{pj}+s)=Q-S_{pj}s+o(|s|)$ with $S_{pj}>0$. In particular this expansion is two-sided and uses the full mixed measure. Define $\kappa_{pj}=(\rho_{pj}/S_{pj})/\sum_\ell(\rho_{p\ell}/S_{p\ell})$ and $A_{pi}=\sum_j\kappa_{pj}\mathbf1_{H_{pj}}(w_i)$. For every fixed real vector $\xi$, the exact signed mass competitors satisfy
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\frac{D(C_\varepsilon)-\beta}{\varepsilon}
\le \frac1M\max_{p\in I}\sum_i\xi_i(A_{pi}-\beta).
$$
If $C$ is a local minimum among all actual positive fiber families over $P$, with the fiberwise Hausdorff topology, there is a probability vector $\pi$ on the selected deepest-base circuits such that $\sum_{p\in I}\pi_p A_{pi}=\beta$ for every selected $i$. This holds for every permitted finite selection of points and one circuit per deepest base. The probability vector is attached to that selection. When $I$ has one base, the corresponding score itself equals $\beta$ at each selected point.

97eab0f821e54041:05.reason: The complete cylinder census leaves exactly the specified origin-layer addition and the base-one share. Brunn–Minkowski gives the positive remote share and planar Steiner yields the exact base-one fraction.
97eab0f821e54041:05.statement: For every pair of integers $n\ge1$, $d\ge2$, let $C=[0,2]\times[0,1]^{n-1}\times B_d$, where $B_d$ is the unit Euclidean ball and $V=|B_d|$. Set $w=(0,e_1)$ and $w_t=(0,(1+t)e_1)$, with $0$ the all-zero base and $t>0$, and let $C_t=\operatorname{conv}(C\cup\{w_t\})$. All original integer fibers are smooth strictly convex balls and $w$ is exposed in $C$. In the all-zero binary layer the actual new fibers at first coordinates $0,1,2$ are $K(t)$, $(K(t)+B_d)/2$, and $B_d$, where $K(t)=\operatorname{conv}(B_d\cup\{(1+t)e_1\})$. All other integer fibers are unchanged. Write $\Delta_0=|K(t)|-V>0$ and $\Delta_1=|(K(t)+B_d)/2|-V$. Then $2^{-d}\Delta_0\le\Delta_1\le\Delta_0$. Thus at least $1/(2^d+1)$ of all added mixed mass lies at distance at least one from $w$, although the entire base-zero addition approaches $w$ as $t\downarrow0$. The normalized added mixed measures cannot converge weakly to the unit point mass at $w$. In dimension $d=2$ the proportion of all added mass in the first-coordinate-one fiber is $\Delta_1/(\Delta_0+\Delta_1)=3/7$ for every $t>0$. The original family and, when $\Delta_0<V/4$, the perturbed family have every fiber mass strictly less than their respective total mixed mass divided by $2^n$.

97eab0f821e54041:06.statement: For the ball-cylinder example of §5 with d=2 and every t>0, set a=1+t, θ=arccos(1/a), s=√(a²−1). Then Δ_0=s−θ, perimeter(K(t))=2π+2Δ_0, and Δ_1=3Δ_0/4. Thus the exact proportion of all added mixed mass in the fiber at base (1,0,…,0) is 3/7.

98181ddbde71e951:01.reason: The shallow positive-volume cap of K at an exposed point fits in its cell, and a sufficiently close P_j has its corresponding cap in that same cell. The volume excess tends to zero, so continuity of the cut-volume function gives the exact truncation. Removed caps are in distinct open cells. For Hausdorff control, fix a point in int K and an inner homothetic copy of K about that point. In each of the finitely many chosen directions its support is strictly below that of K. Choose every shallow cap threshold above the corresponding inner support so that the copy survives the correction. Such copies tend to K as their ratios approach one.
98181ddbde71e951:01.statement: Let K⊂R^d be a convex body, d≥1, and let a finite hyperplane arrangement have open full-dimensional cells R. Let P_j be circumscribed polytopes tending to K in Hausdorff distance and already matching K's volume in each cell except a fixed finite list R_i. If every R_i contains an exposed point of K, then, for all sufficiently large j, at most one truncation per R_i corrects every cell volume exactly. The corrected polytopes can be chosen to tend to K in Hausdorff distance.

Each wall contributes at most two such points, so this clipped body is a polygon. Its non-wall facets are genuine supports of K and can be imposed on the circumscribed approximation to fix the whole cell. Empty cells are fixed by separation, and interior cells are already exact. The exposed-cell correction from §2 handles the rest, and the lines themselves have area zero. Accepted 2021348e0b2d8c9f uses ordinary Hausdorff polygonal approximation in its mixed-area proof; that gives convergence of relevant areas, without the exact finite measurements or the independent corrections.
98181ddbde71e951:02.statement: For every planar convex body K, every finite list of closed halfplanes H_i, and every ε>0, there is a planar convex polygon Q at Hausdorff distance less than ε from K with area(Q∩R)=area(K∩R) for every open full-dimensional cell R of the arrangement of ∂H_i. Consequently area(Q)=area(K) and area(Q∩H_i)=area(K∩H_i) for every i.

If finitely many fixed closed halfplanes cover R² and each has intersection area at most v with K, then K has arbitrarily close polygonal replacements of area T with the same minimum raw maximum depth v and the same recorded cap areas.

a0a4e151af2d0678:01.statement:
Let $K_w(p)\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite actual family of positive compact convex fibers at fixed bases $w\in P$, parametrized on an open neighborhood of $p_0$ (which can be an open coordinate chart of a feasible equality family). Write $\mu_p$ for the sum of their fiber Lebesgue measures and $M(p)>0$ for its total mass. Fix a positive circuit of actual closed caps $H_j(b)=\{(w,x):v_j\cdot w+u_j\cdot x\ge b\}$ through an old interior mark at base $z$, each with the same old raw mass $\tau_0$. The fixed weights satisfy $\sum_j\rho_j=1$, $\sum_j\rho_ju_j=0$, and $A=\sum_j\rho_jv_j$. Assume $F_j(p,b)=\mu_p(H_j(b))$ and $M(p)$ are $C^2$ near the old data and $S_j=-\partial_bF_j(p_0,b_j)>0$.

The actual common-mass thresholds $b_j(p)$ and mass $\tau_c(p)$ solving $F_j(p,b_j(p))=\tau_c(p)$ and $\sum_j\rho_jb_j(p)=A\cdot z$ are locally unique and $C^2$. The caps cover every continuous plane over $A\cdot w\ge A\cdot z$. At the old parameter in direction $\delta$, put $B_j=\partial_pF_j[\delta]$, $\theta_j=(\rho_j/S_j)/\sum_k(\rho_k/S_k)$, $a=\sum_j\theta_jB_j$ and $v'_j=(B_j-a)/S_j$. Then
$$
D\tau_c[\delta]=a,\qquad Db_j[\delta]=v'_j,\qquad
D^2\tau_c[\delta,\delta]=\sum_j\theta_j\bigl(\partial_{pp}F_j[\delta,\delta]+2\partial_{pb}F_j[\delta]v'_j+\partial_{bb}F_j(v'_j)^2\bigr).
$$
For $f_c=\tau_c/M$ with $f_c(p_0)=\beta$, on $\ker Df_c(p_0)$ one has $D^2 f_c[\delta,\delta]=(D^2\tau_c[\delta,\delta]-\beta D^2M[\delta,\delta])/M(p_0)$.

V_{k,m,p}=X_k+pE_+-E_--bY_m,\qquad

$$
The variance of $V_{k,m,p}$ is $\sigma^2=k+p^2+1+mb^2$ and lies in $[k+1,2(k+1)]$. As $k\to\infty$, the probability $\Pr(V_{k,m,p}\ge0)$ tends to $1/2$ uniformly over the admissible $m,p$. a5bd7e36a76479fe:01.statement:
Let $(Z,X)$ have the probability law of normalized summed volume on finitely many compact, positive full-dimensional fibers in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Put $V=\operatorname{Cov}(Z)$ and choose $B$ satisfying $BV=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Z)$. The regression residual $R=X-\mathbb E X-B(Z-\mathbb E Z)$ exists, is independent of the choice of $B$ almost surely, and has positive definite covariance $\Sigma$. Under $z'=Uz+h$, $x'=Ax+Dz+e$ with $U$ integral unimodular, $h$ integral and $A$ invertible, $\Sigma'=A\Sigma A^\top$. An unchanged affine cap margin $L=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ then has
$$
u'=A^{-\top}u,\qquad a'=U^{-\top}(a-D^\top u'),\qquad
b'=b+a'\cdot h+u'\cdot e .
$$
Thus $u^\top\Sigma u$ is invariant. The raw cap masses and hinges scale by $\Delta=|\det A|$ and normalized cap budgets are invariant.

For a fixed source, use the actual hinge cover and Fritz–John conditions of c343c9f3dc96957e with the constraint $u_i^\top\Sigma u_i=1$ in place of the Euclidean sphere. Write $(c_i,P_i,m_i)$ for the cap mass and base and continuous moments, $(S_i,P_i^s,m_i^s)$ for the effective section moments, and $q_{zi}=\lambda_{zi}x_z$ for the weighted contact moment on a positive coverage multiplier $\eta_z$. The two mass and base balances are unchanged, and the continuous balance becomes
$$
\alpha_0m_i+r_im_i^s-\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}
=\alpha_0\Psi_i\Sigma u_i,\qquad
\Psi_i=\int(L_i)_+\,d\mu .
$$
Here the effective section moments integrate $(1,z,x)$ with the same density $\theta_{iz}/\lVert u_i\rVert_2$ on each section, with $\theta_{iz}=1$ on proper sections and $0\le\theta_{iz}\le1$ on supporting sections. The sphere multiplier for $(u_i^\top\Sigma u_i-1)/2$ is $-\alpha_0\Psi_i$. The identity also holds for integrated moments of saddle pairs supported on the zero margin wherever weighted.

a5bd7e36a76479fe:04.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a positive $d$-simplex, $d\ge1$, with volume $v$, centroid $g$ and uniform covariance $\Sigma_K$. Put $S=\{0,1\}^n\times K$ for $n\ge0$, with summed mass $M=2^nv$. Among covers by $2^n(d+1)$ closed caps with continuous normals normalized by the residual covariance, the minimum feasible normalized cap-mass budget is $\gamma_d/2^n$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Isolated canonical centroid caps give a normal hinge stress at that budget with objective multiplier one and all budget multipliers zero. The total hinge at that cover is $M\gamma_d\sqrt{d(d+2)}$.

More generally consider any canonical centroid vertex cap of a simplex fiber, with barycentric gradient $\beta_i$ and centered vertex $w_i$. Suppose its positively weighted contacts lie at the own centroid and the cap has zero actual mass on all other fibers, with zero multiplied section moments from those fibers. Under any fixed positive definite normalization $\Sigma$, the remaining continuous cap balance for a positive objective multiplier requires
$$
\frac{w_i}{d+1}
=\frac{d\,\Sigma\beta_i}{(d+1)^2\,\beta_i^\top\Sigma\beta_i}.
$$
The displayed compatibility holds for all $d+1$ types exactly when $\Sigma$ is a positive scalar multiple of $\Sigma_K$.

a5d3d44181ebed82:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, and let a strictly positive row $x$ have a proper minimizing threshold for the uniform-simplex capacity $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0}t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$, where $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$. Rescale the row and threshold so that this threshold equals $1$. Write $\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$, $c=\mathbf 1-x$, $V=\sum_jc_jE_j$ for independent unit exponentials, $P=P(c)=\Pr(V\ge0)$, $g=\nabla P(c)$, and $H=\nabla^2P(c)$. Set $\eta=H\mathbf 1$, $B=d(d-1)P-\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}H\mathbf 1$, and $K=P^{-1/d}/(dP)$. Then the minimizing section strictly captures at least two vertices, $\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}g=dP$, and
$$
B=d(d-1)[P+f_V'(0)]>0 .
$$
The capacity is locally $C^2$ and
$$
\nabla^2\phi_d(x)
=K\left[\frac{d+1}{dP}gg^\mathsf{T}-H-\frac{(\eta-dg)(\eta-dg)^\mathsf{T}}{B}\right].
$$
In particular, for $g\cdot v=0$ and any real $s$,
$$
(v+s\mathbf 1)^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2\phi_d(x)(v+s\mathbf 1)
=-K\left[v^\mathsf{T}Hv+\frac{(\eta\cdot v-sdP)^2}{B}\right].
$$

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:01.statement:
Let $N_i$ be finitely many independent geometric random variables on the nonnegative integers, with means $b_i\ge0$ and at least one $b_i>0$. A zero mean denotes a deterministic zero variable. Write $N=\sum_i N_i$, $\mu=\sum_i b_i$, $b_{\max}=\max_i b_i$, $p(n)=\Pr(N=n)$, $m_i(n)=\mathbb E[N_i\mid N=n]$, and $\tau(n)=\sum_i b_i(m_i(n)+1)$. Then $p(n)>0$ for $n\ge0$, and for every integer $n\ge1$ the increments $m_i(n)-m_i(n-1)$ belong to $[0,1]$ and sum to one. They are positive for each $i$ with $b_i>0$. The recurrence is
$$
\tau(n-1)p(n-1)=[\tau(n)+n-\mu]p(n).
$$
In particular, $p(n)\ge p(n-1)$ for $1\le n\le\mu-b_{\max}$. In this range equality holds exactly when $n=\mu-b_{\max}$ and all the positive means are equal.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:02.reason: Tilting the negative phases gives a sum of independent geometric counts. The mode comparison supplies the derivative sign and the exact equality case.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:02.statement: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $X$ have the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law, and let $Y=\sum_i b_iE_i$ for finitely many unit-mean exponentials $E_i$, independent of each other and of $X$. Assume $0\le b_i\le1$ and $\sum_i b_i\ge k$. The continuous convolution density $f$ of $X-Y$ is differentiable at zero and satisfies $f'(0)\le0$. Equality holds exactly when $k$ of the $b_i$ equal one and all others equal zero.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:03.reason: A signed size-biased derivative and the augmented gamma-density sign make every nontrivial capped residual equalization strictly decrease the probability.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:03.statement:
Let $k\ge2$ and $q\ge k-1$ be integers. For $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\in[0,1]^q$ with $\sum_i b_i=k-1$, let
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Set $\bar b=(k-1)/q$. Transferring a positive amount from an above-average coefficient to a below-average one, up to the first point at which either reaches $\bar b$, strictly decreases $P_k$. Consequently
$$
P_k(b)\ge \Pr(X\ge E_0+\bar b\,G),
$$
where $G$ is an independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)$ variable. Equality holds exactly when every $b_i=\bar b$.

a6e6fd61fe60c16a:04.reason: Zero padding and strict finite-count equalization give decreasing exact minima. The equalized gamma average converges to its deterministic mean, giving the stated exponential polynomial limit.
a6e6fd61fe60c16a:04.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Consider the laws
$$
P_k(b)=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\sum_{i=1}^q b_iE_i\right),
\qquad 0\le b_i\le1,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^q b_i=k-1,
$$
where $X$ has the $\operatorname{Gamma}(k,1)$ law and $E_0,\ldots,E_q$ are unit-mean exponentials, with all variables independent. Here $q$ ranges over the finite nonnegative integers for which the coefficient constraints are feasible. For $k\ge2$, the fixed-$q$ minimum is
$$
A_{k,q}=\Pr\!\left(X\ge E_0+\frac{k-1}{q}\,G\right),
\qquad G\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(q,1)
$$
with $G$ independent. These minima strictly decrease as $q$ increases and converge to
$$
G_k=\Pr(X\ge E_0+k-1)
=e^{-(k-1)}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{(k-1)^j}{j!}\left(1-2^{-(k-j)}\right).
$$
Thus the infimum over all finite $q$ and all feasible $b$ is $G_k$, and $P_k(b)>G_k$ for every such $b$ when $k\ge2$. In particular $G_2=5/(4e)$ and $G_3=27/(8e^2)$. When $k=1$ every residual coefficient is zero, and $P_1(b)=G_1=1/2$, including the empty list.

a754d14c81eb6c11:01.statement:
Let a planar compact convex body have exactly $N$ nonempty sampled integer fibers, at consecutive sites. Suppose all have positive length, with affine midpoint heights and affine widths. Use the sum of fiber lengths as mass, and closed ambient halfspaces for depth. Subtract the affine center graph, reverse the base when needed, and for a nonconstant width profile divide by its positive increment. Write the resulting lengths as $w_i=q+i$ for $0\le i<N$, with $q>0$. At base $j$ the midpoint attains the largest raw depth in its interval, namely
$$
D_j(q)=\min\left\{\sum_{i<j}w_i+w_j/2,\ \sum_{i>j}w_i+w_j/2,\ T_{j,k}(q)\ (k\ne j)\right\},
$$
where every sum uses $0,\ldots,N-1$ and
$$
T_{j,k}(q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i<k}\min\{q+i,(k-i)(q+j)/(2(k-j))\},&k>j,\\
\displaystyle\sum_{i>k}\min\{q+i,(i-k)(q+j)/(2(j-k))\},&k<j.
\end{cases}
$$
Each $D_j$ is concave and piecewise affine with rational coefficients. The normalized maximum $\max_j D_j/[Nq+N(N-1)/2]$ is piecewise linear-fractional with finitely many rational breakpoints and is monotone or constant on each piece. For constant positive widths the normalized maximum is $1/2$ for odd $N$ and $(N-1)/(2N)$ for even $N$.

a779c844eb8df3e4:02.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb R^r$, $r\ge1$, be a full-rank lattice of covolume $v$. Let $f\colon\mathbb R^r\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded and measurable with compact support and convex strict superlevels $\{f>t\}$ for all $t>0$. Put $T=\sum_{p\in a+L}f(p)>0$ and $M=\int_{\mathbb R^r}f$. There is an affine hyperplane $E$ spanned by $r$ affinely independent coset points such that
$$
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)\le r!M/v,\qquad
\sum_{p\in(a+L)\cap E}f(p)\ge (T-r!M/v)_+,
$$
where $x_+=\max(x,0)$. If the positive sample set has full affine rank, take $E$ from the greedy rule which repeatedly chooses a highest-valued sample outside the previously selected affine span, starting with a highest-valued sample and stopping at $r$ points. For $b=\max_{p\in(a+L)\setminus E}f(p)>0$ the same $E$ satisfies
$$
M\ge \frac{v}{r!}\left[\sum_{p\in a+L}\min(f(p),b)-rb\right].
$$
If the positive sample set has smaller rank, one can choose $E$ containing all positive samples.

For a compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$, $s\ge1$, these conclusions apply to $f(u)=\operatorname{vol}_s(Q_u)$ with $M=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q)$, provided $T>0$. They apply separately to each closed halfspace intersection of $Q$ with positive sampled mass. In the counting case $s=0$, take $f=\mathbf 1_Q$ for compact convex $Q\subset\mathbb R^r$. The coefficient $r!$ in the outside-mass bound is sharp for every $r\ge1$ and $s\ge0$, including full-dimensional bodies whose nonempty sampled fibers all have positive mass.

a779c844eb8df3e4:05.statement:
Let $k\ge0$ and $r,s\ge1$ be integers, let $C\subset\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, and sample at $(z,u)\in\mathbb Z^k\times(a+L)$, where $L$ has full rank and covolume $v$ in $\mathbb R^r$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^k$ let $Q_z=\{(u,x):(z,u,x)\in C\}$, $T_z=\sum_{u\in a+L}\operatorname{vol}_s((Q_z)_u)$, and $M_z=\operatorname{vol}_{r+s}(Q_z)$. Put $T=\sum_z T_z>0$ and $M=\sum_z M_z$ over all coarse integer slices. Let $J\ge1$ be any upper bound on the number of coarse levels with $T_z>0$.

Assume for each $1\le t\le r-1$ that every full-dimensional compact convex body in $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ with positive sampled mass on $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$ has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then $C$ has a sampled point for which every containing closed halfspace has sampled mass, divided by $T$, at least
$$
\frac{\Gamma_s}{J\,2^{r-1}}\left(1-\frac{r!M}{vT}\right)_+.
$$
In particular $J\le2^k$ and $M/(vT)\le1/(2r!)$ imply normalized depth at least $\Gamma_s/2^{k+r}$. For $k=0$ take $J=1$ to obtain the one-level estimate. For $r=1$ all these conclusions are unconditional, and the point can be chosen as the centroid of an actual largest-volume sampled fiber of $C$.

a779c844eb8df3e4:06.statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, with $s\ge1$, and let $a+L$ be a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$. Let $F\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be an affine subspace. Take $P$ to consist of either all the lattice bases in $F$ with nonempty $Q$-fibers or all the lattice bases in $F$ with positive $s$-volume $Q$-fibers. Assume the sum $T_P$ of the retained fiber volumes is positive. Put $A=\operatorname{aff}P$, $t=\dim A$, and
$$
Q_P=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times Q_p).
$$
For every $p\in(a+L)\cap A$ the fiber $(Q_P)_p$ equals $Q_p$ if $p\in P$ and is empty otherwise. The hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body in $A\times\mathbb R^s$. For any $p_0\in P$, the lattice there is $p_0+(L\cap(A-p_0))$, whose difference lattice is saturated in $L$ and has rank $t$. A lattice basis gives an affine identification with $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ and sample lattice $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$, preserving every fiber volume and the raw halfspace depth within the retained source. For every retained candidate, its raw depth in the original source is at least its retained raw depth. The same comparison holds if $Q$ is a fixed coarse slice of a larger original source.

For $t>0$, assume the sharp mixed-integer bound in dimensions $(t,s)$, namely that every full-dimensional compact convex body of positive sampled mass in those dimensions has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then some retained point has raw depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s T_P$ in the original source. At $t=0$ the same conclusion holds unconditionally.

$$
For the two sums only, entries off the given index interval are zero.

Let $h\in\mathbb Z$, $m>0$, and let $(a_i)_{i\le h}$ be finitely supported with $0\le a_i\le m$ and total mass $A$. Write $A=qm+u$ with $q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $0\le u<m$. The largest possible first moment for these $h,m,A$ is
$$
hA-\frac{mq(q-1)}2-qu
=hA-\frac{A^2}{2m}+\frac A2-\frac{u(m-u)}{2m}.
$$
It is attained by putting mass $m$ at $h,h-1,\ldots,h-q+1$, mass $u$ at $h-q$, and zero elsewhere. In particular the first moment is at most $hA-A^2/(2m)+A/2$.

ad88f967d6335089:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, $d\ge2$, and let $P$ be all its nonempty integer-fiber bases. Assume each fiber is full-dimensional and an ambient cap through $(z_0,x_0)$, $z_0\in P$, with continuous normal $u\ne0$, cuts every fiber properly. Suppose its raw mass is a local minimum under variation of the real base-normal coefficient with $u$ fixed. If its actual captured fibers are $K_z=a_zD+v_z$ with $|D|_d=1$ and $a_z>0$, then $\sum_{z\in P}a_z^{d-1}(z-z_0)=0$, so $z_0\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$.

If the roots are affine on $P$, write $a_0=a_{z_0}$, $N=|P|$, $B=\sum_za_z^d$, $E=\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$, and let $\ell\in E$ satisfy $a_z=a_0+\ell\cdot(z-z_0)$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
B&=a_0\sum_z a_z^{d-1}\le Na_0^d,\\
Na_0^d-B
&=\sum_z(a_0-a_z)^2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)a_0^{d-2-j}a_z^j.
\end{aligned}
$$
Equality holds exactly when all $a_z=a_0$. The slope $\ell$ is the unique minimizer of $\sum_z[a_0+\eta\cdot(z-z_0)]^d$ over $\eta\in E$ with all roots positive, and a minimizer over the closure with all roots nonnegative. For the actual whole-fiber roots $r_z=|C_z|_d^{1/d}$, one has the first-moment bound $\sum_z(a_z^d/B)(r_z/a_z)\le r_{z_0}/a_0$.

If the original cap is locally minimizing under joint variation of the base and continuous normal and both $a_z$ and $v_z$ are affine on $P$, then $x_0$ is the ordinary centroid of its own cutting section.

ad88f967d6335089:03.reason: The finite linear equation $\Sigma\ell=\alpha(z_0-\bar z)$ gives the explicit positive admissibility region and exact $d=2$ value beyond the general stationary budget. ad88f967d6335089:03.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite, $z_0\in P$, and $a_z>0$ affine on $P$ with $\sum_z(z-z_0)a_z=0$. Write $N=|P|$, $\bar z=N^{-1}\sum_z z$, $E=\operatorname{span}(P-\bar z)$, $\Sigma=N^{-1}\sum_z(z-\bar z)(z-\bar z)^{\mathsf T}$ on $E$, $w=z_0-\bar z$, and $\Delta=w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}w$. For a singleton take $\Delta=0$ and omit the inverse term. With $\alpha=N^{-1}\sum_z a_z$ and $a_0=a_{z_0}$,
$$
a_z=\alpha[1+w^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(z-\bar z)],\qquad
a_0=\alpha(1+\Delta),\qquad
\sum_z a_z^2=\frac{Na_0^2}{1+\Delta}.
$$
Conversely the displayed affine array for any $\alpha>0$ satisfies the balance and is admissible exactly when all brackets are positive. For $P=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$, $N\ge2$, this is equivalent to $|z_0-\bar z|<(N+1)/6$. At $N=2m,z_0=m-1$, feasibility is equivalent to $m\ge2$, and $\sum_z a_z^2=2ma_0^2(4m^2-1)/(4m^2+2)$. For $a_0^2=4/9$ the latter mass is $4m(4m^2-1)/(9(2m^2+1))$, equal to $112/33$ when $m=4$.

Let $d\ge2$, let $C$ be a convex body with finitely many positive full-dimensional integer fibers $C_z$, $z\in P$, and let $z_0\in P$. Fix a unit continuous normal $u$ and a through-point cap with base coefficient $b$ and thresholds $t_z=u\cdot x_0-b\cdot(z-z_0)$. Suppose on an open interval $I_z$ about each $t_z$ the actual upper cap on $C_z$ is a cone cap whose positive $d$th volume root is $(u\cdot p_z-s)/h$ at threshold $s$, for fixed apex $p_z$ and common $h>0$. $$
M(b+\delta b)=\sum_z[a_z+h^{-1}\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)]^d.
$$
Its increment is $\sum_{k=2}^d\binom dk h^{-k}\sum_z a_z^{d-k}[\delta b\cdot(z-z_0)]^k$. The original cap is a strict local minimizer in every nonzero effective base-tilt direction in $\operatorname{span}(P-z_0)$. Single-cut homothety and fixed-normal tilt criticality alone do not imply this formula.

ae6af582a4950210:02.statement:
Let $A_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite family of nonempty compact convex sets with positive weights $w_i$, and assume at least one member $A_*$ has nonempty interior. Using the envelopes $P_U(A_i)$ in the preceding definition, the objective $F(U)=\sum_i w_i|P_U(A_i)|$ attains a minimum over all simplex orientations. On the sublevel $F(U)\le M$, a member with an inball $B(x_i,\rho_i)$ has every envelope vertex $v$ bounded by
$$
\|v-x_i\|\le dM/(w_i\kappa_{d-1}\rho_i^{d-1}),
$$
where $\kappa_{d-1}$ is the unit ball volume and $\kappa_0=1$. If $P_U(A_i)=a_i+r_iP_U(A_*)$ and $|A_i|>0$, then
$$
(w_*|A_i|/M)^{1/d}\le r_i\le (M/(w_i|A_*|))^{1/d}.
$$
On the sublevel, a sequence has a subsequence with convergent anchor vertices, orientations and labeled vertices of every envelope. Its limit orientation has full-dimensional anchor envelope, and objective values converge. The full-dimensional member hypothesis cannot in general be omitted.

ae6af582a4950210:04.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $A_i$ be finitely many nonempty compact convex sets with positive weights $w_i$ and at least one full-dimensional member. Set $F(U)=\sum_i w_i|P_U(A_i)|$, fix an orientation $U$ and write $P_U(A_i)=a_i+r_iT$ for a representative simplex $T$ of that orientation. At each facet $j$, let $c_{ij}$ be the centroid of the corresponding envelope facet and let $E_{ij}=\{x\in A_i:u_j\cdot x=h_{A_i}(u_j)\}$. For singletons put $r_i=0$ and $c_{ij}$ equal to the point. All right directional derivatives of $F$ under simultaneous linear variations of the facet normals are nonnegative if and only if, for every $j$,
$$
\sum_i w_i r_i^{d-1} c_{ij}\in\sum_i w_i r_i^{d-1}E_{ij}.
$$
In particular any local or global minimizer obeys these identities. Equivalently, there are points $x_{ij}\in E_{ij}$ balancing $\sum_i w_i r_i^{d-1}(x_{ij}-c_{ij})=0$ for each $j$. The facet centroids of the simplex $\sum_i w_i r_i^{d-1} P_U(A_i)$ belong to $\sum_i w_i r_i^{d-1}A_i$. In dimension one the objective is independent of the sole orientation.

$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r,&d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d,&d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d,&d\ge2,\ s\ge dr,
\end{cases}
$$
and extend $\Phi_d$ symmetrically to $r>s$. The branches agree at $s=dr$.

For each pair write
$$
\rho_\ell=\frac{r_{p_\ell}+r_{q_\ell}}2,\qquad
m_\ell=\frac{c_{p_\ell}+c_{q_\ell}}2,\qquad
\delta_\ell=r_j-\rho_\ell,\qquad
\theta_\ell=\frac{\gamma_K(c_j-m_\ell)}{\rho_\ell},
$$
where $\gamma_K(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tK\}$ is the Minkowski gauge. Then $\delta_\ell\ge0$, and the compatibility inclusion $m_\ell+\rho_\ell K\subseteq C_j$ is equivalent to $m_\ell-c_j\in\delta_\ell K$. In particular $\theta_\ell\le d\delta_\ell/\rho_\ell$.

Write $H_i=\{x:(i,x)\in H\}$ for a closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(j,c_j)$, and $t_+=\max\{t,0\}$. For each selected pair,
$$
|C_{p_\ell}\cap H_{p_\ell}|+|C_{q_\ell}\cap H_{q_\ell}|
\ge V(1-\theta_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell})
\ge V(1-d\delta_\ell/\rho_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell}).
$$
Writing $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$, the raw depth obeys
$$
h_S((j,c_j))\ge V\left[\Gamma_d r_j^d+
\sum_\ell (1-\theta_\ell)_+^d\Phi_d(r_{p_\ell},r_{q_\ell})\right].
$$

$$
\Sigma_j=\frac1{M_j}\sum_{z\in P}\int_{K_z^{(j)}}(x-g_z^{(j)})(x-g_z^{(j)})^{\mathsf T}\,dx.
$$
Let \(\ell_j\ge0\) be continuous on the lifted union of the \(j\)-th fibers. Write \(\delta_j=\max_z d_H(K_z^{(j)},K_z^{(0)})\), and assume
$$
\sup_{\substack{p\in P,\ y_j\in K_p^{(j)},\ y\in K_p^{(0)}\\
\lVert y_j-y\rVert\le\delta_j}}\lvert\ell_j(p,y_j)-\ell_0(p,y)\rvert\longrightarrow0.
$$
Set \(f_j(p,y)=(\ell_j(p,y)E_{K_p^{(j)}}(y)/M_j)^{1/(d+1)}\), using the boundary value zero for the projective energy. For \(\epsilon_j\ge0\) with \(\epsilon_j\to\epsilon_0\), let \(b_j(p,y)\) be the infimum of the \(j\)-th summed fiber masses in the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(x-y)+\epsilon_j f_j(p,y)\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_j u}\ge0,
\qquad (a,u)\ne(0,0).
$$
Then \(b_j(p,y_j)\to b_0(p,y)\) uniformly on the displayed correspondences. Each \(b_j\) attains a maximum on its lifted union, and both the maxima and the maxima divided by \(M_j\) converge. b2439018eaa1681d:01.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base with compatible compact convex bodies $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$. Write $S=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_z$, $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and $dm=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_z}$, with $M=m(S)$ and $dP_0=dm/M$. Let $L,U>0$ be continuous concave on $C$, with $\int\log L\,dP_0=\int\log U\,dP_0=0$. Suppose finitely many marks $Y_i\in C$, weights $\sigma_i>0$ with $\sum_i\sigma_i=1$, and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i\frac{\sigma_i}{L_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
$$
If $U(Y_i)/L_i\le e^\delta$ for every $i$, where $\delta\ge0$, then $b=\int(U/L)\,dP_0$ lies in $[1,e^\delta]$,
$$
D\bigl(P_0\,\big\|\,(U/(bL))P_0\bigr)=\log b,\qquad
\int_S |U-L|\,dm
\le M\max_S L\bigl(e^\delta\sqrt{2\delta}+e^\delta-1\bigr).
$$

On any $K_z$, write $B_z=\max_{K_z}U+\max_{K_z}L$, suppressing the base coordinate, and let $\omega_d$ be the unit $d$-ball volume. For every $\varrho>0$ with nonempty core,
$$
\sup_{\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial K_z)\ge\varrho}|U(z,x)-L(z,x)|
\le \left(\frac{2\cdot 4^d B_z^d}{\omega_d\varrho^d}\int_{K_z}|U-L|\,dX\right)^{1/(d+1)},\qquad
\max_{K_z}U\le\frac{(d+1)M\max_S L}{|K_z|}e^\delta .
$$
The first estimate on the core applies to any two nonnegative continuous concave functions on a full-dimensional compact convex body, with the zero case $B_z=0$ understood directly. For bounded $\delta$, the certificate thus gives the modulus $O(\delta^{1/[2(d+1)]})$ on any fixed positive-radius core.

b2439018eaa1681d:04.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty and $d\ge1$. On this fixed base let compact convex bodies $K_{j,z}$ with nonempty interiors converge in Hausdorff distance, for each $z$, to a compact convex body $K_z$ with nonempty interior. Write $S_j=\bigcup_z\{z\}\times K_{j,z}$ and $C_j=\operatorname{conv}S_j$, with $S,C$ for the limits. Assume compatibility $C_j\cap(\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d)=\{z\}\times K_{j,z}$ and the same for $C$. Use the sampled volume $dm_j=\sum_z\delta_z\otimes dX|_{K_{j,z}}$, mass $M_j$, fiber centroids $g_{j,z}$ and pooled covariance
$$
\Sigma_j=M_j^{-1}\sum_z\int_{K_{j,z}}(X-g_{j,z})(X-g_{j,z})^{\mathsf T}\,dX,
$$
and their limiting versions $dm,M,\Sigma$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and $N=d+1$. For any positive continuous concave $U$ on $C_j$ with $\int_{S_j}\log U\,dm_j/M_j=0$, define the raw buffered depth at a mark $(p,y)\in S_j$ as the infimum of the masses of closed pure-base caps containing $p$ and of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)+\varepsilon\bigl(U(p,y)E_{K_{j,p}}(y)/M_j\bigr)^{1/N}
\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_j u}\ge0,\qquad u\ne0 .
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is marked projective energy with its zero boundary value, the infimum of $\int_K[1+b\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over denominators strictly positive on $K$ at interior marks. Allow the whole-base trace, in particular in base rank zero. Let $Q_j(U)$ be the maximum raw depth on $S_j$, and define $Q(L)$ on the limit family in the same way.

Assume $L>0$ is continuous and concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm/M=0$. Suppose there are finitely many marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)\in S$, positive weights $\sigma_i$ summing to one, and probabilities $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfying
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i),\qquad
\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML).
$$
Every $Y_i$ is assumed to have maximal raw depth $Q=Q(L)$, strictly below its own pure-base depth $b_{\rm base}(p_i)$. If $U_j$ are admissible parameters with $Q_j(U_j)\le\inf_U Q_j(U)+o(1)$, then $U_j(z,\cdot)\to L(z,\cdot)$ uniformly on every compact subset of $\operatorname{int}K_z$ at the same coordinates. The zero extensions of $U_j$ and, separately, of $\log U_j$ on the sampled fibers converge in mixed $L^1$ to the corresponding zero extensions of $L$ and $\log L$. The energy-weighted factors $(U_j(z,y)E_{K_{j,z}}(y)/M_j)^{1/N}$ converge uniformly on the sampled coordinate spaces after zero extension, and so do the actual physical shifts uniformly in Euclidean unit continuous normals. Finally $Q_j(U_j)\to Q$ and $Q_j(U_j)/M_j\to Q/M$.

b25c81940a686cf0:05.statement:
Let a compact convex set $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, have positive raw mixed $d$-volume $M$. Suppose a finite collection of closed ambient halfspaces has common normalized mixed mass $\tau$, and their open interiors cover the mixed trace of $D$. Fix a nonempty set $I$ of indices, and choose compact convex positive-volume pieces $A_i$ in the continuous fibers at integer bases $z_i$ for $i\in I$. Each piece is strictly inside its own cap and strictly outside every other cap. Put $V_i=|A_i|$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}\{z_i:i\in I\}$ and
$$
f_I(z)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i V_i^{1/d}:\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i z_i=z\right\}.
$$
Then
$$
|I|\tau M\ge\sum_{z\in Q\cap\mathbb Z^n}\max\left(f_I(z)^d,\ \sum_{i\in I:z_i=z}V_i\right).
$$
For two distinct same-parity bases $z_i,z_j$, this gives
$$
2\tau M\ge V_i+V_j+\left(\frac{V_i^{1/d}+V_j^{1/d}}2\right)^d .
$$
For $k$ distinct same-parity bases with equal exclusive volumes $V$, it gives $V\le k\tau M/(2k-1)$.

b496d79ebd8db77a:01.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, and let $P$ be all its nonempty integer bases. Assume $P\ne\varnothing$ and all its fibers $K_p$ are full-dimensional compact polytopes in $\mathbb R^d$. Write $C_0=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$, and let $\eta$ be the sum of the own-fiber $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ boundary measures with the regular continuous outward unit normal marked. Suppose a finite source $\nu\ll\eta$ is coupled to $\eta$ by a physical martingale $\Pi$ preserving this mark.

Fix a unit vector $u$ and suppose $h_{K_p}(u)=a\cdot p+b$ for every $p\in P$. The plane $u\cdot x-a\cdot z=b$ supports $C_0$. Write $F_u$ for its exposed face and assume $\eta(F_u)>0$. The restrictions of $\eta$ and $\nu$ to $F_u$ are their entire normal-$u$ sectors up to null sets. There are zero crossings in both directions for $\Pi$, so $\nu(F_u)=\eta(F_u)$, and the restricted rows couple $\nu|_{F_u}$ to the full target $\eta|_{F_u}$.

For a linear isometry $E:\mathbb R^{d-1}\to u^\perp$, set $\Psi(z,t)=(z,Et+(a\cdot z+b)u)$ and $D=\Psi^{-1}(F_u)$. The pulled-back target is $\mu_u=\sum_{p\in P}\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{D_p}$, the intrinsic Hausdorff measure of the reduced trace, and $\widehat\nu_u=(\Psi^{-1})_\#(\nu|_{F_u})\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}}\mu_u$ with equal mass and affine physical moments. The measure identity includes zero-weight smaller faces and uses endpoint counting when $d=1$. If $\operatorname{aff}P=\mathbb R^n$, $F_u$ is a nonvertical supporting facet and $D$ is a full-dimensional polytope in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{d-1}$. If $d\nu=\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_j\,d\eta$ is an actual cap-allocation law, its reduced density is $\sum_j\lambda_j(\alpha_j\circ\Psi)$. A cap $c_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge\beta_j$ restricts to
$$
(c_j+(v_j\cdot u)a)\cdot z+(E^{\mathsf T}v_j)\cdot t
\ge \beta_j-(v_j\cdot u)b,
$$
with the original allocation on coincident positive-measure boundaries and indicator agreement almost everywhere for null equality loci.

If the sampled support is affine in the base for every unit direction, the canonical fiber at every $z=\sum_p\theta_p p$ in $\operatorname{conv}P$ is the Minkowski combination $\sum_p\theta_pK_p$, independently of the representation. The boundary coupling decomposes into finitely many such unweighted-target volume transports. With full base span, each nonvertical facet is the common support face $F_u$ for its continuous unit normal $u$, projects onto all of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and has a different continuous unit normal from every other nonvertical facet. Almost every measured own-fiber boundary point then has a unique nonvertical facet owner.

b4ee4b06f66fa552:02.statement:
Let $T$ be an area-one triangle with centroid $g$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_i$, and let $[-2,3]\times T$ have its six integer fibers with summed area. They form an actual cover, and are globally critical at $(0,g)$ and $(1,g)$, respectively, capturing fraction $4/9$ of their own fiber. Put $c=\sqrt5/3$. The one-cap residual-root obstacle at a base is the minimum of the roots of residual areas over the six caps. The sampled convex-threshold program minimizing $\sum h_z^2$ above these obstacles has the unique optimum $h_z=c$. Its nearest-neighbor positive convexity multipliers have component $\{-1,0,1,2\}$, which includes base $-1$ even though the strict residual there for every $H_i$ is empty. Thus nonempty strict residuals at all positive-multiplier transit nodes are not automatic.

Let $S$ be a finite union of sampled convex $d$-fibers with $d$-dimensional volume at least $v>0$ in each fiber, summed measure $dm$ and $M\le M_{\max}$. For finitely many source values $L_i>0$ assume probabilities $\rho_i,\bar\rho_i$ and weights $\sigma_i$ satisfy
$$
\frac{dm}{M}=\sum_i\sigma_i\bar\rho_i,\quad
d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)\,d\rho_i,\quad L/L_i\le A\ \rho_i\text{-a.e.},\qquad
\sum_i\sigma_i\log L_i\le0.

$$
\sigma_i=\frac{\kappa_i (L_i E_i/M)^{1/N}}{\Delta/\varepsilon},
\qquad \Delta/\varepsilon\ge a_*>0.

$$
m\{L>AT\}/M\le B_*/\log T,\qquad
\sup_S L\le 2A\exp(2^dM_{\max}B_*/v)=:L_*.
$$

Let $P=\operatorname{conv}\{(-4,-4),(4,0),(0,4)\}\cap\mathbb Z^2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a nondegenerate triangle with barycentric functions $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$. Let $\eta$ be the sum of arclength measures on $\{z\}\times\partial K$ for $z\in P$, marked by the outer unit normal $n$ of the continuous edge away from its endpoints. Then
$$
\sup_{\Phi}
\frac{\int \Phi(n,z,x)W(z,x)\,d\eta}{\int \Phi(n,z,x)\,d\eta}
=\frac{40}{93}.
$$
The supremum ranges over finite nonnegative potentials convex in the physical variables $(z,x)$ for every fixed $n$, with finite positive denominator. A constant potential attains it. The efficiency falls short of $4/9$ by $4/279$.
