b78a2eb10bd3783f:05.statement:

b84198b3fe4ca80c:01.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact and convex, $d\ge1$, $P=\operatorname{proj}_z C$, $K_z=C_z$, $r(z)=|K_z|^{1/d}$, and $L(z,x)=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ with $u\ne0$. All volumes in a fiber are Lebesgue $d$-volumes. On the domain $z\in P,\ 0\le t\le r(z)$, set $U(z,0)=\max_{K_z}L(z,\cdot)$ and, for $t>0$, set
$$
U(z,t)=\sup\{s:|K_z\cap\{L(z,\cdot)\ge s\}|\ge t^d\}.
$$
The domain is convex and $U$ is finite, bounded, upper semicontinuous and jointly concave. For the cap $H=\{L\ge0\}$, its root $c_z=|K_z\cap\{x:L(z,x)\ge0\}|^{1/d}$ is concave on the projection of $C\cap H$ if that set is nonempty. On a positive fiber a proper cap has the unique root $U(z,c_z)=0$ and the zero and full cases are decided by the fiber support extrema. Its actual mixed cap mass is $\sum_z c_z^d$, summed over the integer bases in $P$.

For each positive fiber,
$$
\int_{K_z} L(z,x)\,dx=d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt.
$$
At a mixed centroid $(j,y)$ with integer $j$, $L(j,y)=0$ and positive total mixed mass, the exact moment equations are $\sum_z(z-j)r(z)^d=0$ and $\sum_z d\int_0^{r(z)}t^{d-1}U(z,t)\,dt=0$. Null fibers contribute zero.

For $H_v=\{L(z,x)+v\cdot(z-j)\ge0\}$, the inverse is $U_v(z,t)=U(z,t)+v\cdot(z-j)$. At a parameter with no endpoint contacts on positive fibers, let $c_z$ now be the cap roots for $H_v$ and $\beta_z=-\partial_t U_v(z,c_z)$ at proper roots. These derivatives exist and are strictly positive. The mixed cap tilt gradient is
$$
\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{dc_z^{d-1}}{\beta_z}
=\sum_{\mathrm{proper}\ z}(z-j)\frac{\mathcal H^{d-1}(K_z\cap\partial H_v)}{\|u\|}.
$$
It vanishes at a tilt minimum. In dimension one, when the oriented continuous coefficient is normalized to one, each proper section has weight one.

external_dependencies: Real Stone–Weierstrass theorem for the coordinate-polynomial algebra on a compact sphere
b90a2673d60a00b3:01.reason: The search found no admitted finite signed measure injectivity result. Unlike cap symmetry on a special source, this treats every angular finite signed measure, including singular laws. Conditional Gaussian Hermite moments have nonzero multiplier at each odd degree, while antipodal differencing kills all even moments. The resulting polynomial test family is dense by Stone–Weierstrass. No graph predecessor is needed.
b90a2673d60a00b3:01.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ and let $\sigma$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\mathbb S^{N-1}$. If $\int\operatorname{sgn}(u\cdot\theta)\,d\sigma(\theta)=0$ for spherical-almost every $u$, then $\sigma$ is antipodally invariant. The value assigned at zero does not affect the almost-everywhere premise.

Consequently, for any nonzero finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^N$ and point $y$ with $\mu(\{y\})=0$, the normalized depth over closed ambient halfspaces is at least $1/2$ precisely when the pushforward of $\mu$ by $a\mapsto(a-y)/\lVert a-y\rVert$ is antipodally invariant. In that case the normalized depth is exactly $1/2$.

b90a2673d60a00b3:02.reason: This is the depth clause of the angular-transform draft. b90a2673d60a00b3:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, and suppose $S=C\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q>0$. Write $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$ and $M=\mu(S)>0$. For any actual $y=(j,c)\in S$, the following are equivalent.

1. Every closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has $\mu$-mass at least $M/2$.
2. The angular pushforward of $\mu$ about $y$ is antipodally invariant.
3. Reflection about $y$ preserves $\mu$.
4. $\mathcal H_q(S\cap(2y-S))=M$.

When these hold, every positive $q$-dimensional fiber has its exact reflected partner, the fiber at $j$ is itself positive and centrally symmetric about $c$, $y$ is the full ambient centroid, and its normalized depth is $1/2$. The conclusions refer to the measured fibers and allow unmatched $\mathcal H_q$-null fibers. For counting measure the implication from half depth to symmetry can fail.

b90a2673d60a00b3:06.statement: Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be an ambient convex body, $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, $q=\dim_H S>0$, and $M=\mathcal H_q(S)$. b90b49210bc91c87:01.reason: The accepted physical simplex Hessian gives the exact lift, sign and cap derivative in each physical chart. Complete tuples add one row relation per group, including permutations and unequal volumes; full/empty derivatives are individually zero. b90b49210bc91c87:01.statement: Fix d≥2, m=d+1, and N selected positive-volume simplex fibers with an open independently admissible neighborhood of all their physical vertices, other fibers and integer support fixed. Partition active caps into h groups of m; each group on each selected fiber has either its complete canonical centroid tuple (up to permutation) or only strict full/empty traces. On each fiber choose c with ∑c_i=0 and the velocity B_ii=−c_i, B_ij=(m c_j+c_i)/(dm−1) for i≠j. Its trace is zero, row sums are −dm c/(dm−1), and normalized canonical Lagrangian Hessian is (d²−1)||c||²/[d(dm−1)]. On the dN-dimensional direct sum E of these modes the aggregate cap derivative map L has rank≤dh and ker L has dimension≥d(N−h). external_dependencies: Finite-dimensional affine strict-orthant separation for the second-acceleration alternative.
b90b49210bc91c87:02.reason: The accepted Hessian on the full physical tangent space and strict full/empty stability yield the weighted block form. Contraction strictly decreases every affected active cap, so affine strict-orthant separation gives an objective-one stress. The kernel vector forces positive proper weights into U for some stress, not for every stress. The one-group physical improvement c8651ae0583260d9 is a strict special case.
b90b49210bc91c87:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$ and $\gamma=(d/m)^d$. Select $N$ positive-volume simplex fibers, of volumes $V_z$, in a finite actual convex fiber family. Assume an open neighborhood in the space of all their labeled vertex positions is admissible with the same integer support and the other fibers fixed. Fix a finite menu of ambient closed caps with feasible upper mass budgets; call a cap active at equality. Partition the active caps into $h$ groups of $m$. On each selected simplex each group restricts either to the full canonical centroid tuple $\{\xi_i\ge1/m\}_{i=1}^m$ in its physical barycentric chart, up to permutation, or to strictly full and strictly empty traces only. A cap is affected if it has a canonical or full trace on some selected fiber.

Write $M$ for total mixed volume and $C_a$ for cap masses. In each barycentric vertex chart use the $d$-dimensional velocity space given by $\sum_i c_i=0$, $B_{ii}=-c_i$ and $B_{ij}=(mc_j+c_i)/(dm-1)$ for $i\ne j$. On the sum $E$ of these spaces the map $L:B\mapsto(DC_a[B])_{a\ {\rm active}}$ has rank at most $dh$. Let $U$ be the set of blocks identically zero on $\ker L$. Then $|U|\le h$, and some $B\in\ker L$ is nonzero on every block outside $U$.

For any normal first stress $\lambda_a\ge0$ on affected active caps with $DM=\sum_a\lambda_a DC_a$ on the full physical tangent space, let $F_z$ be the sum of full-trace multipliers on fiber $z$ and $\alpha_{zi}$ the sum of the multipliers for canonical trace $i$ there. Then all $\alpha_{zi}$ equal $\alpha_z$, and $w_z=1-F_z=m\gamma\alpha_z\ge0$. On $E$ the Lagrangian Hessian is
$$
D^2(M-\textstyle\sum_a\lambda_a C_a)[B,B]=
\sum_z w_z V_z\frac{d^2-1}{d(dm-1)}\lVert c_z\rVert^2 .
$$
At a local fixed-budget volume maximum there exists such a stress with $\{z:w_z>0\}\subseteq U$, hence at most $h$ positive proper-trace blocks. If every normal first stress has more than $h$ such blocks, there is an actual degree-two vertex path increasing total volume and strictly lowering every affected active cap mass for all sufficiently small positive time. In particular this holds if $N>h$ and no selected fiber has a full active trace. Other budgets stay feasible.

b90b49210bc91c87:03.reason: The two actual exposed bases allow independent physical triangles. The accepted lift gives arbitrary zero-sum rows; the partial canonical incidences select two independent rows from the first block and one from the second, so rank 3 really exceeds 2. This checks exactly the omitted hypothesis in the complete-block theorem, not criticality of the chosen caps.
b90b49210bc91c87:03.statement: There is an actual two-fiber triangle family and a single group of three fixed ambient caps covering both whole fiber planes, every proper trace canonical, with first cap derivative of rank $3$ on the direct sum of the two canonical positive velocity spaces. Thus the complete-block bound $dh$ cannot be inferred from the assumption that every proper trace is canonical alone.

b989614dc4f86228:01.reason: Affine evaluations on the finite threshold indices can be fixed while retaining the signs on the diverging indices. This realizes all limiting bounded traces by one actual finite cap.
b989614dc4f86228:01.statement: Fix $n,d\ge1$, finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and a ball $R B_d$ centered at zero with $R>0$. Let $H_j=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot x\ge t_j(z)\}$, where $\|u_j\|=1$ and $t_j$ is real affine. Some subsequence has $u_j\to u$ with $\|u\|=1$ and $t_j(z)\to t(z)\in[-\infty,\infty]$ for every $z\in P$. On $P\times R B_d$, the limiting traces $\{x:u\cdot x\ge t(z)\}$ at finite thresholds, the full traces at $t(z)=-\infty$ and the empty traces at $t(z)=+\infty$ are realized by one actual closed halfspace with unit continuous normal $u$ and a finite affine threshold. For summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on any fixed family of measurable fibers inside that ball, $\mu(H_j)$ along the subsequence tends to the mass of that halfspace. Every fixed point of $P\times R B_d$ contained in infinitely many caps of the subsequence belongs to the realizing halfspace.

external_dependencies: Averkov–Weismantel mixed-integer Helly theorem, Theorem 1.1(3).
b989614dc4f86228:02.reason: Strict threshold relaxation gives a finite interior cover. The mixed-integer Helly number reduces its size, and threshold compactification gives the exact closed cover including the boundary.
b989614dc4f86228:02.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. Assume $M>0$ and put $Q=\max_{(z,x)\in S}h_\mu(z,x)$. Suppose for every $\varepsilon>0$ the interiors of at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces cover $S$, each of mass less than $Q+\varepsilon M$. Then $S$ is covered by at most $N$ nonvertical closed ambient halfspaces of mass at most $Q$, with at least one of mass $Q$.

If $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$, the hypothesis holds with $N=2^n(d+1)$. The conclusion at this cardinality covers $S$.

b989614dc4f86228:03.reason: Use the bounded-cover part of the accepted variational theorem. For each fiber the common missed region is open convex and disjoint from the old fiber, so its separating support constraint with the same cap budgets forces the stated volume maximality.
b989614dc4f86228:03.statement: Given a finite fixed ambient cap cover of a compatible convex fiber family, each fiber K_z disjoint from the open common missed region Q_z admits one closed supporting halfspace E_z containing K_z and disjoint from Q_z, unless Q_z is empty. For an attained depth minimizer S_* over its fixed actual projection P, with mass M_* and value β, the exact caps of §§1–2 and the E_z constraints make S_* an attained global volume maximizer among all compatible fibers on P obeying |S'∩H_j|≤βM_* and K'_z⊆E_z where imposed.

b989614dc4f86228:04.reason: An interior point of a positive-volume fiber contributes positive own-ball depth. At other points a compatible supporting cap has zero mass, and convexification of the positive lifts preserves all positive slices.
b989614dc4f86228:04.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. For a lattice application require $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume compatibility and $M>0$. A point $(z,x)\in S$ has positive depth if and only if $x\in\operatorname{int}K_z$. If $\mathcal L^d(K_z)=0$, every site of $P$ on the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ containing $z$ also has zero fiber volume.

Put $P_+=\{z\in P:\mathcal L^d(K_z)>0\}$ and let $C_+$ be the convex hull of the lifted fibers over $P_+$. The fibers of $C_+$ at the sites in $P_+$ are the original $K_z$, and the bases of $C_+$ in $P$ are exactly $P_+$. Deleting the null fibers therefore preserves $\mu$ and the maximum depth over the remaining mixed set. If $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, then $P_+=\operatorname{conv}(P_+)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ and $C_+\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$ consists exactly of these retained fibers.

b989614dc4f86228:05.reason: The anchored version of threshold compactification attains the infimum. Coupled limit thresholds prove continuity, and finite tilt approximation includes the pure-base comparison.
b989614dc4f86228:05.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$. For each $z\in P$ and $(u,t)\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\times\mathbb R$ define
$$
c_z(u,t)=\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}.
$$
The infimum is attained by a finite $a$, and $c_z$ is continuous on its entire parameter space. For every $x\in K_z$,
$$
h_\mu(z,x)=\min_{\|u\|=1}c_z(u,u\cdot x).
$$
In particular, the depth is continuous on each fiber, is attained by a nonvertical closed halfspace through the point, and attains its maximum over $S$.

b989614dc4f86228:06.reason: The active normalized continuous normals must balance because a separating motion increases every near-active own cap uniformly. A finite positive balance gives the exact whole-plane cover, and null sites are handled by two zero-mass caps.
b989614dc4f86228:06.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge 1$, a finite nonempty $P\subset\mathbb R^n$, and nonempty compact convex sets $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$, and $M=\mu(S)$. Let $h_\mu(z,x)$ be the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(z,x)$.

The family is compatible if the fiber of $C=\operatorname{conv}(S)$ at every $z\in P$ is exactly $K_z$. Equivalently, whenever a convex combination of bases in $P$ equals a base $z\in P$, the same Minkowski combination of the corresponding fibers lies in $K_z$. For a lattice application require $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, so $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

Assume compatibility and $M>0$. Put $q_z=\max_{x\in K_z}h_\mu(z,x)$ and $Q=\max_{z\in P}q_z$. At any maximizing mark $x_z$ of a positive-volume fiber $K_z$, the active unit continuous normals
$$
U_z=\{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}:c_z(u,u\cdot x_z)=q_z\}
$$
have zero in their convex hull, where $c_z(u,t)=\inf_a\mu\{(w,y):a\cdot(w-z)+u\cdot y\ge t\}$. There are $2\le k\le d+1$ actual nonvertical closed caps of mass exactly $q_z$ through $(z,x_z)$ whose unit continuous normals form a minimal positive dependence. The caps cover the whole plane $\{z\}\times\mathbb R^d$. At a null site two actual nonvertical zero-mass caps cover its whole plane. In particular at most $|P|(d+1)$ such caps cover $P\times\mathbb R^d$, each of mass at most $Q$. Caps selected at a site with $q_z<Q$ have strict slack at the common budget $Q$.

b989614dc4f86228:07.reason: At an attained fixed-projection minimum, the chosen exact cap budgets remain a cover for competing bodies. The bounded cover uses explicit support constraints and the whole-plane version needs only the cap budgets.
b989614dc4f86228:07.statement:
Fix $n,d\ge1$ and a finite nonempty lattice-convex projection $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$. Consider compatible families of nonempty compact convex fibers over exactly $P$, with positive total mixed $d$-volume. Compatibility means that the convex hull of the lifted fibers has the specified fiber at every site of $P$. For a family $S$, write $\mu_S$ for summed $d$-volume on its fibers, $M(S)=\mu_S(S)$, and $h_{\mu_S}$ for raw closed-halfspace depth. Suppose $S_*$ attains the minimum of $\max_{y\in S}h_{\mu_S}(y)/M(S)$ in this fixed-$P$ class, with value $\beta$ and total mass $M_*>0$.

There are two fixed-cap volume formulations of this attained minimum.

1. For any finite nonvertical closed cap cover $(H_j)$ of $S_*$ with $\mu_{S_*}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$, at each $z\in P$ whose plane is not entirely covered there is one closed supporting halfspace $E_z$ containing $K_{*,z}$, entirely covered by the cap traces at $z$. Then $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ over compatible families $S'$ on $P$ with $K'_z\subset E_z$ where imposed and $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ for each $j$. In particular such a cover can be chosen with at most $2^n(d+1)$ caps.
2. There is a fixed cover by at most $|P|(d+1)$ nonvertical closed caps such that $S_*$ globally maximizes $M(S')$ subject solely to the budgets $\mu_{S'}(H_j)\le\beta M_*$ in the same class. In each formulation, the tight budget inequalities at $S_*$ are exactly those with cap mass $\beta M_*$.

external_dependencies: Ordinary Brunn–Minkowski inequality in dimension d−1 on the positive interior sections.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:01.reason: The same-height sections and Brunn–Minkowski in dimension d−1 give the additional positive terms. The established 9dd1398102da730a has exactly the d=2, B=T specialization, and dc131fd85b716f8d proves planar section extrusion at each tested level under extra cap-menu hypotheses. The general d≥2 inequality and arbitrary convex facet are retained in this draft.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $D$ be a convex body in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $F$ be a compact convex subset of a hyperplane normal to the unit vector $e$, with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. Translate $F$ to height zero in this direction, let $I$ be the open height interval of $D$, and write $h=|I|$, $m=d-1$, $U=|D|$ and $D_t$ for the height-$t$ section identified with $e^\perp$. Then $(D+F)_t=D_t+F$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
|D+F|&\ge\int_I\bigl(|D_t|^{1/m}+f^{1/m}\bigr)^m\,dt\\
&=U+fh+\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}\binom mj f^{j/m}\int_I |D_t|^{(m-j)/m}\,dt .
\end{aligned}
$$
For $d=2$, $|D+F|=U+fh$.

In particular, suppose $A,K,B$ are convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, $u\ne0$, $D=A\cap\{u\cdot x\ge a_0\}$ is a proper positive-volume cap, and $B\subseteq\{u\cdot x\le b_0\}$ has a support facet $F=B\cap\{u\cdot x=b_0\}$ with $f=\mathcal H^{d-1}(F)>0$. For $q=|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge(a_0+b_0)/2\}|$, the first bound above applies to $2^dq$ with $e=u/\lVert u\rVert$ and $h=(h_A(u)-a_0)/\lVert u\rVert$, where $h_A$ is the support function of $A$. In particular $2^dq\ge U+fh$. If these bodies are the positive-volume fibers at $-1,0,1$ of a mixed body and the closed ambient cap with these three thresholds has raw mixed mass $Q$, then $2^d Q\ge (2^d+1)U+fh$.

For $d=2$, $B=T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1,\ i=1,2,3\}$ and $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1))$, the cap $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ has $2^d Q_i=4Q_i\ge5U_i+3(h_A(v_i)+1)$ for every proper positive $A$ trace of area $U_i$.

b9b0fda52c8adffe:02.reason: The quadratic polynomial of 2021348e0b2d8c9f applies to the ordinary planar bodies T,A and supplies the factor 2V₂(T,A). It does not calculate this triangle's coefficient 3Σ h_A(v_j) or map it to the opposite residual cap. The draft gives both using the same actual body in each calculation.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:02.statement:
Let $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1))$, $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1,\ i=1,2,3\}$, and $b=|T|=9/2$. For every planar convex body $A$, writing $h_A$ for its support function,
$$
|(A+T)/2|=\frac{|A|+b+3\sum_j h_A(v_j)}4.
$$
If $(A+T)/2\subseteq K$ for a planar convex body $K$, the same expression lower-bounds $|K|$. For every $i$ such that $R_i=A\cap\{v_i\cdot x\le-1\}$ has positive area, writing $q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$,
$$
|K|-q_i\ge\frac{|R_i|+b+3\sum_j h_{R_i}(v_j)}4.
$$

b9b0fda52c8adffe:03.reason: The zero-area T facets and the common Q give middle masses Q−U_i. The ordinary planar three-cap cover of ac7ba1e1e0ebc955 (3) gives k≤9Q/4−F with reverse order and the exact γ₂=4/9. The strict target then gives k<a+b−2F. Nonheaviness gives k≥|a−b|, which suffices for F<min(a,b) even at equality in the nonheavy bound. Combining the proposed mixed-area formula with k<a+b−2F gives the support-sum inequality, and U_i≤Q<4(a+b−F)/9 gives the last mass bound. The exact full-T all-proper common-cap configuration with nonheavy B already has Q>2M/9 by 9dd1398102da730a, so these conditional scalar bounds supply no further exclusion there. For the separate elementary chord check, the middle trace is fixed as α varies. The left derivative of the A trace at α=1 is its proper chord length divided by ‖v_i‖ by coarea and continuity of interior section length. The left derivative of the T trace is −3 from its explicit section length ℓ(t)=t+2 on [−2,1]. Their sum is ≤0 at a minimum, giving the claimed capacity without a proper middle trace. This is the fixed-normal, tilt-only counterpart of the first-variation calculation in ba445d671279810a, whose full chord-interval theorem assumes actual depth criticality and proper A,K traces. No additional geometric closure is needed for the full-T nonheavy common-mass case.
b9b0fda52c8adffe:03.statement: In the stated full-T planar normalization let the three proper A cuts have masses U_(1)≤U_(2)≤U_(3), common actual ambient cap mass Q, and F=U_(1)+U_(2)+U_(3)/4. Write a=|A|, k=|K|, b=9/2 and S=Σ_i h_A(v_i). Then k≤(9/4)Q−F. If Q<2(a+b+k)/9 then k<a+b−2F. If in addition a,b≤(a+b+k)/2 then F<min(a,b), S+(8/3)F<a+b and max_i U_i<(4/9)(a+b−F). If each cap minimizes actual through-middle mass over its integer tilt, its A cutting chord has length/||v_i||≤3.

b9d705e0e5ad374f:01.reason: The accepted 9c1d072121e84553 lower bound is strictly above one third, which does not imply three eighths. The proof here exploits the four-site balance $(1+2t,s,1,t)$, the exact stronger quadratic width bound, and the full right-only cap elimination when none of the other noncentral fibers is wholly captured. Pure-base caps retain the entire centroid fiber.
b9d705e0e5ad374f:01.statement: Let a planar convex body have exactly four nonempty integer fibers, each a positive-length interval. If its true mixed length centroid has integer base, that centroid is a sampled point and every closed ambient halfspace containing it captures at least $3/8$ of the total mixed length.

b9d705e0e5ad374f:02.reason: The accepted 1d56946d90d684b0 gives the same first numerical bound under actual convex-body compatibility and integer base of the centroid. The present statement concerns arbitrary separate interval length measures and uses the additional finite-cardinality Cauchy/AM–GM bound. Its proof uses only zero continuous first moment and the absence of an entirely captured interval.
b9d705e0e5ad374f:02.statement: Let $N\ge1$ bounded intervals of positive widths $w_i$ be equipped with the sum of their separate length measures. Suppose the combined continuous centroid is zero. If $x\ge0$ wholly captures none of the intervals, then its length under the sum measure is at least $\sum_iw_i^2/(2\max_iw_i)$, which is at least $M/(1+\sqrt N)$ for $M=\sum_iw_i$. The intervals need not be the fibers of a convex body.

external_dependencies: Brunn–Minkowski in each prelimit affine m-plane.

Borell’s affine-support characterization of s-concave measures, as stated in Fradelizi and Guédon, The Extreme Points of Subsets of s-Concave Probabilities and a Geometric Localization Theorem, §2, https://perso.math.u-pem.fr/guedon.olivier/Articles/02/Fradelizi-Guedon.pdf.
Portmanteau theorem for weak convergence of probabilities.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:01.reason: Unlike the pending bounded-prelimit intrinsic lift 4103337048e3d0cb, weak convergence alone suffices, even for varying affine hulls; Borell on the affine support handles the endpoint and excludes q>m. Fixed interior balls combined with putatively escaping or large-root points give compactness and boundedness; Fubini proves the converse and the claimed sharpness.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:01.statement: For integers D≥m≥1, the weak probability limits in ℝ^D of uniform intrinsic H_m laws on compact m-dimensional convex bodies are exactly the following: a Dirac mass if q=0; a probability with H_q-density f on a compact convex q-dimensional support whose f^(1/(m−q)) has a bounded upper-semicontinuous concave representative if 0<q<m; or a uniform probability on a compact m-dimensional convex body if q=m. Here q is the affine support dimension, and in every case q≤m and the limit law is 1/m-concave for compact positive-mass sets. For 0<q<m the convex lift over x has centered (m−q)-ball of radius (f(x)/κ_{m−q})^(1/(m−q)); it projects ordinary volume exactly to f H_q, also for any finite positive mass. Contracting its hidden directions gives the converse, and the density proportional to (1−Σx_i)^(m−q) on a q-simplex makes the exponent sharp. In the q=m case identity projection represents uniform probability but represents it by unnormalized volume only when the support volume is one; an extra prism direction of height the reciprocal support volume makes its ordinary volume one.

external_dependencies: Brunn–Minkowski and its equality characterization for full-dimensional compact convex bodies.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:02.reason: Brunn–Minkowski equality under equal volumes and midpoint inclusion forces the two outer lifts to be translates and the middle lift to equal their Minkowski average; their projections would have equal length. Common weights give exact midpoint containment.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:02.statement: The compatible planar fibers at −1,0,1 with respective horizontal lengths 1,2,1, common left endpoint 0 and common vertical interval [−ε/2,ε/2] have separately normalized weak laws Uniform[0,1], Uniform[0,2], Uniform[0,1]. No full-dimensional convex lifts of these three laws of equal positive volume in any common dimension and under a fixed linear projection can satisfy the midpoint inclusion. Dividing the original volumes by the common mass 4ε instead gives densities 1/4 on the respective intervals, represented by compatible centered rectangles of height 1/4 and volumes 1/4,1/2,1/4.

external_dependencies: Brunn–Minkowski in the fixed hidden dimension r and Fubini’s theorem.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:03.reason: Pointwise Brunn–Minkowski on the common r-sections yields radius superinterpolation even with nonempty degenerate sections; integrate section volumes and use the projection identity for the exact cap class.
b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e:03.statement: Fix a common orthogonal decomposition ℝ^m=ℝ^q×ℝ^r with r=m−q≥1 and a common c>0. bd3988521f16dd20:1.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:2.reason: Either sign of volume change is available. The two signature weights differ by the nonzero orientation imbalance, so at least one sign region yields a strict decrease.
bd3988521f16dd20:2.statement: At a Hausdorff local minimum of the weighted cap mean among bodies with the same sections, every eligible strict signature patch satisfies $W=\Phi(K)$. A locally positive-curvature normal patch crossing only one unoriented plane class with unequal total weights in its two orientations excludes such a minimum, including when the body is nonsmooth elsewhere.

bd3988521f16dd20:3.reason: A ray on the chosen plane and on no other distinct plane reaches a boundary point where the chosen plane crosses transversely. bd3988521f16dd20:3.statement: For $d\ge2$ with everywhere positive spherical support curvature, any imbalanced unoriented plane class excludes Hausdorff local minimality of the weighted normalized cap mean under exact section constraints. bd3988521f16dd20:4.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

bd3988521f16dd20:5.reason: The bump is $C^3$ at the joins. With $z=\cos^2(6\phi)$, $\psi+\psi''=432z-575z^2\ge-143$. The old patch is at least $\sin(\pi/12)>1/4$ from the other two lines, and at least $\cos(\pi/12)$ from the first, whereas the boundary displacement is at most $25t\le1/40$. The planar area formula follows from $\frac12\int\det(X_t,X_t')=\frac12\int (h_t^2-(h_t')^2)$. Integrating the even cosine powers gives $\int\psi=\pi/16$, $\int\psi^2=35\pi/768$ and $\int(\psi')^2=15\pi/4$. The normalized derivative uses $W=1/3$, $Q/|K|=1/2$ and $V'(0)=\pi/16$. The derivative concerns the upper cover.
bd3988521f16dd20:5.statement: For the unit disk with three equally weighted normals $120^\circ$ apart, take $h_t(\phi)=1+t\cos^4(6\phi)$ on $|\phi|\le\pi/12$ and $h_t=1$ elsewhere, for $0<t\le1/1000$. All three central chords are unchanged. The exact volume change is $\Delta V=\pi t/16-2845\pi t^2/1536>0$, the three cap areas are $(\pi/2+\Delta V,\pi/2,\pi/2)$, the weighted mean is $1/2-\Delta V/[6(\pi+\Delta V)]$, and the normalized equal-cover bound has derivative $-1/96$ at zero.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:02.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be nonempty compact convex fibers. Write $L(z,X)=\ell(z)+c\cdot X$, where $\ell(z)=b+\beta\cdot z$ and $L>0$ on the placed fibers, hence on their convex hull. On the fixed fiber $z$, $T_z(X)=X/L(z,X)$ has signed Jacobian $\ell(z)L(z,X)^{-d-1}$. If $\ell(z)\ne0$, its inverse on the image is $X=\ell(z)Y/(1-c\cdot Y)$ and its image is convex. Positivity of $L$ allows collapse when $\ell(z)=0$.

Assume now that $\ell>0$ at every sampled base. The label-preserving images $J_z=T_z(K_z)$ are compatible, meaning $\sum_j\lambda_jJ_{z_j}\subseteq J_q$ for each anchored relation $q=\sum_j\lambda_j z_j\in P$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, if and only if for every such relation and $X_j\in K_{z_j}$,
$$
\frac{\ell(q)\sum_j\lambda_j X_j/L(z_j,X_j)}{\sum_j\lambda_j\ell(z_j)/L(z_j,X_j)}\in K_q.
$$
Equivalently, for every $v\in\mathbb R^d$ the support $\alpha_z(v)$ is the unique solution of $h_{K_z}(v-\alpha c)=\alpha\ell(z)$, and compatibility holds exactly when $\alpha_q(v)\ge\sum_j\lambda_j\alpha_{z_j}(v)$ for every extreme anchored representation and every $v$. For polytopes the maximum defining $\alpha_z(v)$ occurs at an original vertex. If $K_z=\ell(z)K$ with $1+c\cdot X>0$ on $K$, then all $J_z$ coincide and are compatible.

A closed cap $a\cdot z+u\cdot X\ge h$ transforms on the positive chart into $a\cdot z-h+[\ell(z)u-(a\cdot z-h)c]\cdot Y\ge0$. This expression is affine if $u\beta^{\mathsf T}-ca^{\mathsf T}=0$. A positive denominator depending on $X$ can destroy compatibility even under strict proper closed-minor quotas, and it can send a cap to a nonconvex set or to traces that are not those of a single halfspace even for compatible image fibers. For a full-dimensional fiber, $T_z$ pushes $dX/L$ to $\ell(z)^{d-1}(1-c\cdot Y)^{-d}\,dY$ on $J_z$, with density ratio $(\max_{K_z}L/\min_{K_z}L)^d$. This ratio is unbounded under positivity alone. For $c=0$ the density is $\ell(z)^{d-1}$, equal across labels when $d=1$.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:06.statement:
The pushforward of $dX/(1+X)$ on $[0,1]$ under $X\mapsto Y=X/(1+X)$ is the measure $(1-Y)^{-1}\,dY$ on $[0,1/2]$. It cannot be the $Y$-marginal, up to a common positive factor, of uniform Lebesgue volume on a compact convex body in $\mathbb R^{1+r}$ for any integer $r\ge1$.

Even requiring only preservation of total tilted masses at original integer labels can fail. Use the same volume-one convex fiber at $z=-1,0,1$ and $L(z)=1+z/2$, giving tilted masses $(2,1,2/3)$. No compact convex fibers $A_{-1},A_0,A_1\subset\mathbb R^r$ with $(A_{-1}+A_1)/2\subset A_0$, $1\le r<\infty$, have these three volumes up to a common positive factor. More generally, set $L(-1)=e$, $L(0)=1$, $L(1)=2-e$ with $0<e<1$, extended affinely, and $\nu_z=1/L(z)$. If such compatible fibers have $r$-volumes $W_z$ with $s\nu_z/D\le W_z\le sD\nu_z$ for some $s>0$ and $D\ge1$, then
$$
D\ge\left(\frac{e^{-1/r}+(2-e)^{-1/r}}2\right)^{r/2}\ge[e(2-e)]^{-1/4}.
$$
In particular no uniform two-sided factor works even with the lift dimension freely chosen.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:10.reason: Accepted a25fd77c033ce8f5 gives the full ordinary constant-normalized chart and label-plane comparison, and f6c497926ac327fa uses a homogeneous slice before taking a marginal. bd4e19d78aaec9e1:10.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be compact and convex, with $d\ge1$, and write $w=(z,X)$. For $L>0$ on $C$, set $\Phi(w)=(Z,Y,s)=(z,X,1)/L(w)$. The inverse on the image is $(z,X)=(Z,Y)/s$. Each original closed halfspace $a\cdot z+u\cdot X\ge h$ corresponds on the image to $a\cdot Z+u\cdot Y-hs\ge0$.

If $L=b+\beta\cdot z+c\cdot X$ is affine, its image is the convex slice
$$
(Z,Y)\in sC,\qquad s>0,\qquad \beta\cdot Z+c\cdot Y+bs=1.
$$
The original label $z$ lies in $Z=zs$, $\ell(z)s+c\cdot Y=1$, where $\ell(z)=b+\beta\cdot z$. For $c\ne0$ these $d$-planes are nonparallel for distinct labels, and $Z$ varies along each full-dimensional old fiber with $z\ne0$. On any full-dimensional old $d$-fiber the intrinsic $d$-Jacobian and tilted density are, respectively,
$$
J_{\Phi,z}=L^{-d-1}\sqrt{\ell(z)^2+(1+|z|^2)|c|^2},\qquad
\frac{d\Phi_*(dX/L)}{d\mathcal H^d}=\frac{L^d}{\sqrt{\ell(z)^2+(1+|z|^2)|c|^2}}.
$$
Here the second $L$ is evaluated at the inverse point. Neither formula requires $\ell(z)\ne0$.

If $L=\min_j A_j>0$ for finitely many affine $A_j$, the image is the locus $\min_j A_j^{\rm hom}=1$ within the convex set $(Z,Y)\in sC$, $s>0$, $A_j^{\rm hom}\ge1$ for every $j$. Here $A_j^{\rm hom}(Z,Y,s)=s A_j((Z,Y)/s)$. Each active cell maps to a convex affine slice. The whole image can fail to be convex. On a single fiber $C=[-1,1]^2$ with $L=2-|X_1|$, both the homogeneous image and the injective map $X\mapsto X/L$ have nonconvex images, despite positive constants in both affine pieces.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:11.reason: The draft includes the exact intrinsic Jacobian for each original full-dimensional fiber, hence the density of dX/L with respect to its own image d-measure. bd4e19d78aaec9e1:11.statement: For a fixed old d-fiber z in the positive affine homogeneous chart the intrinsic d-Jacobian is J=√(ℓ(z)²+(1+|z|²)|c|²)L^(−d−1); the pushed dX/L has intrinsic density L^d/√(ℓ(z)²+(1+|z|²)|c|²). No ℓ(z)≠0 condition is required for the lift.

bd4e19d78aaec9e1:12.reason: The actual row masses and original-volume mixture follow by setting ν_i=(σ_i/L_i)ρ_i in 86609687edc6bef4 equation (1) or in the finite part of 91a17de92a473aeb. bd4e19d78aaec9e1:12.statement:
Let $S$ be the union of finitely many placed compact positive-volume $d$-fibers, let $C=\operatorname{conv}S$, and let $dm$ be the summed fiber Lebesgue measure of total $M>0$. Let $L$ be continuous and positive on $C$, and put $\Phi(w)=(w,1)/L(w)$. Suppose nonnegative weights $\sigma_i$ and probability rows $\rho_i$ on $S$ for the positive weights have marks $Y_i\in C$, $L_i=L(Y_i)$, and satisfy
$$
\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i,\qquad \int L\,d\rho_i=L_i,\qquad
\sum_{i:\sigma_i>0}\frac{\sigma_i}{L_i}\rho_i=\frac{dm}{ML}.
$$
Then the labeled row measures $\Phi_*[(L/L_i)\rho_i]$ are probabilities with means $\Phi(Y_i)$. Their weighted sum with the unchanged $\sigma_i$ is $\Phi_*(dm/M)$. If $L=\min_j A_j$ for finitely many affine $A_j$, then for each $j$ with $A_j(Y_i)=L_i$, the corresponding lifted row is concentrated on $A_j^{\rm hom}=1$, where $A_j^{\rm hom}(U,s)=s A_j(U/s)$ for $s>0$.

bd886f63d6450164:01.statement:

H''(v)=w(v)[av+b+cA(v)],\qquad \operatorname{supp}(-A'')\subseteq\{H=0\}.

If $c\ne0$, or if $c=0$ and $av+b$ is a nonzero affine function, then the curvature measure $-A''$ is supported on at most two points in $J$.

be37e5b9b9c4c946:01.statement:
Let $n=d=1$, $\sigma=\sqrt{5/24}$, $\varepsilon,h>0$, $H=h\sigma$ and $Y=\sigma(\varepsilon+h)/2$, with $Y+H<1/2$. Take the actual hull of the intervals $K_{-1}=[-1,0]$, $K_0=[Y-1,Y+1]$, $K_1=[0,1]$ at bases $-1,0,1$. Its mixed mass is $4$ and its pooled within-fiber covariance is $\sigma^2$. For a source $(p,c+t)$ in a length-$L$ interval centered at $c$, use the tied profile $f_H=(L/4)\sqrt{1-(2t/L)^2}$. For continuous orientation $s=\pm1$ and arbitrary physical tilt $A$, the cap value is the mixed integral of
$$
\Psi\left(\frac{s(x-(c+t))+A(z-p)+\varepsilon\sigma f_H}{H}\right),\qquad
\Psi(q)=(q+1)_+-q_+ .
$$
Include closed pure-base caps with their ordinary masses. The unique globally deepest mark for the infimum over these caps is $(0,Y)$ with raw depth $2+Y$. Every positive-orientation tilt is minimizing there. For the untilted positive cap the lower and upper strip planes are $x=-H/2,+H/2$, and the normalized strip coarea masses on bases $-1,0,1$ are $\sigma/2,\sigma,\sigma/2$. beffb23a92dd631a:02.statement:

$$

beffb23a92dd631a:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^r$ be finite and affinely spanning, with the origin in the relative interior of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$. For each $p\in P$, let $K_p$ be a compact convex set of positive $d$-volume. Suppose the family is compatible, meaning that the convex hull of $S=\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$ has exactly $K_p$ as its fiber at $p$. Write $\mu=\sum_p\delta_p\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_p})$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For an affine $L$ positive on $P$, take the unweighted fiber-volume measure of the family obtained from $S$ by $(p,x)\mapsto(p/L(p),x/L(p))$. Assume its maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth is locally minimized at $L=1$ among positive affine denominators. Write $\beta$ for this maximum at $L=1$ and $Q=\beta M$.

Index the deepest bases by $p_i$. At each one choose any exact positive circuit of nonvertical closed caps
$$
H_{ij}=\{(p,x):a_{ij}\cdot p+u_{ij}\cdot x\ge b_{ij}\},\qquad
\|u_{ij}\|=1,\qquad \mu(H_{ij})=Q,
$$
whose boundaries pass through a common deepest mark $(p_i,x_i)$ and whose weights satisfy $\rho_{ij}>0$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, and $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. At every other base use a fixed circuit covering the full fiber plane with each cap of mass strictly below $Q$. Such choices exist.

For each selected critical cap, let $\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}$, $\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}$ and $\theta^{\rm out}_{ij}$ be the sums of $(d-1)$-dimensional section area on its proper sections, inside supporting sections (the fiber is contained in the closed cap), and outside supporting sections (the cap meets the fiber in a supporting face of zero $d$-volume), respectively. These are measures on the lifted sections in the original coordinates, with zero-area sections contributing zero. For $d=1$ the section measure is counting measure.

For every such choice of circuits and every Borel system $\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ on the inside supporting sections, there exist outside densities $\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\in[0,1]$ and nonnegative multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$. Put
$$
\zeta_{ij}=\theta^{\rm pr}_{ij}+\sigma^{\rm in}_{ij}\theta^{\rm in}_{ij}
                     +\sigma^{\rm out}_{ij}\theta^{\rm out}_{ij},
\qquad S_{ij}=\zeta_{ij}(\mathbb R^{r+d})>0.
$$
One such choice satisfies the linear identity
$$
-d\int A(p)\,d\mu
=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\left[-d\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
                             +\int \ell_{ij}(p,x)\,d\zeta_{ij}\right]
\tag{1}
$$
simultaneously for every signed affine $A$ and every signed cap velocity $\ell_{ij}(p,x)=\delta a_{ij}\cdot p+\delta u_{ij}\cdot x-\delta b_{ij}$ satisfying, for every $i$,
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}\delta u_{ij}=0,\qquad
\sum_j\rho_{ij}(\delta a_{ij}\cdot p_i-\delta b_{ij})=0.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular, the same certificate gives
$$
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta,\qquad
\int A(p)\,d\mu=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}\int_{H_{ij}} A(p)\,d\mu
\quad\text{for every affine }A,\qquad
\lambda_{ij} S_{ij}=c_i\rho_{ij}\quad(c_i\ge0).
\tag{3}
$$
Consequently each group has either all multipliers positive or all zero. Equivalently, $\lambda_{ij}=\pi_i\kappa_{ij}/\beta$, where $\pi_i=\beta\sum_j\lambda_{ij}$ are nonnegative and sum to one, and $\kappa_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/\sum_l(\rho_{il}/S_{il})$. The same choice of outside allocations and multipliers works for all tests in (1)–(3) for the prescribed inside system.

c0611f2da2e55fa1:02.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact polytope, $d\ge1$, whose nonempty integer fibers are all positive $d$-volume. The target of the rows starting in $F$ is $\eta|_F-\zeta_F$, where $\zeta_F$ is exactly the target law of the rows starting outside $F$ and ending in $F$. Its mass is
$$
L_F=\eta(F)-\nu(F)=\Pi\{w\notin F,\ w'\in F\}\ge0.
$$
The raw restriction of the coupling has target $\eta|_F$ exactly when $L_F=0$. In general it extends, by adding the diagonal coupling of $\zeta_F$, to a martingale from $\nu|_F+\zeta_F$ to $\eta|_F$. Without the correction, $\int_F\psi\,d\nu\le\int_F\psi\,d\eta$ for each finite nonnegative convex function on the affine plane of $F$.

$$

c0fc791108fc8765:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define $E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over $a$ for which the denominator is positive on $K$, and let $a_y$ be its unique minimizer. The maps $y\mapsto a_y$ and $y\mapsto E_K(y)$ are smooth on $\operatorname{int}K$ and
$$
\nabla_y E_K(y)=(d+1)E_K(y)a_y,\qquad
\nabla_y E_K(y)^{1/d}=\frac{d+1}{d}E_K(y)^{1/d}a_y.
$$
The optimal denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$ is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $K$ and strictly greater than $1/(d+1)$ on $\operatorname{int}K$.

The fibers $C_z$ are convex bodies with a uniform positive inradius. If $h_K(u)=\max_{x\in K}u\cdot x$, then
$$
h_{C_z}(u)=\max_{\substack{\lambda_p\ge0,\ \sum_p\lambda_p=1\\ \sum_p\lambda_p p=z}}
\sum_p\lambda_p h_{K_p}(u).

$$

c1694074e553a581:03.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, and let $y=(z_0,x_0)\in C$ with $z_0\in\mathbb Z$. Write $K_z$ for its continuous fibers. Set $N_k^\pm=(K_{z_0\pm k}-x_0)/k$ for integers $k\ge1$ and let $h_\pm(a)$ be the extended gauge of $C-y$ evaluated at $(\pm1,a)$. Then $N_k^\pm=\{a:h_\pm(a)\le1/k\}$ are nested decreasing. The strict-side volume pushforwards under $(z_0\pm k,x)\mapsto (x-x_0)/k$ have densities
$$
f_\pm(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^d\mathbf1_{N_k^\pm}(a)=F_d(\lfloor1/h_\pm(a)\rfloor),\qquad F_d(m)=\sum_{k=1}^m k^d,
$$
where $1/\infty=0$. They have convex superlevels, total masses $\sum_{k\ge1}|K_{z_0\pm k}|$, and first moments $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-1}\int_{K_{z_0\pm k}}(x-x_0)\,dx$.

For strict-side endpoint directions $a,b$ at distances $k,\ell$, their intersection with base $z_0$ has continuous coordinate $T=x_0+[k\ell/(k+\ell)](a+b)$. Thus its membership in a closed halfspace through $y$ depends only on the direction sum, and each subcoupling of the directional volume measures lifts to a subcoupling of the strict-side original volumes. In particular the largest subcoupling mass carried by $a+b=0$ is
$$
\int_{\mathbb R^d}\min\{f_-(a),f_+(-a)\}\,da
=\sum_{k\ge1}|K_{z_0-k}\cap(2x_0-K_{z_0+k})|.
$$
Only one copy of each reflected base pair is counted. If the strict-side total volumes are equal and positive, the choice $x_0=\sum_{\pm,k}(w_{\pm k}/k)c_{\pm k}/\sum_{\pm,k}w_{\pm k}/k$, with $w_{\pm k},c_{\pm k}$ the volumes and centroids of the positive-volume fibers, belongs to $K_{z_0}$ and makes the sum of the directional first moments zero.

c21aa22115d69526:05.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

For $0\le a\le1/(2d)$ and $v\in[0,1]$, let
$$
\begin{aligned}
L_v(x)&=(1-vx)^{d-1}[1-(d+1-dv)x]_+,\\
R_{a,v}(x)&=(1+av+vx)^{d-1}[1-dav-(d+1+dv)x]_+ .
\end{aligned}
$$
The kernels are defined for $x\ge0$ and set to zero beyond the positive-part supports. Let $I_R(a,v)=\int_0^\infty R_{a,v}(x)\,dx$, $J_d(v)=\partial_a I_R(0,v)$ (the right derivative), and $G_d(v)=\int_0^\infty L_v(x)\,dx+I_R(0,v)-1/(d+1)$. Then $J_d$ and $G_d$ are continuous on $[0,1]$ and both vanish at $0$. For $0<v\le1$, with $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+dz/(d+1))^d$,
$$
G_d(v)=\frac{f(v)+f(-v)-2}{dv^2}-\frac1{d+1}.
$$
Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_d&=3d(3d+1)2^{d-3},&
T_d&=\frac{2^{d-3}(9d^2-7d+2)}{d+1},&
B_d&=(d+2)2^{d-4},\\
C_d&=\frac{V_d}{4}+\frac d8+\frac{T_d}{2}+B_d,&
K_d&=\frac{d(2d+1)}{(d+1)^2}\left(1+\frac1{d+1}\right)^{d-2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
\frac{D(a,atv)}{\Gamma}=-\frac{G_d(v)}a-J_d(v)-\frac12+\rho_d(a,v),
\qquad
|\rho_d(a,v)|\le C_d a,\qquad |J_d(v)|\le K_d v .
$$

  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

With the constants $C_d$ and $K_d$ of the uniform deficit expansion, define
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac1{4[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]}\right\}.

$$

$$
In particular $D(a,\beta)\le-\Gamma/4$ for all $0<a\le\varepsilon_d$ and $0\le\beta\le at$.

c22519c29667168e:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ be nonzero vectors with $p_i,-p_i\in\partial K$ for every $i$. $$
\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|\ge \frac49|K|,
$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes planar area. The constant is sharp. Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a triangle with centroid $0$ and, after dropping zero weights and merging repeated oriented chords, the three $H_i$ are the vertex halfplanes through $0$ parallel to the opposite sides, with total weight $1/3$ on each. A balanced opposite pair, or a positive noncollinear triple with one weight $1/2$, has weighted cap area $|K|/2$.

c2528b1460a23da4:01.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be nonempty compact sets, $V$ a linear subspace, $q\ge0$ with $\mathcal H_q(A)<\infty$, and $Z=V+\operatorname{conv} B$. Suppose nonnegative Borel functions $F$ on $\mathbb R^m$ and $g$ on $A$ satisfy $F(a+b)\ge g(a)$ for all $a\in A$, $b\in B$. Then
$$
\int_{(A+B)\setminus Z}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge\int_{A\setminus V}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
For any one compact $P\subseteq A$ contained in an affine subspace $L$ this gives
$$
\int_{A+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q\ge
\int_{P+B}F\,d\mathcal H_q+\int_{A\setminus L}g\,d\mathcal H_q.
$$
The inequalities allow extended integrals and include $q=0$. If $A,B$ lie in $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, the translated source pieces lie in that lattice as actual sum points.

Let $A,B,K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional convex bodies with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$, let $P\subseteq A$ be nonempty compact with $\dim\operatorname{aff}P<d$, and let $v_i\cdot b\le1$ for every $b\in B$ and $i=1,\dots,s$. Write $\sigma_i(x)=\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot x<0\}}$ and $\rho_i(a)=\mathbf1_{\{v_i\cdot a<-1\}}$. For every coordinatewise nondecreasing $\Psi:\{0,1\}^s\to[0,\infty)$, the same baseline $P+B$ gives
$$
2^d\int_K\Psi(\sigma)\,dx
\ge \int_{P+B}\Psi(\sigma)\,dx+\int_A\Psi(\rho)\,da.
$$
This includes unions, intersections, and positive excess above a threshold for the number of missed caps. For compact mixed-lattice source sets on one common integer parity class and finite source measure $\mathcal H_q(A)$, with Borel $K$ containing all actual midpoints, the factor is $2^q$, the integrals use $\mathcal H_q$, and the final integral is over $A\setminus\operatorname{aff}P$.

In the planar case with three nonzero spanning normals $v_0+v_1+v_2=0$, suppose the three caps $v_i\cdot x-z\ge0$ each have raw mixed area $Q$ in the actual fibers $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. $$

\ge \sum_i |(P+B)\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<0\}|+\sum_i|R_i(A)|.
$$

c260aef7098c009e:02.statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^2$ be compact and convex, with integer-fiber length measure $\mu$. Its positive fibers are intervals $K_i=[l_i,u_i]$ of widths $w_i=u_i-l_i$ on the finite consecutive index set $P$. Fix $j\in P$, put $d_i=i-j$, $M=\sum_iw_i$, and let
$$
T_j=\max\left\{\sum_i m_i:0\le m_i\le w_i,\ \sum_i d_i m_i=0\right\}.
$$
For $0<t\le T_j$ let $B_j(t)$ be the interval of continuous centroids of dominated sources $0\le f\le1$ of mass $t$ and base centroid $j$. Let $c_j(t)$ be its midpoint, including the singleton convention. Write $Q_v(t)$ for the maximum of $\sum_i(v_i m_i-m_i^2/2)$ over the same box with centered base moment zero and $\sum_i m_i=t$. With $U=Q_u$ and $V=Q_{-l}$,
$$
 B_j(t)=[-V(t)/t,U(t)/t],\qquad c_j(t)=\frac{U(t)-V(t)}{2t}.
$$
Each optimizer is unique and has the form $m_i=\operatorname{clamp}(v_i-b-\nu d_i,0,w_i)$ for finite multipliers $b,\nu$, where $\operatorname{clamp}(x,0,w)=\min(w,\max(0,x))$. The intervals are nested in decreasing order as $t$ increases and $c_j(0)=(l_j+u_j)/2$ gives a continuous extension.

The functions $U,V$ are continuous finite piecewise quadratics on $[0,T_j]$. On any open interval of one fixed empty/free/full pattern with free set $A$ of at least two indices, set $S=|A|$, $Z=\sum_{i\in A}d_i$ and $ZZ=\sum_{i\in A}d_i^2$. Then $Q_v'=b$ and $Q_v''=-1/(S-Z^2/ZZ)$. If only $j$ is free on an open interval, then $Q_v'=b$ and $Q_v''=-1$. Denote the boundary values at base $j$ of the optimizing upper and lower caps by $b_+=b_U$ and $b_-=-b_V$, respectively. Away from finitely many transition masses they determine the path by
$$
c_j(t)=\frac{1}{2t}\int_0^t[b_+(s)+b_-(s)]\,ds.
$$
If all endpoints are rational, the path has form $At+B+C_0/t$ on finitely many rational mass intervals with rational coefficients, with $C_0=0$ on the first interval. Its range has rational or quadratic-algebraic endpoints with decidable endpoint inclusion. At any rational raw mixed-depth level, one can decide exactly whether a positive-time path point reaches that level in the original measure, using all closed halfspace orientations.

Its positive fibers are $K_i=[l_i,u_i]$, with $w_i=u_i-l_i$ on a consecutive finite integer index set $P$. Fix $j\in P$. Let $T_j$ be the maximum mass of any dominated source of base centroid $j$, equivalently the maximum of $\sum_i m_i$ over $0\le m_i\le w_i$ with $\sum_i(i-j)m_i=0$. Let $c_j(T_j)$ be the midpoint of the interval of continuous centroids of all such maximal-mass sources.

The maximizing allocation $m^*$ is unique. If the original base centroid is $j$, it keeps all fibers. If the base centroid is larger than $j$, it keeps all fibers through $j$, fills the fibers to the right in order of increasing index until the moment is balanced, and discards the remaining right fibers. There is at most one partially filled terminal fiber. If the original base centroid is smaller than $j$, the reflected description holds. In the convex hull of the retained full intervals and the centered subinterval of the partial terminal fiber, if present, the positive integer fibers are exactly these retained intervals. This hull has mixed length $T_j$ and true mixed centroid
$$
\left(j,c_j(T_j)\right),\qquad
c_j(T_j)=\frac{1}{T_j}\sum_i m_i^*\frac{l_i+u_i}{2}.
$$
The original raw closed-halfspace depth at this point exceeds $T_j/3$ when the hull has more than one positive fiber, and is at least $T_j/2$ when it has one. In particular $T_j\ge 3M/4$ implies a positive-mass path point of original raw depth at least $M/4$.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:01.reason: The affine pullback and the representation-preserving evaluations prove exact anchored equivalence, compatible measured sections, Helly preservation, and depth monotonicity on each retained base.
c280bb0dcfd30f3d:01.statement:
For a nonempty finite set $P$ in a real affine space, call $T\subseteq P$ closed if $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$. An anchored representation of $q\in P$ is $q=\sum_{p\in P}\lambda_pp$ with $\lambda_p\ge0$ and $\sum_p\lambda_p=1$. Let $L(P)\subseteq\mathbb R^P$ be the space of scalar functions preserving every such equality. For a basis $1,g_1,\ldots,g_{\ell-1}$ of $L(P)$, the map $\Phi_P(p)=(g_1(p),\ldots,g_{\ell-1}(p))$ is injective, with an affine projection back to $P$. Its image has affine dimension $\ell-1$, preserves exactly the anchored representations and the closed traces, and all representation-preserving functions on $\Phi_P(P)$ are affine restrictions. In particular its relative Helly number equals $h(P)$, the least number of ambient convex sets needed to certify an empty common trace on $P$ from any finite such system.

Fix $d\ge1$. A family of nonempty compact convex sets $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ is compatible if $\sum_p\lambda_p K_p\subseteq K_q$ for every anchored representation of $q$. This is equivalent to being the exact sections of the convex hull of their placed fibers at all sites of $P$. For families of positive $d$-volume let $D_P(K)$ be the maximum, over placed fiber points, of the infimum of normalized mass of containing closed halfspaces, using the sum of fiber $d$-volumes. Let $M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d$ for nonempty $T\subseteq P$. Then, with the same retained fibers,
$$
D_P(K)\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_T(K|_T)
\ \ge\ \frac{M_T}{M_P}\,D_{\Phi_T(T)}(K|_T).
$$
Here $T$ has its inherited placement and the last depth uses its own canonical lift. The closed-minor operation followed by canonical lifting, iterated on an initial $P$, produces only lifts of its nonempty closed subsets up to affine equivalence. For a closed $T$, $h(T)\le h(P)$.

c280bb0dcfd30f3d:03.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$ and $\tau>0$. For a finite nonempty base $P$ let $D_P(K)$ be normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth on the full compatible positive $d$-volume fibers $K$, and let $b_d(P)=\inf_K D_P(K)$ over all such families. Write $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Use one of the following budgets consistently on closed subsets and their canonical lifts.

- For an arbitrary finite base $P$, use its relative Helly number $q(P)=h(P)$.
- For a complete finite affine-lattice base $P$, use the number $q(P)=k(P)$ of occupied parity classes. Each closed subset uses the inherited affine lattice, and each canonical lift uses its complete integer graph realization with the inherited graph lattice.

Suppose $D_P(K)<\tau/q(P)$ for some positive compatible family. Then among the canonical lifts of nonempty closed subsets of $P$ with $b_d(\Phi_U(U))<\tau/q(U)$, choose one with the fewest sites. Write $B=\Phi_U(U)$ for any such choice, using the integer realization in the parity case. It is dependence-connected, $q(B)=q(U)\le q(P)$, every representation-preserving function on $B$ is affine, and $\dim\operatorname{aff}(B)\le h(B)-1$. In the parity case $B$ is complete in its inherited affine lattice, even if its affine rank exceeds the original rank.

On this $B$ the unrestricted infimum $\beta=b_d(B)<\tau/q(B)$ is attained by a compatible family of total volume one with every fiber of positive $d$-volume, and $\beta\ge\gamma_d/|B|>0$. More precisely, for every $0<\delta<\tau/q(B)$, the mass-one sublevel $D_B(K)\le\delta$ has a uniform positive lower bound on all fiber volumes and is sequentially compact for simultaneous fiber Hausdorff convergence after common continuous affine normalizations and affine shears on $B$. For every nonempty proper closed $T\subset B$ every member of this sublevel satisfies
$$
M_T\ \le\ \frac{D_B(K)}{\tau}\,q(T)\ \le\ \frac{\delta}{\tau}\,q(T)\ <\ \frac{q(T)}{q(B)},
\qquad M_T=\sum_{p\in T}|K_p|_d.
$$
For $\tau=\gamma_d$, the Helly case is the auxiliary finite-base reduction. In the parity case an actual mixed-integer body on $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$ with positive total mixed $d$-volume and normalized maximum depth below $\tau/2^n$ supplies a strict bad input on its complete positive-fiber base. This includes $\tau=\gamma_d$ and any fixed $c_0\in(0,1/e)$ by taking $\tau=c_0$.

c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d:01.statement:
Let $g_0,\ldots,g_{m-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence on consecutive indices, with $m\ge1$. Concavity means that its successive differences are nonincreasing. Put $H=\max_i g_i$ and choose any index $j$ with $g_j=H$. For every real $p\ge2$,
$$
(p+1)\sum_i g_i^p-pH\sum_i g_i^{p-1}
\ge \frac{H^p}{2}\left(\frac1{2j+1}+\frac1{2(m-1-j)+1}\right).
$$
The bound allows zero endpoints, a peak at either endpoint, and an arbitrary choice of peak in a plateau.

c3c2ca0e4dcbdc9d:02.statement:
Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{L-1}$ be a nonnegative, nonzero concave sequence on consecutive indices, with $L\ge1$. Put $R=\max_i f_i$ and choose any $j$ with $f_j=R$. For real $p\ge2$ and $0\le c\le R$, set $Q_p(c)=\sum_i(f_i-c)_+^p$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $0\le t<R$ let $[a(t),b(t)]$ be the strict superlevel interval of indices with $f_i>t$, and set
$$
\kappa_j(t)=\frac12\left(\frac1{2(j-a(t))+1}+\frac1{2(b(t)-j)+1}\right).
$$
The function $\kappa_j$ is nondecreasing and $1/L\le\kappa_j(t)\le1$. For $0\le c<R$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_p(c)
&\ge (1-c/R)^{p+1}Q_p(0)
  +(R-c)^{p+1}\int_0^c\frac{\kappa_j(t)}{(R-t)^2}\,dt\\
&\ge (1-c/R)^{p+1}Q_p(0)+\kappa_j(0)\frac{c(R-c)^p}{R}.
\end{aligned}
$$
For $0<c<R$, partition $[0,c]$ at the distinct sequence values in $(0,c)$, writing the endpoints and knots as $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=c$. The integral is exactly
$$
\sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}\kappa_j(s_\ell)
  \left(\frac1{R-t_{\ell+1}}-\frac1{R-t_\ell}\right),
\qquad s_\ell\in(t_\ell,t_{\ell+1}),
$$
and it is zero at $c=0$. At $c=R$ the scaled integral remainder has continuous extension zero. Both inequalities are equalities at $c=0$ and $c=R$, and are identities for every $c$ if $L=1$. The bound with the remainder dropped is strict for $0<c<R$.

c62d1cc13c75171f:01.statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-dimensional simplex, $k\ge1$, with normalized volume $\mu_F$, and let $t$ be one of its barycentric coordinates. For $b\in(0,1)$ put $r=\frac14\min\{b,(1-b)/k\}$. Every continuous nonnegative convex function $f$ on $F$ satisfies
$$
\int_{\{|t-b|\le\eta\}} f\,d\mu_F
\le \frac{2\eta}{r}\int_F f\,d\mu_F,\qquad 0\le\eta\le r.
$$

Let $S$ be a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, and $C_i=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b\}$. Suppose $K$ is a compact convex body with $g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S$ for $0\le\delta<1$. Write $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap C_i|/|S|$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume. For any affine margin $\phi$ with $H=\{x:\phi(x)\ge0\}$, if $\sup_{x\in S}|\phi(x)-(\lambda_i(x)-b)|\le\eta\le(1-\delta)/(4m)$, then
$$
\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap(H\mathbin{\triangle}C_i)|}{|S|}
\le 8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau .
$$
In particular, $|(S\setminus K)\cap H|/|S|\le R_i+8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau$. The affine margin may have any threshold satisfying the stated bound.

For the radial formula used to obtain this bound, let $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap S$, let $\rho$ be the Minkowski gauge of $K-g$, and put $f_j(z)=\rho(z-g)-1$ and $w_j(z)=1-\rho(z-g)^{-d}$ on $F_j$. Each $f_j$ is continuous, convex and nonnegative, and $d(1-\delta)^d f_j\le w_j\le d f_j$. For a measurable $A\subset F_j$, the missing volume on rays from $g$ towards $A$ equals $(|S|/m)\int_A w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$. In particular $\tau=m^{-1}\sum_j\int_{F_j} w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$.

c62d1cc13c75171f:02.reason: The admitted relative-depth theorem checks the canonical vertex caps, nearby margins and compact complement using the same explicit point and the coefficient Γc/4.
c62d1cc13c75171f:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$ and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There is a constant $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ with the following property. Suppose $S$ is a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$ with centroid $g$, $K$ is a compact convex body, and
$$
g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S,\qquad 0\le\delta\le\delta_d.
$$
Assume the centroid of every facet of $S$ belongs to $K$. With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$, there is one $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ such that for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$,
$$
\frac{|K\cap H|}{|K|}\ge\Gamma+\frac{\Gamma c}{4}\tau .
$$
In particular, if $D(K)$ is the maximum normalized ordinary halfspace depth and $\mu_K,\mu_S$ are the normalized uniform laws, then
$$
\sup_{H\ \mathrm{closed\ halfspace}}|\mu_K(H)-\mu_S(H)|
\le \operatorname{TV}(\mu_K,\mu_S)=\tau
\le \frac{4}{\Gamma c}\bigl(D(K)-\Gamma\bigr).
$$

The loss estimates below use the same nested inclusion and facet-centroid contacts before imposing the depth radius $\delta_d$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the barycentric functions of $S$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge b\}|/|S|$. For $0\le\delta<1$ one has $\sum_i R_i\le m\Gamma(1-c)(1-\delta)^{-d}\tau$. Put
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac{1}{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot8m\cdot2^{d+1}}\right\},
\qquad E=8m\eta\,2^{d+1},\qquad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+E\tau\},\qquad
\bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i .
$$
For $\delta\le1/2$, each $L_i$ bounds the deleted fraction relative to $|S|$ for every affine margin within $\eta$ of $\lambda_i-b$ on $S$. For $\delta\le\min\{1/2,c/(4d)\}$, $\bar L\le\Gamma(1-c/2)\tau$. The point in the depth conclusion can be taken with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i(y)=b+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$.

c6aadce19d219a98:01.reason: The beta-step conditional and mixture laws agree with the finite source formula in every coordinate dimension, including the one-point simplex.
c6aadce19d219a98:01.statement: For an integer $m\ge1$, let $\mu_m$ be uniform probability on $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$. Independently draw $W\sim\mu_m$, a uniform index $J\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $R$ with density $m(1-r)^{m-1}$ on $(0,1)$. Write $e_j$ for the standard basis vectors. Then $X=(1-R)W+Re_J$ has law $\mu_m$. Given $J=j$, its law has density $mx_j$ relative to $\mu_m$. For $V=(mW+e_J)/(m+1)$, one has $\mathbb E[X\mid W,J]=V$ and hence $\mathbb E[X\mid V,J]=\mathbb E[X\mid V]=V$.

c6aadce19d219a98:02.reason: The minimum-cell coupling gives the sharp convex-order range and the exact martingale at the endpoint. The reviewed proof adds the affine and slice-affine equality criteria.
c6aadce19d219a98:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $Z$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, and let $I$ be independent and uniform on its vertex indices. For $0\le b\le1$ set $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$. Then $Y_b\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} Z$ if and only if $b\le1/d$, where the order means $\mathbb E\phi(Y_b)\le\mathbb E\phi(Z)$ for every continuous convex $\phi$ on $\Delta_d$. Equivalently the inequality reverses for every continuous concave test.

At $b=1/d$, there is a coupling $(Y,X)$ of $Y_{1/d}$ and $Z$ with $\mathbb E[X\mid Y]=Y$ in which the minimum coordinate value and its unique index agree almost surely. The common minimum has survival function $(1-ds)_+^{d-1}$ for $s\ge0$. In fact for every $b\ge1/d$, $\mathbb E\min_j(Y_b)_j=(1-b)/(d(d-1))$, whereas $\mathbb E\min_j Z_j=1/d^2$.

At $b=0$ every test gives equality. For $0<b<1/d$ equality holds precisely for affine tests. At $b=1/d$ equality holds precisely when the test is affine on every slice $\{x\in\Delta_d:x_i=t/d,\ x_j\ge t/d\text{ for all }j\ne i\}$, for every $i$ and $0\le t\le1$. In particular the minimum is a nonaffine concave equality test at the critical step. When $d=2$ and $b=1/2$ the whole laws agree. For $d\ge3$ the critical comparison is strict for every strictly convex test.

c6aadce19d219a98:03.reason: The stationarity proof uses the exact simplex density equation and dense-grid additivity, with the scope of independent absolutely continuous steps and at least three vertices.
c6aadce19d219a98:03.statement: For an integer $m\ge3$, let $W$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, let $J$ be uniform on its vertex indices, and let $B$ have an absolutely continuous probability density $w$ on $[0,1]$. Assume the three variables are independent. Then $(1-B)W+Be_J$ is uniform on $\Delta_m$ if and only if $w(b)=m(1-b)^{m-1}$ almost everywhere. If an atom at zero is allowed, any mixture of this beta law and the unit mass at zero is stationary. For $m=2$ the constant step $B=1/2$ is also stationary.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:01.reason: A fixed whitening converts the covariance norm to the Euclidean cap law. The fixed-face theorems supply contact rigidity and the maximal occupied-face midpoint argument counts the groups in the inherited lattice.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:01.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine lattice, equal to the lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and let $d\ge1$. At each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, with $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$ is a convex representation. Write $C$ for the canonical convex hull of the lifted fibers, $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$, and $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_z}\,dX)$ for the measured fibers. Put $M=\sum_z|K_z|$, let $g_z$ be the centroid of $K_z$, and define
$$
N=d+1,\qquad
\Sigma=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}\,dX,\qquad
\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},\qquad
f(z,x)=\left(\frac{E_{C_z}(x)}{M}\right)^{1/N}.
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over parameters with positive denominator on $K$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and is zero on the own boundary. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$, the raw buffered depth $b_\varepsilon(p,y)$ is the infimum of $\mu$-masses of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(Z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of the closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (with value $M$ in base rank zero). Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K)=\max_{p\in P,\ y\in K_p}b_\varepsilon(p,y)/M$. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and suppose every old buffered maximizing mark has a proper shifted own section in every nonvertical direction, meaning the shifted plane cuts its own fiber interior. Let $Q=M\beta_\varepsilon$ and $I$ be the sampled bases at which $Q$ is attained. Then $I$ is the full lattice trace of $\operatorname{conv}I$. There are at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ cap groups, with parity counted in the inherited affine lattice of $P$. Each group $i$ is associated with a face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ and an old maximizing source over a sampled base in $\operatorname{relint}F_i$. The sets $J_i=I\cap F_i$ cover $I$. Each group consists of at most $d+1$ nonvertical caps $\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}\}$ of actual mass $Q$, with $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$, $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, and weights $\rho_{ij}>0$ summing to one. They are proper on the group source's own fiber and their thresholds are right upper $Q$-quantiles. Define $P_i(z,x)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot(z,x)$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. Then
$$
P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon f(z,x)\ge0\qquad(z\in F_i,\ x\in C_z).
$$
For every real $z\in F_i$ the zero is a unique own-interior mark $y_z$, every selected buffered quantile constraint is an equality there, and the marks are affine on $F_i$. The bodies $C_z-y_z$ and the positive energy $E_{C_z}(y_z)=E_i$ are constant on that face, so $f(z,y_z)=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:02.reason: Local strictly decreasing right quantiles and the minimum across entire current assigned fibers give the exact moving cover. Positive Hausdorff continuity uses recomputed covariance and preserves the gap at the other bases.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:02.statement:
Take a positive compatible family and fixed energy-only buffered cap groups as in the preceding parity-face theorem. In particular, $\varepsilon>0$ is fixed, $Q$ is the old raw maximum, $I$ is the set of old deepest bases, $J_i$ cover $I$, and the selected caps have fixed normals $N_{ij}=(a_{ij},u_{ij})$ and actual mass $Q$ at thresholds $c_{ij}$. Use the same $P_i,h_i,\rho_{ij}$ as in that theorem. Let $K_z(t)$ be positive compatible bodies on the same bases with $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance as $t\downarrow0$. Write $\mu_t,M_t,\Gamma_t,f_t,b_{\varepsilon,t}$ for their actual measure, mass, covariance norm, energy-only profile and raw buffered depth. Put
$$
A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}),\qquad
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}
[P_i(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon A_i(t)f_t(z,x)].
$$
Then $A_i(t)\to1$, $\alpha_i(t)\to0$, and the minimizing marks approach the finite old contact set $\{(z,y_z):z\in J_i\}$. For each $i,j$ let $c_{ij}(t,q)$ be the right upper $q$-quantile of $\mu_t$ in the fixed normal $N_{ij}$. For small $t$ there is a unique solution $q_i(t)$ near $Q$ to
$$
\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}(t,q_i(t))=h_i+\alpha_i(t).
$$
It tends to $Q$, and for all small $t$ one has
$$
b_{\varepsilon,t}(z,x)\le q_i(t)\quad (z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)),\qquad
M_t\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))\le\max_i q_i(t).
$$

c6bafe9ff5de0861:03.reason: The two-sided radial shell estimate and the positive minimizing-denominator floor yield uniform energy differentiation on compact interior marks. Centered covariance differentiates on the same path.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:03.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $N=d+1$, and let finitely many convex bodies $K_z(t)\subset\mathbb R^d$ move through $K_z=K_z(0)$ as $t\downarrow0$. In each old body choose an interior origin $o_z$, and let $R_z,R_{z,t}$ be the old and moving radial functions about it. Suppose $|R_{z,t}-R_z|\le Ct$ and $(R_{z,t}-R_z)/t\to r_z$ almost everywhere on the sphere. At a regular old boundary point $X=o_z+R_z(\omega)\omega$ set $v_z(X)=-r_z(\omega)n_z(X)\cdot\omega$, with $n_z$ the outward unit normal. This is the signed inward speed. Use endpoint counting measure in dimension one. Let
$$
M=\sum_z|K_z|,\quad D=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS,\quad
J=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}v_z(X)\,dS
$$
with $g_z$ the old centroids, and define $M_t,\Sigma_t,\Gamma_t$ using actual moving masses and within-fiber centroids as in the invariant energy-only buffer. For a compact $U\subset\operatorname{int}K_z$, write $a_y$ for the unique old parameter minimizing the projective energy at $y$, and set
$$
C_z(y)=\int_{\partial K_z}[1+a_y\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}v_z(X)\,dS.
$$
Then, uniformly for $y\in U$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{K_z(t)}(y)&=E_{K_z}(y)-tC_z(y)+o(t),\\
f_t(z,y)&=f(z,y)+t\,\frac{f(z,y)}N
 \left[-\frac{C_z(y)}{E_{K_z}(y)}+\frac DM\right]+o(t),
\end{aligned}
$$
where $f_t(z,y)=(E_{K_z(t)}(y)/M_t)^{1/N}$. The right derivatives at zero satisfy
$$
\dot M=-D,\qquad \dot\Sigma=(D\Sigma-J)/M,\qquad
\dot\Gamma(u)=\frac{u^{\mathsf T}\dot\Sigma u}{2\Gamma(u)}\quad(u\ne0).
$$

c6bafe9ff5de0861:04.reason: Use the energy and covariance derivatives at all old contacts, then localize every new contact minimizer to the finite old zeros. This gives the derivative as their minimum.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:04.statement:
In the exact fixed-cover continuation for the energy-only covariance buffer, assume the compatible path also satisfies the bounded signed radial hypotheses of the uniform marked-energy and covariance lemma. Use its $D,J,C_z(y)$, and for group $i$ write $E_i=E_{K_z}(y_z)$ and $f_i=(E_i/M)^{1/N}$ for the old common energy and profile at its contacts. Put
$$
J_i^{\rm cov}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}J u_{ij}.
$$
Then $A_i(t)=1+t(D-J_i^{\rm cov})/(2M)+o(t)$, and
$$
\alpha_i(t)=t\,\dot\alpha_i+o(t),\qquad
\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon f_i
\left[\min_{z\in J_i}\frac{C_z(y_z)}{NE_i}
+\frac{J_i^{\rm cov}}{2M}-\frac{(N+2)D}{2NM}\right].
$$
In the variant with the old norm held fixed and the unnormalized profile $E^{1/N}$, use the corresponding old cap groups (equivalently rescale the old buffer parameter by $M^{-1/N}$). For its fixed parameter $\varepsilon$ the formula becomes $\dot\alpha_i=\varepsilon E_i^{1/N}\min_{z\in J_i}C_z(y_z)/(NE_i)$.

c6bafe9ff5de0861:05.reason: The same regular moving traces give joint cap differentiation and exact inverse quantile differentiation. The strict descent test uses every group on the same actual path.
c6bafe9ff5de0861:05.statement:
Use the exact fixed-cover continuation and its finite-contact derivative on one actual compatible signed radial path for the energy-only buffer. Put $\beta=Q/M$ and $\dot M=-D$. Suppose for each selected old cap its actual tail has the regular joint expansion
$$
\mu_t\{N_{ij}\cdot(Z,X)\ge c_{ij}+t s\}
=Q-t(L_{ij}+S_{ij}s)+o(t),\qquad S_{ij}>0,
$$
uniformly on bounded $s$ intervals. Here $L_{ij}$ is the first loss of mass at the fixed threshold. A sufficient trace condition is that each selected plane on each old fiber be a proper section, a strict full or empty cut, or a supporting section of zero $(d-1)$-dimensional measure. Under this condition $S_{ij}$ is the sum of proper section measures divided by $\lVert u_{ij}\rVert$, and $L_{ij}$ integrates the signed inward speed on the captured old boundary.

Let $B_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}$ and $\theta_{ij}=(\rho_{ij}/S_{ij})/B_i$. Then the right derivatives of the continued budgets satisfy
$$
\dot q_i=-\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}-\frac{\dot\alpha_i}{B_i},
\qquad
\left.\frac{d}{dt^+}\right|_{0}\frac{q_i(t)}{M_t}
=-\frac{\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i-\beta D}{M}.
$$
If $\sum_j\theta_{ij}L_{ij}+\dot\alpha_i/B_i>\beta D$ for every old group on this one path, then $\beta_\varepsilon(K(t))<\beta$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$.
