The new use is a weighted inverse of actual mark-depth functions. 66947afeef056d3b optimizes log mass at fixed cap-bound marks and does not provide this through-mark depth comparison.
c72585e587868cec:02.statement:
Assume the actual compatible fixed-base bodies and old positive continuous log-normalized parameter $L$ satisfy the finite volume certificate hypotheses of 569a05581be52e0e at a fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular the contact probabilities $\rho_i$ have weights $\sigma_i>0$ summing to one, full means $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ and $L$-means $L_i=L(Y_i)$, and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Each $Y_i$ is an old maximizing mark with raw depth $Q$, strictly below its closed pure-base depth. Let $K_z(t)\to K_z$ be positive compatible bodies in the fixed-base fiber Hausdorff topology as $t\downarrow0$, with mixed volume $dm_t$ and total $M_t$. Define $v(t)=\inf_U Q_t(U)/M_t$ over current positive continuous concave, log-normalized parameters. Choose $U_t$ with $Q_t(U_t)/M_t\le v(t)+t^2$.

Choose a common inward fractional contraction $a_t\to0$, $0\le a_t<1$, of the old fibers about their old centroids $g_z$ so that its image $I_{t,z}$ is contained in $K_z(t)$. Let $T_t(z,X)=(z,g_z+(1-a_t)(X-g_z))$ and $j_t=(1-a_t)^d$. Let $Y_i^t$ be the mean of $(T_t)_\#\rho_i$, and $B_i(t,s)$ its actual raw buffered depth with scalar parameter value $s$. On a common interval of raw depths about $Q$, for all sufficiently small $t$ there is a unique positive inverse $s_i(t,q)$ of this scalar depth. Define $H_t(q)=\sum_i\sigma_i\log(s_i(t,q)/L_i)$ and let $\chi_t$ denote its local inverse. If
$$
\xi_t=-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log U_t\,dX,
$$
then $H_t(Q_t(U_t))\ge\xi_t$ and $Q_t(U_t)\ge\chi_t(\xi_t)$.

Let $h_t=\sum_z|K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}|$ and let $B\ge1$ be a common sampled upper bound for $U_t$. Then $\xi_t\ge-h_t\log B/(Mj_t)$ and $v(t)\ge\chi_t(-h_t\log B/(Mj_t))/M_t-t^2$. More precisely, for positive continuous reference values $L_{\rm ref,t}$ on the sampled moving fibers that converge to $L$ along all convergent sampled marks, we have $\sup_{S_t}(U_t-L_{\rm ref,t})_+\to0$ and
$$
\xi_t\ge-\frac1{Mj_t}\sum_z\int_{K_z(t)\setminus I_{t,z}}\log L_{\rm ref,t}\,dX+o(h_t).
$$
If the moving endpoint on the ray through a regular old boundary point $X$ from $g_z$ is $g_z+(1-b_{z,t}(X))(X-g_z)$, assume $|b_{z,t}(X)|=O(t)$ uniformly and $b_{z,t}(X)/t\to v_z(X)/[n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)]$ surface-almost everywhere, where $v_z$ is a bounded measurable signed inward speed. With $a_t=ct+o(t)$ and $H_z(X)=n_z(X)\cdot(X-g_z)$, containment gives $cH_z-v_z\ge0$ and
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\xi_t}{t}\ge
c_{\rm col}:=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\log L(z,X)[v_z(X)-cH_z(X)]\,dS.
$$

If, independently, $H_t(Q+tr)=t(A_0 r+B_0)+o(t)$ uniformly for bounded $r$, with $A_0>0$, and $\liminf\xi_t/t\ge c_0$, then $\liminf (Q_t(U_t)-Q)/t\ge(c_0-B_0)/A_0$. If also $M_t=M-tD+o(t)$, then
$$
\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(t)-Q/M}{t}
\ge\frac{(c_0-B_0)/A_0+(Q/M)D}{M}.
$$

$$

v(s)=
\begin{cases}1,&s\le1,\\ (s+1)/(2s),&s\ge1,\end{cases}
$$

$$

external_dependencies: Linear coarea formula on each d-dimensional fiber, with normal Jacobian |u|.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:01.reason: 0366ccb8fa1881a1 supplies the hinge differential and c343c9f3dc96957e supplies coarea. The quadratic moment, the signed scalar chain rule and its two simultaneous scaling actions are additional and are proved directly.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:01.statement:
Let $\mu$ be the sum of Lebesgue $d$-volume on finitely many compact full-dimensional convex fibers, $d\ge1$. For $L=a\cdot z+u\cdot x-b$ with $u\ne0$, put $H=\{L\ge0\}$, $c=\mu(H)$, $\Psi=\int L_+\,d\mu$, and $T=\int L_+^2\,d\mu$. The last two functions are continuously differentiable in the affine margin parameters, with $D\Psi[\dot L]=\int_H\dot L\,d\mu$ and $DT[\dot L]=2\int_H L\dot L\,d\mu$. Call a cap regular if on every fiber the cut plane meets its interior, is strictly separated from it, or meets it in a supporting section of zero $(d-1)$-measure. At a regular cap let $\tau=\sum_z\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{K_z\cap\{L=0\}}/\lVert u\rVert$, with the base label attached, so $Dc[\dot L]=\int\dot L\,d\tau$. For a $C^1$ cost $\Phi(c,\Psi,T)$ its derivative is the affine moment of the signed measure
$$
\Phi_c\tau+\Phi_\Psi\mu|_H+2\Phi_T L\mu|_H.
$$
An invertible continuous affine change with common absolute fiber determinant $\Delta$ and a unimodular change of integer bases sends the moments of the same margin to $(\Delta c,\Delta\Psi,\Delta T)$. Multiplication of the margin by $s>0$ sends them to $(c,s\Psi,s^2T)$.

cb4b6b63cebf7744:02.reason: Use the cap-gradient construction in c343c9f3dc96957e for the finite positive fibers and a fixed nonvertical margin. Nearby ordinary coarea sections project onto each limiting cutting plane with area Jacobians tending to one. Their limit measures on a supporting facet have density in [0,1]. A convex combination giving a chosen Clarke covector uses the same density for its mass, base moment and continuous moment; proper sections keep full density. This is exactly the asserted consistent affine differential, without a constant-density restriction on a supporting trace.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:02.statement: At supporting-facet contacts of polytopal fibers, an effective coarea section measure with density in [0,1] on supporting traces represents the corresponding Clarke cap-mass differential, consistently across the components of a selected affine-parameter covector.

cb4b6b63cebf7744:03.reason: 290ddd8516d76865 uses related beta section geometry for depth bounds. It does not determine the two homogeneities or the full affine gradient of these costs.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:03.statement:
Suppose a cap is strictly empty on all but one $d$-simplex fiber, $d\ge1$, on which its affine margin $L$ is strictly positive at just one vertex and strictly negative at the others. Let $c$ be its mass, $H$ the positive apex margin, $\Psi=\int_{L>0}L\,d\mu$ and $T=\int_{L>0}L^2\,d\mu$. Then for every real $p>-1$,
$$
\int_{L>0}L^p\,d\mu=cH^p\frac{\Gamma(p+1)\Gamma(d+1)}{\Gamma(d+p+1)}.
$$
Consequently $R=cT/\Psi^2=\kappa_d=2(d+1)/(d+2)$ identically on the open parameter region of these sign conditions. Every smooth cost on the positive moment orthant with source degree $h$ under common scaling and margin degree $k$ under $(c,\Psi,T)\mapsto(c,s\Psi,s^2T)$ has the form $\Phi=c^{h-k}\Psi^k f(R)$. On the stated region,
$$
\Phi=f(\kappa_d)c^h[H/(d+1)]^k,\qquad D\Phi=(h\Phi/c)Dc+(k\Phi/H)DH.
$$
An arbitrary smooth scalar cost of these three moments has its differential in the span of $Dc,DH$ there, and the same holds for smooth costs of any fixed finite collection of positive-order moments.

cb4b6b63cebf7744:04.reason: The accepted hinge theorem already identifies the same geometric equation and proves its covariance equivalence. The new implication derives it for every nonzero margin-degree moment cost, conditional on the stated stress equations and the disappearance of the off-fiber covector.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:04.statement: For a canonical centroid vertex cap of a simplex fiber with apex $v$, centroid $g$ and apex margin $H=u\cdot(v-g)>0$, fix a positive definite matrix $A$ and impose $u^\top A u=1$. Consider the cap's stationary fixed-source cover equations for a smooth homogeneous cap-moment cost $\Phi$ of margin degree $k$, with objective multiplier $\alpha_0$. Assume the other fibers contribute zero cap mass and zero combined multiplied section covector to these equations, and all positively weighted contacts of this cap are at its own centroid. If $\alpha_0 k\Phi\ne0$, then $v-g=H A u$. For all canonical cap types of this simplex the geometric equations hold exactly when $A$ is a positive scalar multiple of its uniform volume covariance.

cb4b6b63cebf7744:05.reason: aaef76e8cbfd4465 constructs a hinge stress at the common simplex covariance. This construction works in any fixed quadratic metric for pure section objectives and treats scalar normalization with a different exponent.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:05.statement:
Consider a finite cover with one canonical centroid cap of each vertex type of every positive simplex fiber, all strictly empty on every other fiber. For a smooth cap-moment cost $\Phi$ of margin degree zero and source degree $h$ with $h\Phi>0$ on every cap, the fixed-source cap-cover stationarity equations admit an objective multiplier one, zero budget and metric multipliers, and a centroid contact for each fiber, in any fixed positive definite quadratic normalization of the continuous normals. On each fiber the local contact weights are proportional to $S_i=dc/H_i$ and the coverage multiplier is $(h\Phi/c)\sum_i S_i$.

More generally replace the quadratic normalization by $N(c,\Psi,T)=1$ with source and margin degrees $h_N,k_N$ and $k_N\ne0$. Let $F$ have degrees $h_F,k_F$, and let both shape factors be positive at $\kappa_d$. On the strict simplex cone region, the normalization is regular and the reduced cost is
$$
F_{\mathrm{eff}}(c)=f_F(\kappa_d)f_N(\kappa_d)^{-k_F/k_N}c^\rho,
\qquad \rho=h_F-k_Fh_N/k_N.
$$
With objective multiplier one, the normalization multiplier $-k_FF/(k_NN)$ leaves the section coefficient $\rho F_{\mathrm{eff}}(c)/c$. When $\rho>0$, the canonical cover has a normal zero-budget stress with equal local contact weights and coverage multiplier $(d+1)(\rho F_{\mathrm{eff}}/c)dc/H$ on each fiber. For $\rho=0$ the reduced differential is zero.

cb4b6b63cebf7744:06.reason: The sharp six-cap census in 9d4d414e0693f328 depends only on the normalized budget and actual cover, so applies to the stated smooth homogeneous cost. The contacts of each cap with positive multiplier are its own centroid. For the first-fiber e1 cap the other triangle has a unique maximizer (2,0) in its continuous direction. A zero-area other-fiber trace is therefore either strictly empty or supporting at only that point, with zero H¹ section measure. The regular coarea formula gives zero for the whole other-fiber cap and budget covectors. The local metric necessity in the new :04 theorem now requires v−g=H A u whenever α_0 kΦ≠0. Here v−g=(2/3,−1/3) has coordinate ratio −1/2 whereas A e1 has ratio −1/5. Since k and f(κ₂) are nonzero and c,Ψ>0 on the cap, a positive objective multiplier is impossible.
cb4b6b63cebf7744:06.statement: Let K_0=conv(0,e_1,e_2), K_1=diag(2,1/2)K_0 and take their lifted convex hull at z=0,1. For the fixed-source six-cap problem at normalized budget 2/9, with u^T A u=1 for A=(1/144)[[20,−4],[−4,5]], no positive-objective-multiplier stress exists for a smooth homogeneous Φ with k≠0 and f(κ_2)≠0, including caps supporting the other fiber.

cb7ea417552f0084:01.reason: Specialize accepted max-affine duality to one packet (t,y). Tests with ℓ(y)≤0 are automatic and positive tests normalize to ℓ(y)=1, so feasibility is exactly t≤inf_u G(u). Coercivity follows from an inner ball about y. Equality forces the indicator off the hinge's null plane. At the centroid G(u) attains |K| exactly when the hinge's underlying affine function is nonnegative on K. Away from the centroid the maximizing cap is proper, and different normalized proper hinge planes would give different indicators on an open subset of int K. The cited pending note 49e262af8d182671 §1 gives this same hinge calculation independently.
cb7ea417552f0084:01.statement: For a convex body K in R^d, d≥1, and y∈int K, put T_K(y)=max{∫_K f: 0≤f≤1, ∫_K(x−y)f=0}. This value equals the attained minimum of G(u)=∫_K[1+u·(x−y)]_+. The unique maximizing density is the indicator almost everywhere of the corresponding cap K∩{1+u·(x−y)≥0}. At the centroid the cap is all of K and the compact hinge optimizer set U is −(K−y)^polar; elsewhere the optimizer is unique.

cb7ea417552f0084:02.reason: Uniform hinge expansion on the common compact optimizer set gives the moving-mark derivative and the centroid gauge. The quotient uses actual physical radial losses.
cb7ea417552f0084:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y,o\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $K_\varepsilon$ be nested compact convex bodies for $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $K_0=K$. Suppose that for some $C\ge0$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
$$
o+(1-C\varepsilon)(K-o)\subseteq K_\varepsilon\subseteq K.
$$
For $x\in\partial K$, write the radial endpoint of $K_\varepsilon$ on the ray from $o$ through $x$ as $o+(1-t_\varepsilon(x))(x-o)$. At a regular boundary point $x$, let $n(x)$ be its unique outward unit normal and set $dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}$ on $\partial K$. Assume that for a bounded measurable $v$,
$$
\frac{t_\varepsilon(x)}{\varepsilon}\longrightarrow
\frac{v(x)}{n(x)\cdot(x-o)}
\qquad\text{for $dS$ almost every }x.
$$
Then $v\ge0$ almost everywhere. Take $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ for a fixed $w\in\mathbb R^d$. For a body $L$ and $q\in\operatorname{int}L$, let
$$
T_L(q)=\max\left\{\int_L f(x)\,dx:\ 0\le f\le1,\ f\text{ measurable},\
                       \int_L(x-q)f(x)\,dx=0\right\}.
$$
Set $T=T_K(y)$ and let $U$ be the compact nonempty set of minimizers of $G_0(u)=\int_K[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+\,dx$, where $[a]_+=\max(a,0)$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, $y_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{int}K_\varepsilon$. The following right derivative exists, and the minimum is attained:
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=\min_{u\in U}\left\{
-\int_{\partial K}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{1}
$$
When $y$ differs from the centroid $g_K$, $U$ is a singleton. When $y=g_K$, put $V=|K|$, $D=\int_{\partial K}v\,dS$ and $B=\int_{\partial K}(x-y)v(x)\,dS(x)$. For the Minkowski gauge $p_{K-y}(z)=\inf\{t\ge0:z\in t(K-y)\}$, (1) becomes
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}T_{K_\varepsilon}(y_\varepsilon)
=-D-p_{K-y}(-B-Vw).
\tag{2}
$$
The ordinary centroid satisfies $g_{K_\varepsilon}=y-\varepsilon B/V+o(\varepsilon)$. The derivative in (2) equals $-D$ exactly when $w=-B/V$, and is strictly smaller otherwise. In dimension $1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints. The formula allows hinge hyperplanes incident with vertices, edges, and supporting facets; it does not require a differentiable cutting section.

cb7ea417552f0084:03.reason: At the centroid the active hinge set is the negative polar, whose support gives the exact gauge penalty. The centroid velocity is −B/V and is the unique penalty-free velocity.
cb7ea417552f0084:03.statement: Under the erosion hypotheses of §§1–3, at y=g_K let V=|K|, D=∫_{∂K}v, B=∫_{∂K}(x−y)v, and p_{K−y} be the Minkowski gauge. Then T' = −D−p_{K−y}(−B−Vw) and g_{Kε}=y−εB/V+o(ε). Equality T'=−D holds exactly when w=−B/V; all other w give a strict extra loss.

cb7ea417552f0084:04.reason: Accepted 8ea29efd36f51d69 (1) gives the feasible barycenter interval for each mass on [0,1]. Affine rescaling to [L,R] gives [L+t/2,R−t/2] at mass t, hence largest mass 2 min(y−L,R−y). Substituting the displayed paths and simplifying yields both formulas.
cb7ea417552f0084:04.statement: For Kε=[−1+εl,1−εr], l,r≥0, and mark yε=εw with fixed real w, for all sufficiently small ε the exact retained mass is T=2−2ε max(l−w,r+w), with derivative −(l+r)−|r−l+2w|.

external_dependencies: Gauss–Green theorem for a Lipschitz vector field on a convex body.
cb7ea417552f0084:05.reason: Affine change of variables preserves the mark moment constraint. Gauss–Green with the Lipschitz hinge gives the boundary calibration using the cap's barycenter y.
cb7ea417552f0084:05.statement: For Kε=p+(1−ε)(K−p), p∈K, and yε=p+(1−ε)(y−p), one has exactly T_{Kε}(yε)=(1−ε)^d T_K(y). Its physical inward normal speed is v=(x−p)·n(x), and for any old optimal hinge u the integral of [1+u·(x−y)]_+v over ∂K is T_K(y)[d+u·(y−p)]; the derivative is −dT_K(y).

cb7ea417552f0084:06.reason: The physical derivative and total mass loss give the quotient rows, with fixed-baseline averaging and a conditional finite-path envelope stated separately.
cb7ea417552f0084:06.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, $n\ge0$, and let the positive-volume $d$-dimensional fibers $K_{z,\varepsilon}$, $z\in P$, be those of an actual nested convex deformation with fixed measured sites $P$. Assume each fiber satisfies the homothet and almost-everywhere radial speed hypotheses of the physical retained-mass derivative theorem, with old fiber $K_z$ and inward speed $v_z$. Let
$$
M_\varepsilon=\sum_{z\in P}|K_{z,\varepsilon}|,\qquad
M=M_0,\qquad D_{\rm mix}=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS .
$$
Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$ and prescribe $y_\varepsilon=y+\varepsilon w+o(\varepsilon)$ in that fiber. Let $U_p$ be the old optimizing hinge set for $T=T_{K_p}(y)$ and put $\tau=T/M$. The right derivative is
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{0+}
\frac{T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y_\varepsilon)}{M_\varepsilon}
=\frac1M\min_{u\in U_p}\left\{
\tau D_{\rm mix}
-\int_{\partial K_p}[1+u\cdot(x-y)]_+v_p(x)\,dS(x)-T\,u\cdot w
\right\}. \tag{6}
$$
It is nonnegative exactly when every row in braces is nonnegative. Off the centroid there is a single row. At $y=g_{K_p}$ the criterion is exactly
$$
\tau D_{\rm mix}-D_p-p_{K_p-y}(-B_p-|K_p|w)\ge0,\qquad
D_p=\int_{\partial K_p}v_p\,dS,\quad
B_p=\int_{\partial K_p}(x-y)v_p\,dS .
\tag{7}
$$
When $K_p$ is a polytope and $y=g_{K_p}$, the minimum can be taken at the finitely many vertices of $U_p=\{u:1+u\cdot(a-y)\ge0\text{ for every vertex }a\text{ of }K_p\}$. These are linear response rows when the actual physical speeds and prescribed velocity depend linearly on deformation parameters.

One actual setting for such averaging is the single-baseline case of accepted fact 84cd8a85417b0d7a. Use one fixed continuous-in-normal, affine-in-base support baseline satisfying its majorization hypotheses; average the nonnegative convex cut fields on that baseline before constructing the body. For a Borel probability average, assume a nonempty compact metric field parameter space and joint continuity of the fields, and average prescribed velocities integrable in that parameter. The response in (6) is then the average of individual responses off the centroid; at the centroid it is the minimum of the averaged rows.

For a conditional use of (6), define depth as the infimum of the physical mixed masses of closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark, and deepest points as the maximum-depth points on $\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_{p,\varepsilon}$. For this maximum, define $T_L(q)$ at boundary marks by the same mass and moment constraints; it is zero there since a supporting hyperplane through $q$ is Lebesgue-null and every feasible density with barycenter $q$ must be concentrated on that hyperplane. Suppose the secondary maximum $S(\varepsilon)$ of $T_{K_{p,\varepsilon}}(y)/M_\varepsilon$ among deepest points exists for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$. Assume a fixed nonempty finite list of paths $(p_j,y_j(\varepsilon))$, each deepest for all such $\varepsilon$, with $p_j\in P$, $y_j(0)\in\operatorname{int}K_{p_j}$ and $y_j(\varepsilon)=y_j(0)+\varepsilon w_j+o(\varepsilon)$. Assume every secondary maximizer for small $\varepsilon>0$ lies on a listed path. Let $\tau_j=T_{K_{p_j}}(y_j(0))/M$ and $b_j$ be the derivative (6) on path $j$. Then
$$
S(\varepsilon)=\tau_*+\varepsilon\max_{j:\tau_j=\tau_*}b_j+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad \tau_*=\max_j\tau_j .
\tag{8}
$$
This gives the finite right derivative at zero if and only if $\tau_*=S(0)$, equivalently if at least one listed path begins at an old secondary maximizer. Without this equality, (8) is the right-hand expansion about the branch limit.

cb7ea417552f0084:07.reason: Use the fixed-baseline realization of the accepted response theorem. The actual radial speed averages pointwise, giving a linear off-centroid response and a minimum of linear rows at the centroid.
cb7ea417552f0084:07.statement: For the one-source fixed-supporting-slope averaged cut-field family, averaging the field and marked-point velocities makes the normalized retained derivative linear off the centroid, and a minimum of linear rows at the centroid. In the polyhedral centroid case the rows are finite.

cb7ea417552f0084:08.reason: The symmetric interval erosion gives a neutral two-cap cover and zero retained-ratio derivative at a quadratically drifting mark whose depth is strictly suboptimal.
cb7ea417552f0084:08.statement: Even with an actual nested convex-cut erosion, exact neutrality of an old critical cover and zero first derivative of the normalized retained mass on a prescribed path through the old deepest point do not imply that the path remains deepest. For any $n\ge0$, take $[-1/4,1/4]^n\times[-1,1]$ with only measured base $0$ and continuous dimension $1$, and impose the cuts $x+\varepsilon\le1$ and $-x+\varepsilon\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ the old covering halfspaces $x\ge0$ and $x\le0$ each still have half the mixed mass. The mark $(0,\varepsilon^2)$ has zero first derivative of normalized retained mass at zero, but its raw depth is $1-\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2$, strictly smaller than the new deepest depth $1-\varepsilon$.

cb7ea417552f0084:09.reason: Use the finite-path part of the accepted response theorem with the same deepest paths and velocities. The expansion starts at the maximum old value among the listed branches. It gives the derivative at the old global maximum exactly when some listed branch starts there.
cb7ea417552f0084:09.statement: Suppose finitely many actual deepest paths y_j(ε) with finite velocities represent all maximizers of T/Mε on the new deepest set for every small ε>0. The maximum of their retained ratios has right-hand expansion with constant equal to the largest limiting old ratio among the paths and linear coefficient the largest (19) derivative among paths tied at that value. This is a right derivative of the old global secondary optimum if an old secondary maximizer is reached by at least one of the branches.

cbd731cd19c40abd:01.reason: 2b4d031c54005638 uses true facets of a planar triangle and erodes by the other endpoint in a joint clipping chart. The displayed enclosure is available in every dimension for arbitrary actual K, retains separate barycentric upper bounds, and has an exact volume and attainment when K is aligned. This extends the equal-threshold calculation in 909e13cc5d1371df and source eb88c1c4c388daab §2.
cbd731cd19c40abd:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero. Set $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$ and $V=|T|$. Let $A,K$ be full-dimensional convex bodies. cd833c78fb705a2e:01.reason: The finite cover is used on a positive-mass closed convex remainder. Continuity and the vanishing tail supply finite trimming thresholds for positive alpha. The abstract hypothesis applies to that remainder even when the initial support is unbounded.
cd833c78fb705a2e:01.statement:
Let $D\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^D$ with convex support $K=\operatorname{supp}\mu$, and suppose every affine hyperplane has zero $\mu$-mass. Assume there is a fixed $g>0$ such that every closed convex subset $L\subseteq K$ of positive $\mu$-mass contains a point $y$ satisfying $\mu(L\cap H)\ge g\mu(L)$ for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$.

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be a finite cover of $K$ by closed halfspaces with nonzero normals, with $m\ge1$, and let $A_i=\mu(H_i)$. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\mu(K)\le\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{g},
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
\tag{1}
$$

For ordinary volume on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$, write $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(K)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$. Then (1) holds with $g=\gamma_D$ and $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$. In particular, for $a=\min_i A_i$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a.
\tag{2}
$$
Arrange the cap masses in decreasing order and append zeros if $m<3$. For $D\ge2$,
$$
A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V,
\tag{3}
$$
where $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$. For $D=1$, $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

cd833c78fb705a2e:02.reason: Set the measure to ordinary volume on the convex body. Accepted 6769574fc1bd9f8d at full mass on each positive-volume closed convex restriction supplies the depth premise. This ordinary formula has identical hypotheses and conclusion at eb88c1c4c388daab §3 (7) and 64b80eee72258d21 §1 (1).
cd833c78fb705a2e:02.statement: Let $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$ be a convex body of volume $V$, where $D\ge1$, and let $m\ge1$ closed halfspaces with nonzero normals cover $K$. For $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$, every $\alpha\ge0$ satisfies $\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \alpha/\gamma_D\ge V$.

cd833c78fb705a2e:03.reason: Take alpha equal to the least cap mass. Then the positive-part sum is the sum of all cap masses minus m times that least mass. For D=2, gamma_2=4/9, and for D≥3 the reciprocal gamma_D is strictly less than 3.
cd833c78fb705a2e:03.statement: For the same ordinary cover, $a=\min_{1\le i\le m}A_i$ satisfies $\sum_i A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a$. For $m=D+1$ the coefficient is $D+1-1/\gamma_D$, strictly greater than one when $D\ge3$. For $D=2$ and $m=3$ the coefficient is $3/4$.

cd833c78fb705a2e:04.reason: Use the third-largest cap mass for alpha. The two displayed differences are nonnegative even with ties. For m<3, alpha is zero and the union bound gives the padded inequality. The matching assertion at eb88c1c4c388daab §4.2 (12) assumes m≥3, so its scope is a strict specialization. The conclusion controls masses from the full cover and makes no assertion that its three largest caps cover the body.
cd833c78fb705a2e:04.statement: For $D\ge2$, order the ordinary cap masses $A_{(1)}\ge A_{(2)}\ge A_{(3)}\ge\cdots$, appending zeros if $m<3$. Then $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V$, with $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$.

cd833c78fb705a2e:05.statement: For $D=1$, the two largest ordinary cap masses, with a zero appended if $m=1$, satisfy $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

cd9374750b11bd94:04.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V>0$ and volume centroid zero. Let $0<r\le s$, and for $u\ne0$ define $F_u(t)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge t\}|/V$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

For every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
r^dF_u(t/r)+s^dF_u(-t/s)\ge\Phi_d(r,s).
$$
If $d\ge2$ and $s>r$, then $\Phi_d(r,s)>2\Gamma_d r^d$. For each fixed $u\ne0$ the minimum of the left side over $t\in\mathbb R$ is at most $r^d$. It equals $r^d$ and is attained at a finite threshold if $s\ge dr$, which includes every $0<r\le s$ in dimension one.

For the supplied array with just $rK$ at base $-1$ and $sK$ at base $1$, the raw source depth at $(0,0)$ is at least $V\Phi_d(r,s)$, and is exactly $Vr^d$ if $s\ge dr$. Here raw source depth is the infimum, over closed ambient halfspaces containing $(0,0)$, of the sum of the volumes captured from the two supplied sources.

cd9374750b11bd94:05.reason: The two retained endpoint copies are at distinct integer bases and the centroid midpoint of their Minkowski sum lies in the retained middle copy. Each containing halfspace pays the accepted two-endpoint bound and the full-mass centroid bound on the disjoint middle fiber.
cd9374750b11bd94:05.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be full-dimensional, compact and convex with volume centroid zero and volume $V>0$. Suppose that for $p\in\mathbb Z^n$, $v\in\mathbb Z^n\setminus\{0\}$, $a_-,a_+\in\mathbb R^d$ and $0<r\le s$, the actual fibers $C_{p-v}$ and $C_{p+v}$ contain $a_-+rK$ and $a_++sK$, respectively. Put $g=(a_-+a_+)/2$ and $q=(r+s)/2$. Then $g+qK\subseteq C_p$.

Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $c_d=(2\Gamma_d)^{1/d}$. Define
$$
\Phi_d(r,s)=
\begin{cases}
r, & d=1,\\
\left[r c_d+\dfrac{s-r}{d-1}(1-c_d)\right]^d, & d\ge2,\ r\le s\le dr,\\
r^d, & d\ge2,\ s\ge dr.
\end{cases}
$$
The two $d\ge2$ branches agree at $s=dr$.

Every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(p,g)$ captures total $d$-volume at least
$$
V\bigl[\Phi_d(r,s)+\Gamma_d q^d\bigr]
$$
from the three retained copies on the distinct bases $p-v,p,p+v$. In particular this lower bounds the raw depth of $(p,g)$ for $C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$.

cdad0ee8b68e978a:01.reason: The proof deletes every zero-volume trace on a fixed positive fiber simultaneously. The closed union of the remaining traces contains the fiber interior by the almost-everywhere cover and therefore contains the boundary as well. e81d0f726880ea4a:05 is the specialization to the weight δ on a face supplied by c4532e797cea64f9.
cdad0ee8b68e978a:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Suppose finitely many closed halfspaces $H_1,\dots,H_N$ cover $K$ up to a Lebesgue-null set. Write $J_+=\{j:|K\cap H_j|_d>0\}$. Then $K\subset\bigcup_{j\in J_+}H_j$. The same holds if some $H_j$ are the whole space or the empty set.

In particular, if $|K\cap H_i|_d=0$ and $F_i=K\cap\partial H_i$ is a supporting face, then for every nonnegative $\mathcal H^{d-1}$-measurable $w$ on $F_i$,
$$
\int_{F_i}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
\le\sum_{j\in J_+}\int_{F_i\cap H_j}w\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$
For $d=1$ use counting measure. This applies separately on every positive fiber of a finite closed ambient mixed cover.

cdad0ee8b68e978a:02.reason: The exact ratio is 1/(2ε). Both positive recipients are proper, complementary, and belong to a positively balanced cover. Actual common minimizing-cap hypotheses and small-budget restrictions are outside this example.
cdad0ee8b68e978a:02.statement: There is no universal constant bounding the total length of positive-area recipient traces on an empty supporting face of a planar triangle by the sum of the recipients' own section lengths, even when the family covers the triangle, both recipients cut it properly, and the three inward unit normals have a strictly positive dependence. More precisely, for $0<\varepsilon<1$ take $K=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1)\}$, $H_0=\{y\ge0\}$, $H_+=\{y\ge-1+\varepsilon\}$ and $H_-=\{y\le-1+\varepsilon\}$. The face $F_0=K\cap\partial H_0$ has length $2$ and the two traces on it have lengths $2,0$. The recipient cap areas are $1-\varepsilon^2,\varepsilon^2$, and their own section lengths sum to $4\varepsilon$.

cf1b9ba5ada0a5ef:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $v_0,\ldots,v_d$ span $\mathbb R^d$ with sole linear dependence generated by $\sum_{i=0}^d v_i=0$. Let $A,K,B$ be convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ satisfying $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$ and $B\subseteq\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\text{ for all }i\}$. Write $|\cdot|$ for $d$-volume, $a=|A|$, and $b=|B|$. Define
$$
R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{x:v_j\cdot x<-1\},\qquad
Z_i=K\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{x:v_j\cdot x<0\},\qquad r_i=|R_i|.
$$
For every $i$ with $r_i>0$, $(R_i+B)/2\subseteq Z_i$ and $|Z_i|\ge2^{-d}(r_i^{1/d}+b^{1/d})^d$. The $Z_i$ are pairwise disjoint. For every subset $J\subseteq\{i:r_i>0\}$,
$$
\left|K\cap\bigcap_{\ell\notin J}\{x:v_\ell\cdot x<0\}\right|
\ge 2^{-d}\sum_{i\in J}(r_i^{1/d}+b^{1/d})^d.
$$
The intersection on the left is $K$ if $J$ is the full index set. With $U_j=|A\cap\{x:v_j\cdot x\ge-1\}|$, one also has $r_i\ge a-\sum_{j\ne i}U_j$.

In the planar case, place $A,K,B$ at the only positive-area integer fibers $-1,0,1$. If the three ambient caps $\{(z,x):v_i\cdot x\ge z\}$ have common mixed area $Q$ and zero captures on $B$, then for distinct $i,j$ with $r_i,r_j>0$ and remaining index $\ell$,
$$
|K|-Q+U_\ell\ge\frac{(\sqrt{r_i}+\sqrt b)^2+(\sqrt{r_j}+\sqrt b)^2}{4}.
$$

There are s≤2^n groups of nonvertical original auxiliary outward caps of mass <T, each a minimal positive continuous-normal dependence of rank k_i−1 and size k_i≤d+1 with positive weights summing to one. Their projected inequalities a_i·z≤h_i, a_i≠0, jointly exclude P. Each group has an attained real contact q_i=(r_i,y_i) where its own inequalities are tight and every selected inequality is nonpositive. There are expanded offsets β_i>h_i and distinct witnesses p_i∈P with a_i·p_i=β_i and a_j·p_i<β_j for j≠i. Witness parities are distinct, so s is at most the number of occupied parities of P.

d332d092619053f4:02.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K_1,\ldots,K_r$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$. Write $S_K$ for the pushforward of $\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{\partial K}$ by the almost everywhere unique outer unit normal. For $\lambda_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, let $M=\sum_j\lambda_jK_j$. For any finite nonnegative Borel measure $\nu$ on the sphere and constants $a_j\ge0$ with $S_{K_j}\ge a_j\nu$ for every $j$,
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j a_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\nu.
$$
For $\sigma=\sum_j S_{K_j}$ and $f_j=dS_{K_j}/d\sigma$, one also has
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j f_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\sigma.
$$
In particular, every common submeasure of $S_A,S_B$ is dominated by $S_{(1-t)A+tB}$ for $0\le t\le1$. This applies to the greatest common submeasure $S_A\wedge S_B$, whose density relative to $S_A+S_B$ is the minimum of the two densities. The coefficient one in the common-submeasure conclusion is sharp, and homothetic bodies attain equality in the density bound.

d358c029b6047209:01.reason: The one-coordinate closed-interval comparison and induction prove the exact subset sum for every actual compact convex cap. e4ef1ac154c5d280 compares a fine measure to a cell-rounded continuous model using a containing-box mesh error. It does not state this actual quotient-measure error or the corresponding full-rank and degenerate cap scopes. No accepted premise is used.
d358c029b6047209:01.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $d\ge0$. In any fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates, let $\pi_I$ delete integer coordinates indexed by $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$. For a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, including the empty set, put $A_I(K)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I K)$, where $\mu_{j,d}$ sums $d$-volume over the $\mathbb Z^j$ fibers. Use $\mu_{0,d}=\operatorname{vol}_d$ and count the nonempty singleton in dimension zero. Then
$$
|\mu_{n,d}(K)-\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(K)|\le \sum_{\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}} A_I(K).
$$
In particular, every closed ambient halfspace $H$ satisfies $\mu_{n,d}(C\cap H)\ge \operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(C\cap H)-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}A_I(C)$. Lower-dimensional sets and boundary fibers are included.

d358c029b6047209:03.statement:
Let $n\ge1,d\ge0,D=n+d$ and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body. Work in fixed unimodular integer-base coordinates and use the actual projected mixed volumes $A_I(C)=\mu_{n-|I|,d}(\pi_I C)$. Put $M=\mu_{n,d}(C)>0$, $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(C)$, $E=\sum_{I\ne\varnothing} A_I(C)$, $V_i=\operatorname{vol}_{D-1}(\pi_{\{i\}}C)$, and $\Gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$ for $j\ge1$, $\Gamma_0=1$.

For the ordinary centroid $c$ and any real displacement $y=c+(\delta,0)$, every containing closed halfspace $H$ has ordinary cap volume at least $\Gamma_DV-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i$, and $V_i\le\sum_{I\ni i}A_I(C)$. In particular, round the integer coordinates of $c$ independently to nearest integers with deterministic ties, leaving the other coordinates fixed. At the resulting $y$ every containing closed halfspace has raw mixed mass at least
$$
\Gamma_DV-E-\sum_i|\delta_i|V_i\ \ge\
B_\delta:=\Gamma_D M-\sum_{I\ne\varnothing}
(\Gamma_D+1+\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|)A_I(C).
$$
If $B_\delta>0$, this $y$ belongs to the actual mixed set $S$ and to its convex hull. Let $B$ be the same expression with $\sum_{i\in I}|\delta_i|$ replaced by $|I|/2$. If $B\ge2^{-n}\Gamma_d M$, the rounded point attains at least $2^{-n}\Gamma_d$ normalized depth. In all cases the maximum normalized depth on $S$ is at least
$$
\max\{\Gamma_d W/M,\ \max(0,B)/M\},
\qquad W=\max_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z).
$$

d39df975a8a78959:01.statement:

$$
(s_0,\ldots,s_9)=((-3,-1),(-2,0),(-1,1),(-1,2),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(1,3),(2,3),(3,3)).
$$
Use unit counting mass on $S$ and take depth at a site to be the minimum mass of a closed ambient halfspace containing it. The largest parity class modulo $2\mathbb Z^2$ has size four, and the maximum raw depth over $S$ is exactly three, or $3/10$ after division by the original total mass. Thus the largest parity cardinality need not lower bound the best lattice depth.

dafd411c026c302c:1.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional convex body, $d\ge1$, with volume $V$ and centroid $g$. For $u\ne0$ write $F(s)=|K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}|/V$, and set $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. For every $s\in\mathbb R$,
$$
F(0)+F(s)+\frac12F(-s)\ge\gamma_d+\frac12.
$$
The right-hand side is attained. Equivalently, for every Lebesgue-measurable $A\subseteq K$ of volume $a$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge0\}|+
|A\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge t\}|+
|K\cap\{u\cdot(x-g)\ge-t\}|
\ge \gamma_d V+\frac a2.
$$

dafd411c026c302c:5.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Set $S=(\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C)$, measured by summing $d$-dimensional volumes on its three fibers. If a convex body $K$ satisfies $A\subseteq K\subseteq B\cap C$, let $a=|A|$, $V=|K|$, $E=|B|+|C|-2V$ and let $g_K$ be the volume centroid of $K$. Then the actual point $(0,g_K)$ has normalized mixed halfspace depth at least
$$
\frac{\gamma_d V+a/2}{2V+E+a}.
$$
This is at least $\gamma_d/2$ if $E\le(1/\gamma_d-1)a$. In particular, for $B=C=K$ the displayed bound holds with $E=0$, and the same conclusion holds at the actual middle centroid when $B$ and $C$ are translates of one another, taking $V=|B|$.

If $A,B,C$ are totally ordered by inclusion, some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/2$. The same holds if such an order is obtained by an affine change preserving $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d$, including a shear affine in the integer base.

db95f50a50308952:03.statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $D_j$ be convex bodies containing zero in their interiors, and let finitely many indexed fibers have the form $K_{p,j}=y_{p,j}+l_{p,j}D_j$ with $l_{p,j}>0$. Suppose positive affine denominators on those fibers have the common form
$$
A_j(p,y_{p,j}+l_{p,j}\xi)=l_{p,j}(1+c_j\cdot\xi)>0 \qquad (\xi\in D_j).
$$
Fix $p_0$ and let $a_{p,j}=l_{p,j}/l_{p_0,j}$ and $T_{p,j}(X)=y_{p,j}+a_{p,j}(X-y_{p_0,j})$. For any common $M_j>0$, define $\nu^A_{p,j}=dX/(M_jA_j(p,X))$ restricted to $K_{p,j}$. Then
$$
\nu^A_{p,j}=a_{p,j}^{d-1}(T_{p,j})_\#\nu^A_{p_0,j}.
$$
Assume $y_{p,j}\to y_p$, $l_{p,j}\to l_p>0$ and $\lambda_j\downarrow0$ (or simply $\lambda_j>0$ and $\lambda_j\to0$). Mark each measure by $r^A_{p,j}(X)=(-\lambda_j\log A_j(p,X))_+$. Along any subsequence with simultaneous finite weak limits of the marked measures on $\mathbb R^d\times[0,\infty)$, writing $a_p=l_p/l_{p_0}$ and $T_p(X)=y_p+a_p(X-y_{p_0})$, those limits satisfy
$$
\widehat\nu^A_p=a_p^{d-1}(T_p,\operatorname{id})_\#\widehat\nu^A_{p_0}.
$$
In particular the equality holds after restriction to every Borel positive-rate tail.

Along finite weak limits it survives for bounded continuous tests of that form. This yields order of each spatial tail measure by nonnegative continuous spatial tests, without a no-atom assumption. db95f50a50308952:05.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let a finite family of compact positive $d$-volume fibers $K_z$ be placed over bases $z\in P$ with summed fiber-volume measure $m$. Write $b(p)$ for the closed-halfspace depth of a base $p$ with weights $|K_z|$; in base rank zero set $b(p)=m(S)$. Let $e$ be a unit continuous covector and let an affine function $A$ have continuous gradient $ce$, $c>0$, and be nonnegative on the entire sampled family. Let a closed cap $H$ have raw mass $Q=m(H)$ and margin $(t/c)A+\ell(z)$ with $t>0$ and affine $\ell$. Suppose $A_{\rm sec}>0$ bounds the sum of maximal areas of sections of the individual $K_z$ perpendicular to $e$, using counting measure on zero-dimensional sections for $d=1$. If $b(p)\ge Q+g_0$ for all $p\in P_+$ and $g_0>0$, then
$$
\ell(z)\le -t g_0/A_{\rm sec}\qquad (z\in\operatorname{conv}P_+).
$$
Consequently the same cap misses every point over that hull with $A/c<g_0/A_{\rm sec}$, including its $A=0$ face.

dcde24475c7f190c:04.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, and place convex bodies $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ at bases $-1,0,1$. Assume $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$ and write $a=|A|$, $b=|B|$, $c=|C|$, $M=a+b+c$, with $0<a<c$, $c<a+b$, and $b<a+c$. $$
Y=\left\{\frac{b g_B+a g_A+\int x\,d\sigma}{b+2a}:0\le\sigma\le\mathbf 1_C dx,\ \sigma(C)=a\right\}.
$$
This set is nonempty, compact, convex and uniformly inside $B$, and $f$ attains its maximum there. For every maximizer $y_*$ with $D=f(y_*)<M/2$, there are $k\le d+1$ actual minimum caps $H_j=\{(z,x):u_j\cdot(x-y_*)+v_jz\ge0\}$, $\lVert u_j\rVert=1$, $\mu(H_j)=D$, and positive weights $\omega_j$ of sum one. Each cap has effective section measures $\tau_{jz}$ on its trace in $K_z$, where $(K_{-1},K_0,K_1)=(A,B,C)$. They are ordinary $H^{d-1}$ on a proper trace, zero on an empty or $H^{d-1}$-null trace, and $\theta_{jz}H^{d-1}$ on a supporting facet with a measurable $0\le\theta_{jz}\le1$. Write $S_{jz}=\int d\tau_{jz}$, $S_j=\sum_z S_{jz}$ and $X_j=\sum_z\int x\,d\tau_{jz}$. Then
$$
S_j>0,\qquad S_{j,-1}=S_{j,1},\qquad X_j=S_jy_*,\qquad
\bar u\cdot(y-y_*)\ge0\quad(y\in Y),\qquad
\bar u=\sum_j\omega_j S_j u_j .
$$
When $\bar u\ne0$, the selector density producing $y_*$ is uniquely the indicator, up to volume-null sets, of the actual lower $\bar u$-cap in $C$ of volume $a$. When $\bar u=0$, the displayed sum gives a positive section-weighted normal balance.

dcde24475c7f190c:05.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let convex bodies $K_{-1},K_0,K_1\subset\mathbb R^d$ at the indicated bases satisfy $(K_{-1}+K_1)/2\subseteq K_0$. Fix $y\in\operatorname{int}K_0$, a unit vector $u$, and $v\in\mathbb R$. In the ambient plane $P=\{u\cdot(x-y)+vz=0\}$ let $\tau$ be the sum of the ordinary central section measure and endpoint submeasures dominated by the respective $H^{d-1}$ section measures. Assume the endpoint masses are both $s\ge0$ and $\int x\,d\tau=S y$, where $S=S_0+2s$ is the total and $S_0>0$ is the central section mass. Write $\Gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for $q\ge1$ and $\Gamma_0=1$. Every closed halfspace of $P$ containing $(0,y)$ has $\tau$-mass at least $\kappa S$, where $\kappa=\Gamma_{d-1}/2$. If $d\ge2$ and $s=0$, the lower bound improves to $\Gamma_{d-1}S$. If $d=1$, the exact depth fraction is $(1+s)/(1+2s)$.

For any closed ambient through-$(0,y)$ cap $H'=\{u'\cdot(x-y)+v'z\ge0\}$ with unit $u'$, set $p=\tau(H')/S$ and $b'=\tau(\partial H')/S$. Then $\kappa\le p\le\min(1,1-\kappa+b')$. If $u'$ and $u$ are nonparallel, $b'=0$. If $u'=\epsilon u$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, and $v'=\epsilon v$, then $p=b'=1$. Otherwise in the parallel case
$$
p=\frac{S_0+s}{S_0+2s}\in[2/3,1],\qquad b'=\frac{S_0}{S_0+2s}.
$$
In a finite family of such anchored caps, the average cap indicator on any one's effective section is at least $\kappa+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j$ in normalized section mass, where $\lambda_j$ is that section's own cap weight in the probability mixture.

$$

$$

c_2=\frac49,\qquad
c_d=\frac1{1+\max\{4/3,\sqrt{2(d-1)/d}\}}\quad(d\ge3).
$$
For $3\le d\le9$ this is $3/7$. For $d\ge10$ it is strictly greater than $2/5$. In particular $c_d>(d/(d+1))^d$ for $d\ge3$.

Consequently, in any dimension $d\ge1$, if $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, each central section has full centroid $0$, and the positive-weight normals span a space of dimension at most two, then the same weighted mean is at least $(d/(d+1))^d$. e25e172f74df55a2:01.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and let the reference labeled simplex of volume $V>0$ have vertex matrix $I$ in barycentric coordinates. In each direction $i$, take finitely many fixed proper caps $\xi_i\ge a_{gi}$, $0<a_{gi}<1$, with multipliers $\ell_{gi}\ge0$. For column-sum-one $W$ near $I$, let $F_{gi}(W)$ be the actual cap volumes and $L(W)=V\det W-\sum_{gi}\ell_{gi}F_{gi}(W)$. Define
$$
X_{gi}=\frac1{1-a_{gi}},\quad \eta_{gi}=\ell_{gi}(1-a_{gi})^d,\quad
e_i=\sum_g\eta_{gi},\quad \chi_i=d\sum_g\eta_{gi}(X_{gi}-1).
$$
The Lagrangian is stationary over all physical vertex velocities if and only if $e_i=e>0$ and $\chi_i=1-de$ at every $i$. In this case $0<e<1/d$ and the distributions with weights $\eta_{gi}/e$ have common mean $\mu=1/(de)$ in $X$. The single-threshold model with threshold $a_*=1-1/\mu=1-de$ at every vertex and multiplier $e/(1-a_*)^d$ has the same first derivative as the multigroup Lagrangian. Let $Q_*(B)$ be its normalized Hessian, and let $\sigma_i^2=\operatorname{Var}_i(X)$ under the vertex $i$ weights. For each zero-column-sum $B$,
$$Q_{\mathrm{multi}}(B):=\frac{D^2 L(I)[B,B]}{V}
=Q_*(B)-d(d-1)e\sum_i\sigma_i^2 B_{ii}^2.$$
The correction is zero exactly when $B_{ii}=0$ for every $i$ with $\sigma_i^2>0$. With $b_i=B_{ii}$, $A$ the off-diagonal part of $B$, $s_i=\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}$, and $T=\operatorname{tr}B$, the effective Hessian is
$$
Q_*(B)=T^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-e\sum_i
\left([T+s_i+d(\mu-1)b_i]^2-\operatorname{tr}(B^2)-d\mu^2 b_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}(b_i-A_{ij})^2\right).
$$

e2c21ddfc5abb8ca:01.statement:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $\lambda_i\ge0$ with at least one positive. Put $K=\sum_i\lambda_i A_i$. For an enclosing $d$-simplex $S$ whose every facet supports $K$, use its outward facet normals $u_0,\ldots,u_d$ and set $P_i=\{x:u_j\cdot x\le h_{A_i}(u_j)\ \forall j\}$. Each $P_i$ contains $A_i$ and is a translated positive homothet of $S$, their weighted Minkowski sum is $S$, and
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)\le |S|-|K|.
$$
If $r_i>0$ are the scales of the parallel $P_i$ in any common simplex frame and $\alpha_i=\lambda_i r_i/\sum_j\lambda_jr_j$, this says $\sum_i\alpha_i^d(1-|A_i|/|P_i|)\le1-|K|/|S|$. If $K$ is itself a simplex then each positive-weight $A_i$ is homothetic to $K$.

If $K\subseteq Q$ for a compact convex body $Q$ and $S$ is any enclosing simplex of $Q$, define $P_i$ with the facet normals of $S$ and put $R=\sum_i\lambda_iP_i$. Then $K\subseteq R\subseteq S$ with $R$ supporting $K$ on every facet, and $\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)\le |R|-|K|\le (|S|-|Q|)+(|Q|-|K|)$. In particular this holds for every minimum-volume enclosing simplex of $Q$.

e2c21ddfc5abb8ca:03.statement:
For every $d\ge2$ there is a finite constant $A_d$ depending only on $d$ such that every compact convex body $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior and every minimum-volume enclosing simplex $S$ satisfy
$$
|S|\le(d+2)^d|Q|,\qquad
1-|Q|/|S|\le A_d\,[D(Q)-\Gamma_d],
$$
where $D$ is maximum normalized ordinary closed-halfspace depth and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. The latter bound also bounds the total variation and the supremum of closed-halfspace mass differences between the two uniform probability laws.

Let $K=\sum_i\lambda_i A_i\subseteq Q$ for full-dimensional compact convex bodies $A_i$ and finitely many coefficients $\lambda_i\ge0$, at least one positive. Write $u_j$ for the outward facet normals of $S$ and $P_i=\bigcap_j\{x:u_j\cdot x\le h_{A_i}(u_j)\}$. Then
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i^d(|P_i|-|A_i|)
 \le A_d(d+2)^d |Q|\,[D(Q)-\Gamma_d]+|Q|-|K|.
$$
If $Q=K$, express the parallel $P_i$ as translated homothets of a common simplex with positive scales $r_i$, and put $\alpha_i=\lambda_i r_i/\sum_j\lambda_jr_j$. In that case
$$
\sum_i\alpha_i^d(1-|A_i|/|P_i|)\le A_d\,[D(K)-\Gamma_d].
$$
For $d=1$ the summand defects vanish.

e4ccf81294305ade:09.statement:

$$
(w,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i(z_i,g_{z_i}),\qquad
\lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad |K_{z_i}|>0,
$$
set $a=(\sum_i\lambda_i|K_{z_i}|^{1/d})^d$ and $\delta=1-a/|K_w|\in[0,1)$. For a nonzero linear functional $u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ let $W=\max_{K_w}u-\min_{K_w}u$. Then
$$
\frac{|u(x-g_w)|}{W}
\le \min\left\{\delta,\ \frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta}{1-\delta},\ \frac{d}{d+1}\right\}.
$$
For $0\le\varepsilon<1$, let $S_\varepsilon(w)$ be the set of all $x$ admitting such a representation with $a\ge (1-\varepsilon)|K_w|$. The width of $u(S_\varepsilon(w))$ is at most $\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}W$.

For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\delta<1$, an actual body with $n=1$, three integer fibers, and a representation at $w=0$ attains
$$
\frac{u(x-g_w)}{W}=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta(1-\delta^{1/d})}{1-\delta}.
$$
Consequently the coefficient $d/(d+1)$ is optimal to first order as $\delta\downarrow0$, even for such bodies. For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, an actual body with $n=2$, five integer fibers, and $w=0$ has width $\varepsilon W$ for $u(S_\varepsilon(0))$. Thus the width coefficient one is optimal to first order as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

$$

$$
Here $|\cdot|$ is ordinary $d$-dimensional volume.

Let $d\ge3$, $m=d+1$, and $c=(1-d^{1-d})/[(d-1)^2m]$. There exists $\delta_d>0$ depending only on $d$ such that for every full-dimensional simplex $S$ with centroid $g$, and every convex body $K$ with
$$

$$
p_K(y)-\Gamma\ \ge\ \frac{\Gamma c}{4}\left(1-\frac{|K|}{|S|}\right).
$$
With $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_i$ of $S$, one may take $\lambda_i(y)=1/m+(\bar L-L_i)/(m\Gamma)$, where
$$
\eta=\min\left\{\frac1{8m},\frac{\Gamma c}{4\cdot 8m\cdot 2^{d+1}}\right\},\quad
R_i=\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap\{\lambda_i\ge1/m\}|}{|S|},\quad
L_i=\min\{\tau,R_i+8m\eta\,2^{d+1}\tau\},\quad \bar L=\frac1m\sum_i L_i.
$$

In the ordinary affine frame of a reference simplex, let $T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)$, $L=8(d+1)^3$, and

edf02845b3275e8c:02.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge 1$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ put $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $P=\{z:w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)>0\}$.

Suppose finitely many labeled mass and base moment pairs $(t_i,m_i)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ are feasible: there are $s_{iz}\ge 0$ with $\sum_i s_{iz}=w_z$ for $z\in P$ and $(t_i,m_i)=\sum_{z\in P}s_{iz}(1,z)$ for every label. Discard the labels with $t_i=0$ and index the remaining $k$ labels by $1,\ldots,k$. Fix any vectors $u_i\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto(u_i-u_j)\cdot x$ is nonconstant on each $K_z$ for $z\in P$ whenever $i\ne j$.

There are finite $\theta_i\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$ such that the affine scores $L_i(z,x)=\theta_i\cdot(1,z)+u_i\cdot x$ give closed cells
$$
D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge L_j(z,x)\}.
$$
Each $D_i$ is an ambient convex body cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces, and $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q$. The cells satisfy
$$
\bigcup_iD_i=C,\qquad
\mu(D_i\cap D_j)=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
\left(\mu(D_i),\int_{D_i} z\,d\mu\right)=(t_i,m_i).
$$
In particular they exhaust the mixed measure. The centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i$, has base $m_i/t_i$, and lies in $D_i\cap\Lambda$ if that base is integral. Suitable $u_i$ always exist.

f1516303d16df6d4:01.statement:
Let $T$ be a full-dimensional $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, of volume $V$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$, $0\le i\le d$. Set $m=d+1$, $\Gamma=(d/m)^d$. For a dimension-only $\eta_d\in(0,1/2)$, let $U_i=\{x\in T:\lambda_i(x)>1-\eta_d\}$, and let $K$ be any convex body with $T\setminus\bigcup_i U_i\subset K\subset T$. Write $t_i=|U_i\setminus K|/V$ and $t=\sum_i t_i$.

In a fixed neighborhood of the centroid, the minimum ordinary closed cap volume of $K$ at $y$, divided by $V$, is
$$
\min_i \bigl\{d^d\prod_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(y)-t_i\bigr\}.
$$
The global raw maximum is $DV$, where $D$ is the unique root near $\Gamma$ of
$$
\prod_i(D+t_i)\left(\sum_i(D+t_i)^{-1}\right)^d=d^d.
$$
The unique deepest point has barycentrics $\lambda_i^*=(D+t_i)^{-1}/\sum_j(D+t_j)^{-1}$. The normalized maximum is $D/(1-t)$.

f29d64ab4f68c3cc:04.statement:
Let $dm$ be the sum of Lebesgue volume on the finitely many sampled positive fibers of a compact canonical hull $C$, with $M=\int dm>0$. Let $L$ be continuous and strictly positive on the compact hull. For finitely many positive affine charts $W_Q$ and constants $b_Q>0$, put $G_Q=b_QW_Q$ and $U=\min_Q G_Q$. Let nonnegative source weights $\sigma_i$ at marks $Y_i$ be assigned once each to groups $Q$. Assume finite nonnegative whole-row measures $\eta_Q=L\nu_Q$ satisfy $\sum_Q\eta_Q=dm/M$ and
$$
s_Q=\eta_Q(C)=\sum_{i\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ Q}\sigma_i,\qquad
\int (W_Q/L)\,d\eta_Q=s_Q.
$$ Let $\Psi(z,x)=[E_{C_z}(x)|C_z|^{1/d}]^{1/(d+1)}$ with ordinary projective energy, and assume $U\ge\Psi$ and $\Psi(Y_i)/L(Y_i)=b_Q$ on the sources of $Q$. Set $\widehat\eta_Q=W_Q\nu_Q$ and, for $A=U,\Psi$, set
$$
\Delta_A=\sum_{i:\sigma_i>0}\sigma_i\log\!\frac{\Psi(Y_i)}{L(Y_i)}
-\int\log(A/L)\,\frac{dm}{M}.
$$
For equal-mass measures use $D(\eta\|\widehat\eta)=\int\log(d\eta/d\widehat\eta)\,d\eta$, with zero for a zero row. Then the following finite nonnegative slacks satisfy
$$
\Delta_U=\sum_Q D(\eta_Q\|\widehat\eta_Q)+\sum_Q\int\log(G_Q/U)\,d\eta_Q,\qquad
\Delta_\Psi=\Delta_U+\int\log(U/\Psi)\,\frac{dm}{M}.

Equality in $\Delta_U\ge0$ holds exactly when $W_Q=L$ and $G_Q=U$ $\eta_Q$-almost everywhere for every $Q$. Equality in $\Delta_\Psi\ge0$ also requires $U=\Psi$ $dm$-almost everywhere.

s_Q=\eta_Q(C)=\sum_{i\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ Q}\sigma_i,\qquad
\int (W_Q/L)\,d\eta_Q=s_Q.

f38040720425d155:01.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body, $d\ge1$. Set $\eta=\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{\partial K}$ and $\sigma=(G_K)_\#\eta$, where $G_K$ is the almost everywhere unique outer unit normal, extended Borelly on its null exceptional set. Let $\eta_u$ be the conditional probabilities of $\eta$ given $G_K=u$. For $\sigma$-almost every $u$,
$$
\eta_u\ \sim\ \mathcal H^{m(u)}|_{F_K(u)},\qquad
F_K(u)=\{x\in K:u\cdot x=h_K(u)\},\qquad m(u)=\dim\operatorname{aff}F_K(u).
$$
Here $\sim$ is mutual absolute continuity. In particular $\eta_u(\operatorname{rb}F_K(u))=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}\eta_u=F_K(u)$. A singleton face gives a Dirac probability and a facet normal gives normalized facet area.

For any finite Borel normal reference measure $\lambda$ with $\sigma\ll\lambda$, the unnormalized conditional of $\eta$ relative to $\lambda$ is $\bar\eta_u=(d\sigma/d\lambda)(u)\eta_u$. For $\lambda$-almost every $u$ it is either zero or has the same measure class and support as $\eta_u$ above. If $0\le\xi\le c\eta$ for a finite constant $c\ge0$, the unnormalized conditional $\xi_u$ relative to $\lambda$ satisfies $0\le \xi_u\le c\bar\eta_u$ for $\lambda$-almost every $u$.

f7c05b2c30c8cfcb:08.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine lattice, equal to the lattice points of $\operatorname{conv}P$, and let $d\ge1$. At each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, with $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$ is a convex representation. Write $C$ for the canonical convex hull of the lifted fibers, $C_z$ for its fiber over $z$, and $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf1_{K_z}\,dX)$ for the measured fibers. Put $M=\sum_z|K_z|$, let $g_z$ be the centroid of $K_z$, and define
$$
N=d+1,\qquad
\Sigma=\frac1M\sum_z\int_{K_z}(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^{\mathsf T}\,dX,\qquad
\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u},\qquad
f(z,x)=\left(\frac{E_{C_z}(x)}{M}\right)^{1/N}.
$$
Here $E_K(y)$ is the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(X-y)]^{-N}\,dX$ over parameters with positive denominator on $K$ when $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and is zero on the own boundary. At a sampled mark $(p,y)$, the raw buffered depth $b_\varepsilon(p,y)$ is the infimum of $\mu$-masses of the closed caps
$$
a\cdot(Z-p)+u\cdot(X-y)\ge-\varepsilon f(p,y)\Gamma(u),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
and of the closed pure-base caps containing $p$ (with value $M$ in base rank zero). Write $\beta_\varepsilon(K)=\max_{p\in P,\ y\in K_p}b_\varepsilon(p,y)/M$. The case $\varepsilon=0$ gives ordinary normalized closed-halfspace depth.

Fix $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and let $k(P)$ be the number of occupied parity classes in the inherited affine lattice. Suppose $\beta_0(K^{\rm ref})<b<\gamma_d/k(P)$ for a positive compatible family on $P$. Assume there is a compact set $\mathcal A$ of positive compatible families for the simultaneous Hausdorff metric with $M=1$, $K_z\subseteq R B_d$ and $\beta_0\le b$, such that every positive compatible family with $\beta_0\le b$ can be taken into $\mathcal A$ by an invertible map $(z,X)\mapsto(z,AX+Bz+c)$. Here $R>0$, $B_d$ is the Euclidean unit ball, and $L=|P||B_{d-1}|R^{d-1}$ with $|B_0|=1$.

For every $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that $\varepsilon_0LR<b-\beta_0(K^{\rm ref})$, and every $0\le\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, the infimum $\beta_\varepsilon^*=\inf_K\beta_\varepsilon(K)$ over all positive compatible families on the fixed $P$ is attained, with a representative in $\mathcal A$. Moreover
$$
\beta_0^*\le\beta_\varepsilon^*\le\beta_0^*+\varepsilon LR .
$$
For $\varepsilon_j\to0$ in that interval, any sequence of minimizers can be represented in $\mathcal A$ and has subsequences converging there to ordinary minimizers. If also $\varepsilon_0 LR<\gamma_d/(4|P|)$, every buffered maximizing mark of every family in $\mathcal A$ has a proper own shifted trace in every nonvertical direction.

f89d52b54ff6950f:2.statement:

Let $Q(\alpha,\theta)$ be the sum of the areas of the traces $x_1+\theta x_2+\alpha\cdot(z-z_0)\ge0$. For $0<\theta<1$ put $s=1-\theta$, $t_z=z-z_0$, and $k_z=\alpha\cdot t_z$. The trace area at $z$ is
$$
\begin{cases}
0& k_z\le -(2-\theta)r_z,\\
((2-\theta)r_z+k_z)^2/(2s)&-(2-\theta)r_z\le k_z\le(1-2\theta)r_z,\\
(9/2)r_z^2-((1+\theta)r_z-k_z)^2/(2\theta)&(1-2\theta)r_z\le k_z\le(1+\theta)r_z,\\
(9/2)r_z^2& k_z\ge(1+\theta)r_z .
\end{cases}
$$
Call the two proper states $I$ and $J$ in that order. If $\ell_z$ is the length of the section projected onto its $x_2$ coordinate, then $Q$ is $C^1$ in the open angular chart and
$$
\nabla_\alpha Q=\sum_z\ell_z t_z,\qquad Q_\theta=\sum_z(\ell_z^2/2-r_z\ell_z).
$$
In a strict trace cell put $v_z=(t_z,\ell_z-r_z)$. Its Hessian is $\sum_I v_zv_z^\top/s-\sum_J v_zv_z^\top/\theta$ and is positive semidefinite at an interior local minimum.

At an interior stationary point put $T_X=\sum_Xr_z\ell_z$ and $S_X=\sum_X\ell_z^2$ for $X=I,J$, with a middle-vertex transition assigned to either adjacent state, and let $M=T_I+T_J$. f991b5d72c5d9103:01.statement:
Let $\mu$ sum $d$-volumes on finitely many positive-volume compact convex fibers, $d\ge1$. Fix $Y=(p,y)$, $\delta>0$, and positive definite $\Sigma$. For $u\ne0$, put $G(u)=(u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u)^{1/2}$, and let $H(a,u)$ have margin $a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(x-y)+\delta G(u)$. Use the nonnegative side as the cap. On its old plane set $\xi=(z-p,x-y+\delta\Sigma u/G(u))$. Let $\theta_P,\theta_I,\theta_O$ be the sums of section $\mathcal H^{d-1}/\|u\|$ over proper, inside-supporting (full capture), and outside-supporting (zero capture) traces, with $\mathcal H^0$ counting. For a normal increment $D=(\alpha,v)$ the raw right derivative is
$
\int D\cdot\xi\,d\theta_P-\int(-D\cdot\xi)_+\,d\theta_I+\int(D\cdot\xi)_+\,d\theta_O.
$
Strictly saturated fibers contribute zero, and $(a,u)\cdot\xi=0$ on the old plane.

Put $m=\int \xi\,d\theta_P$ and $Z(\theta)=\{\int q\xi\,d\theta: q\text{ Borel},\ 0\le q\le1\}$. The derivative is nonnegative for every $D$ exactly when $-Z(\theta_I)\subseteq m+Z(\theta_O)$, or equivalently when every inside density $q_I$ admits an outside density $q_O$ with $m+\int q_I\xi\,d\theta_I+\int q_O\xi\,d\theta_O=0$. Equivalently for every $D$ one has
$
\left|D\cdot m+\tfrac12\int D\cdot\xi\,d(\theta_I+\theta_O)\right|
\le \tfrac12\left(\int|D\cdot\xi|\,d\theta_O-\int|D\cdot\xi|\,d\theta_I\right).
$
If the own trace is proper, this condition with $\theta_O=0$ implies $\theta_I=0$ and that the coarea-weighted proper-section centroid is $(p,y-\delta\Sigma u/G(u))$. In particular a positive-area inside supporting trace at a normal local minimum requires a positive-area outside supporting trace.

fc860651e80d6fd0:01.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and $P\subset E$ a nonempty finite set. For $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, where $d\ge1$, and write $w_z=|K_z|_d>0$ and $g_z$ for its volume centroid. Let $M=\sum_{z\in P}w_z$ and $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Give the graph $T=\{(z,g_z):z\in P\}$ the atomic weights $w_z$, and write $w(F)=\sum_{(z,g_z)\in T\cap F}w_z$. The measured family has raw cap mass $\mu(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|\{x\in K_z:(z,x)\in H\}|_d$.

Fix $0<\alpha\le M$ and $y=(p,g_p)\in T$ such that every closed ambient halfspace containing $y$ has atomic weight at least $\alpha$. Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$, allowing the whole hull. Then the raw halfspace depth $h_\mu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\mu(H)$ is at least $\gamma_d\alpha$. Equality implies $w(F)=\alpha$ and the existence of a single unit $u\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfying
$$
|K_z\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g_z)\ge0\}|_d=\gamma_d w_z
\qquad\text{for every }(z,g_z)\in F\cap T.
$$
In particular, $w(F)>\alpha$ implies $h_\mu(y)>\gamma_d\alpha$.

If $g_z=G(z)$ for a single affine map $G:E\to\mathbb R^d$, these two conditions also imply equality and a through-$y$ closed halfspace attains it. \quad X=\prod_j s_j,\quad \rho=\prod_j(1-x_j),\quad E=\rho^{-1}-1.

fe4ccc381e7e406a:01.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and let $r$ be a continuous nonnegative concave function on $[a,b]$ with $a<0<b$ and $r(0)>0$. Write $R=\max r$ and $\{z:r(z)\ge v\}=[-B(v),A(v)]$ for $v\in[0,R]$. Both arms are continuous, concave and nonincreasing, with $A(0),B(0)>0$ and $A+B\ge0$. Equip $\{(x,z):a\le z\le b,\ |x|\le r(z)\}$ with the planar density $f(x,z)=r(z)^{m-1}/2$. Define $V$ as its total mass, $P(s)$ as the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and $C(s),M(s)$ as the line integrals of $f,zf$ on $z+sx=0$ with line measure divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Then
$$
V=m\int_0^R v^{m-1}(A+B)\,dv .
$$
For $s>0$ define the even function
$$
j_s(t,v)=
\begin{cases}
m v^{m-1}|t|/2,& |t|\ge sv,\\
s(m+1)v^m/4+(m-1)v^{m-2}t^2/(4s),& |t|\le sv.
\end{cases}
$$
For $v>0$ off the branch boundaries put $c_s=\partial_t j_s$ and $k_s=-s\partial_s j_s$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
P(s)&=V/2+\int_0^R[j_s(A(v),v)-j_s(B(v),v)]\,dv,\\
C(s)&=\int_0^R[c_s(A(v),v)+c_s(B(v),v)]\,dv,\\
M(s)&=\int_0^R[k_s(A(v),v)-k_s(B(v),v)]\,dv.
\end{aligned}
$$
At $s=0$ one has $P(0)=V/2+(m/2)\int_0^R v^{m-1}(|A|-|B|)\,dv$, $C(0)=r(0)^m$, and $M(0)=0$. Terms with coefficient $m-1$ are omitted for $m=1$.

fee4b98d94ecbcf2:01.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interiors and $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Put $S=(\lbrace-1\rbrace\times A)\cup(\lbrace0\rbrace\times K)\cup(\lbrace1\rbrace\times B)$, measured by $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mu$ on $S$. Fix $y\in K$ and let $Q$ be the infimum of $\mu(S\cap H)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(0,y)$.

Suppose $H_\alpha=\lbrace(z,x):u\cdot(x-y)+\alpha z\ge0\rbrace$, with $u\ne0$, attains $Q$. Let $U,q,V$ be the respective $d$-volumes of its traces on $A,K,B$. Write $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$ and $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. Suppose $q\ge\Gamma|K|$ and $U^{1/d}+V^{1/d}\ge2(1-\eta)q^{1/d}$ for some $0\le\eta\le1$. Set $D=2(1-\eta)^d$ and $\rho=(D\Gamma)^{1/d}$. Then the normalized depth at $(0,y)$ satisfies

$$
\frac{Q}{M}\ge\frac{(1+D)\Gamma}{1+\rho^d+(2-\rho)^d}.
$$

If $\eta\le1/[2(d+1)]$, then $Q/M>8\Gamma/15>\Gamma/2$.

fee4b98d94ecbcf2:02.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex bodies with nonempty interiors and $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Put $S=(\lbrace-1\rbrace\times A)\cup(\lbrace0\rbrace\times K)\cup(\lbrace1\rbrace\times B)$, measured by $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mu$ on $S$. Fix $y\in K$ and let $Q$ be the infimum of $\mu(S\cap H)$ over all closed ambient halfspaces $H$ containing $(0,y)$. Write $M=|A|+|K|+|B|$ and $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$. Suppose finitely many closed ambient halfspaces $H_i=\lbrace(z,x):u_i\cdot(x-y)+\alpha_i z\ge0\rbrace$, with $u_i\ne0$, attain $Q$ and their middle traces cover $K$. For each $i$ let $U_i,q_i,V_i$ be the respective captured volumes in $A,K,B$. Suppose that for the same $\eta\in[0,1]$, every $i$ satisfies $U_i^{1/d}+V_i^{1/d}\ge2(1-\eta)q_i^{1/d}$. Set $D=2(1-\eta)^d$ and $\rho=(D\Gamma)^{1/d}$. Then

$$
\frac{Q}{M}\ge\frac{(1+D)\Gamma}{1+\rho^d+(2-\rho)^d},
\qquad
\frac{Q}{M}>\frac{8}{15}\Gamma>\frac{\Gamma}{2}
\quad\text{if }\eta\le\frac1{2(d+1)}.
$$

At $\eta=0$ the first lower bound is

$$
\frac{3\Gamma}{1+2\Gamma+(2-(2\Gamma)^{1/d})^d}.
$$

This is $1/2$ for $d=1$ and $12/(61-24\sqrt2)$ for $d=2$. For $d\ge2$ it strictly exceeds $3\Gamma/[1+\Gamma+((d+2)/(d+1))^d]$, which in turn is strictly greater than $3\Gamma/5>\Gamma/2$.

fee4b98d94ecbcf2:03.statement:

In particular, $Q\le3q$.

ff5285005955b0c7:01.statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$ be integers with $m=n+d\ge1$, and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with positive mixed $d$-volume $M$, with counting measure when $d=0$. Choose $R\ge1$ with $C\subset R B_m$ and a finite $1/k$-net $U_k$ of the unit sphere containing the signed coordinate vectors. With $T_k=k(R^2+1)+R$ and $h_C(u)=\max_{x\in C}u\cdot x$, put
$$
C_k=\bigcap_{u\in U_k}B(-T_k u,T_k+h_C(u)+1/k),
$$
where the balls are closed. These bodies are strictly convex, contain $C$ in their interiors, and satisfy
$$
d_H(C_k,C)\le\frac{1+\sqrt m(R+1)+R}{k}.
$$
Eventually the nonempty integer bases are exactly those of $C$. Each original nonempty integer fiber is full-dimensional in $C_k$ and converges in Hausdorff distance to its original fiber.

Let $\mu_k,\mu$ be the ambient measures obtained by summing the $d$-volumes of their respective fibers, with totals $M_k,M$. Then
$$
\sup_{A\ \mathrm{Borel}}|\mu_k(A)-\mu(A)|=\delta_k=M_k-M\longrightarrow0.
$$
If $A_\nu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\nu(H)$ for closed ambient halfspaces, then
$$
\sup_y\left|\frac{A_{\mu_k}(y)}{M_k}-\frac{A_\mu(y)}{M}\right|\le\frac{\delta_k}{M_k}.
$$
Every subsequential limit of mixed points $y_k\in C_k$ of normalized depth at least $c$ is an original mixed point of normalized depth at least $c$. For $d\ge2$, all positive fibers of the approximants have zero $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ measure on each supporting hyperplane. For $d=1$, a supporting endpoint of a positive interval has $\mathcal H^0$ measure one. For $d=0$, the counting measures eventually coincide.
